News.title: Moment fleeing crowds scream in fear as fireworks are lobbed in city centre in Halloween chaos as seven arrested
News.content:
Next

THIS is the moment scattered crowds scream in fear over fireworks being thrown around a city centre as police arrest seven.

A night of Halloween chaos descended over the streets of Birmingham as yobs turned the city into a firework warzone.



One video shows masked thugs on bikes shooting the light displays at a moving police car.

Explosions can then be heard ringing out across Corporation Street as people duck for cover.



Another video shows a bus being tormented with fireworks as it’s stuck at a red light.

Once the bus pulls away, the thugs turn to target other moving cars.



More shocking footage shows another scene unfolding as fireworks are thrown directly into a crowd.

At least five officers can be seen in one clip chasing a group of fleeing thugs as they attempt to bring the chaos to an end.

More fireworks were launched at bystanders with yobs dressed in black seen setting off the colourful explosives.

Members of the public ran for cover and recorded on their phones as sparks rained down on them.

Rockets could be seen flying up and down a busy street as fireworks were launched back and forth between crowds of revellers.



Crowds of people could be seen running away and screaming in terror after the rockets were launched along New Street.

One onlooker said: “It was like a warzone. People were just letting off fireworks at each other like it was just a bit of harmless fun.

“I didn’t see anyone getting hurt but I would be amazed if nobody was injured during that as fireworks were exploding next to people in the street. It was mayhem.”



Other residents expressed their shock and dismay on social media with one person writing: “Absolute morons, somebody could have been killed.”

Another added: “That is absolutely crazy, fair play to that one woman on her phone walking by as if nothing is happening.

“I would have been running for my life.”

Police were called to the scene after the city centre was turned into a “war zone” by the thugs.



West Midlands Police said seven people – aged between 15 and 26 – had been arrested for a variety of offences.

Some were taken into custody on suspicion of assault, possession of fireworks and possession of an offensive weapon.

All seven remain in police custody at this time, the arrests were made in and around Stephenson St and Corporation St.

A police spokesperson said in a statement yesterday: “We responded to reports of fireworks being set off in a dangerous manner.

“In total we arrested seven people (aged between 15 and 26) for a number of offences including assault, possession of fireworks and possession of an offensive weapon.



“They all remain in custody for questioning.

“The arrests were made in and around Stephenson St and Corporation St.”

Anyone who witnessed antisocial behaviour last night in the city can contact West Midlands Police, the force said.

News.title: Fears serial killer babysitter smothered SIXTH victim as ex-friend ‘reveals chilling confession’ decades on
News.content:
Next

A MONSTER babysitter convicted of smothering three children to death may have claimed another victim, it is feared.

Cold case cops in Australia have reopened a murder probe into Helen Patricia Moore after a documentary shed fresh light on her sick reign of terror – and revealed a chilling “confession”.



The twisted serial killer was jailed for life nearly 50 years ago after suffocating three children and attempting to murder two others – but walked free from prison after serving just 13 years behind bars.

Now, detectives are examining claims that her twisted killing spree actually began with the death of her baby stepbrother, Andrew.



In March 1979, a teenage Moore was looking after her siblings at their home in Sydney when her brother was asleep in his cot.

Her brother Craig Moorley recalled the horror when Moore suddenly began shrieking, telling A Current Affair: “We raced into the bedroom, she ran out to the neighbour’s house.”

He added: “I picked him up and put him on Helen’s bed and tried to give him mouth-to-mouth. I was only 12 at the time, I didn’t know what I was doing. I couldn’t bring him back.”

Charges over Andrew’s death were initially dropped due to a lack of evidence, but one of Moore’s former school friends has now come forward with a chilling confession.

Cat Delaney claimed: “She just looked at me straight in the face and just told me matter-of-factly, ‘I killed my little brother’.”

Moore continued babysitting for unsuspecting parents and picked her next target, baby cousin Susan Louise.



Heartbroken mum Pat recalled: “We were panicking because there was nothing wrong with her when we left.

“She was perfectly healthy and asleep. We truly believed Helen had killed her.”

Cops initially blamed Susan’s death on choking on her own vomit, leaving Moore to roam free and strike again.



She went on to target two toddler boys on separate babysitting jobs by attempting to smother them.

Both miraculously survived – but one of the young victims was left with permanent, life-changing physical disabilities.

Moore then targeted baby Rachel Hay, carrying out a horrifying attack witnessed by an older sibling.

Rachel’s older brother Darren said: “I remember the screams, the screams were just horrific.

“I remember Helen saying she was going to put Rachel to bed, and my older sister Sonya was in the doorway.



“[Sonya saw] Helen do something [to Rachel] and the cold-hearted, evil person she was, [she] turned around and said to my sister…‘If you say anything, your brother and sister will be next.’”

Just one month later, the sick babysitter murdered her seven-year-old brother Peter.

Moore was eventually convicted of murdering Susan, Rachel and Peter, as well as attempting to kill the two young boys.

Brother Craig has spearheaded the fight to reopen the investigation into baby Andrew, saying: “I’m hoping she’s charged with additional murder. I believe this can protect the kids.”

Former New South Wales (NSW) detective Peter Moroney backed the new probe, adding: “Without being critical of the original police at the time, they may have got it wrong.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

“There’s got to be something in it for them, in a sense, they know it’s solvable and they are going to have that last-ditch effort at doing it.

“I would like to see at least the matter put before the courts if there is sufficient evidence.”

News.title: Two arrested for attempted murder after five teens stabbed at Halloween house party
News.content:
HALLOWEEN ARRESTS Two arrested for attempted murder after five teens stabbed at Halloween house party







Next

TWO teenagers have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after five boys were stabbed at a Halloween party.

A 17-year-old boy is fighting for his life after the horror attack, which left four other teenagers seriously injured.



The victims, three aged 16 and two aged 17, were rushed to hospital following the bloodshed in Chandler’s Ford in Hampshire.

Cops were called to a property just after 10.30pm on Saturday after reports that the boys had been stabbed.



Police say a group of uninvited males climbed over a garden fence to gatecrash the party.

Upon entering they reportedly unleashing their attack on five guests in the garden and surrounding roads.



Now the force has confirmed that a 17-year-old and 16-year-old boy have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder.

They both remain in police custody at this time.

Two boys remain in hospital with serious injuries, including the 17-year-old whose condition is life-threatening.

The other three victims have since been discharged.



The attack has sparked shock among the local community, with two schools and colleges confirming that some of those injured were former or current pupils.

Barton Peveril Sixth Form College, near Chandler’s Ford, contacted parents today to reassure them that support was available following the stabbing.

In an email, the college said: “We are doing all we can to support our Barton Peveril Community at this time.

“Students can access support through their student progress advisors and the health and wellbeing team.

“Security is always present at both entrances of the college to ensure that only Barton Peveril College students have access to the campus.”



It added: “Our thoughts are with the victims and their families.”

Thornden School in Chandler’s Ford also confirmed some of those injured were former pupils.

Headteacher Caroline Lowing said: “We understand that some of our former students have sustained injuries and are receiving treatment and support.

“This news has been deeply upsetting for our school community.

“We are working to support any current students and families who may be affected and have appropriate wellbeing support available within school.”



The local Neighbourhood Policing Team will also visit schools and colleges over the coming week to offer reassurance and support to those affected.

Police scenes remain in place around the address in Park Road as detectives continue their investigation.

Officers are speaking to witnesses and examining CCTV and other footage from the area.

Senior investigating officer DCI Elizabeth Pirie said: “Whilst the two arrests are a significant development in our investigation, which has moved at pace since the incident was first reported to us, we still urge our communities to contact us with any information, no matter how small it may seem.

“I understand the effect that such an incident will have had on the local community, and I do not underestimate the disruption that our scenes have caused to those living in the area.



“We are working hard to reduce the impact.

“We are extremely grateful for the understanding of our communities whilst we continue working to establish the full circumstances surrounding this incident.”

She urged anyone who attended the party or had footage from the area to come forward.

She added: “If you were at the party and have not spoken with officers yet, or you have any CCTV, mobile phone, dash cam or doorbell camera footage covering Park Road and the surrounding area, then please get in touch.”

Eastleigh MP Liz Jarvis said: “My thoughts are with the victims and their families and the local community at this time and my thanks goes to the emergency services for their swift response.



“I know many people will be shocked and upset by what has happened.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“This area is generally very safe and welcoming.

“I hope that residents feel reassured that the police are doing all that they can and I would urge people not to speculate or share information from unverified sources.”

News.title: Man in his 50s dies after punch bag machine is pushed over and lands on him during fight
News.content:
TRAGIC END Man in his 50s dies after punch bag machine is pushed over and lands on him during fight







Next

A MAN has died after a punch bag machine is believed to have been pushed over and landed on him during a fight.

Cops were called to Berkley Street in Toxteth, Liverpool, shortly before 7pm on Thursday, following reports of a disturbance.

The victim, in his 50s, suffered a serious head injury and was rushed to hospital, Merseyside Police said.



Iliasse Alhag, 22, of Toxteth, a Moroccan national according to police, has been charged with affray, assault and wounding without intent and was due to appear at Liverpool Adult Remand Court earlier.



The Crown Prosecution Service was reviewing the charges in light of the death.

Det Ch Insp Alyson Keenan said: “We are continuing our enquiries into this incident and urge anyone who was in the area of Berkley Street at the time, or who has information which could assist the investigation, to please get in touch.”

Anyone with information should contact Merseyside Police social media desk via X or Facebook @MerPolCC using reference 26000888085.

Alternatively, contact the independent charity Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111, or via their website.

News.title: Tech tycoon, wife & two toddler kids among 9 people killed in horrifying Learjet crash
News.content:
Next

A TEXAS tech tycoon and his wife were among the nine people killed in a horror private jet crash on Sunday.

Adam Robinson, 44, his wife, Helen, their two children and two close friends were reportedly on the Learjet 60 when it exploded in Palm Beach County, Florida.



The family also was traveling with their nanny.

“It’s quite a blow,” said one relative in Texas. “We had a daughter, her husband and two grandchildren on the plane.”



A family member told TMZ that Jeff Gregory, 55, was piloting with co-pilot Natalia Gadelha Filgueiras, 20.

The National Transportation Safety Board held a news conference Monday, confirming that ice began forming on the plane amid moderate turbulence.

The flight crew requested permission to climb from 35,000 feet to 37,000 feet shortly before declaring an emergency.

The two pilots and seven passengers were killed in the crash.

Co-pilot Filgueiras’s mother, Camila, confirmed to the New York Post that her daughter was aboard the twin-engine aircraft, which had departed Austin, Texas, and was headed to the Bahamas.

The aircraft came crashing down in a residential area, bursting into a massive fireball on impact. Shocking dashcam footage captured the moment the jet slammed into the ground, leaving behind a large crater and widespread destruction.



Florida Governor Ron DeSantis described the horrifying scene, saying the aircraft looked like “a missile going down.”

Even more disturbing was the audio recorded during the plane’s final moments, which captured the cockpit crew desperately attempting to regain control of the aircraft.

During the emergency transmission, Filgueiras could be heard reporting the plane’s terrifying rate of descent.

“We are in an overspeed condition, descending 20,000 feet per minute,” she said.

She later issued repeated warnings as the aircraft continued its rapid descent.



“We’re descending 8,000 — mayday, mayday — we’re descending 10,000 feet per minute.”

A male pilot, whose identity has not been released, could also be heard reciting the Lord’s Prayer as the situation deteriorated.

At one point, Filgueiras desperately warned, “We’re going to crash into the ground.”



Her final words included an expletive as the crew appeared to realize there was no time left. The recording then fell silent.

The U.S. Sun has decided not publish the final seconds of the distress call.

Filgueiras’ death is particularly heartbreaking given how young she was when she first achieved her dream of becoming a pilot.



A Palm Beach County native, she earned her private pilot’s license in October 2023 while attending West Boca Raton High School. She was just 17 years old at the time.

Her achievement was highlighted in a report by CBS affiliate WPEC, where she proudly explained that she had learned to fly before obtaining her driver’s license.

“I definitely do brag because people say, ‘Oh, you can’t drive,’ and I’m like, ‘Yeah, but I can fly,'” she said during the interview.

She added that she enjoyed doing something different from her classmates and was proud of accomplishing something many people her age had never considered.

Her aviation journey began in 2020, when she enrolled in Ground School during her sophomore year.



Her interest in flying was also encouraged by her father, who began flying recreationally in 2018 and helped introduce her to aviation.

By the time she earned her license, Filgueiras had accumulated 88 hours of flight experience and successfully completed the required aviation knowledge examination.

Her training was funded through the Palm Beach County School District’s Aviation Academy.

The tragedy also sparked false speculation online that legendary musician Lenny Kravitz had been among those onboard. His representative quickly dismissed the claims, telling BocaNewsNow that the reports were “untrue and incorrect.”

The National Transportation Safety Board is investigating the circumstances surrounding the disaster.



Meanwhile, former pilot Martin Varsavsky has suggested that severe weather may have played a role in the aircraft’s sudden loss of control.

One possibility he raised was a dangerous aerodynamic phenomenon known as coffin corner.

This occurs at high altitudes when an aircraft’s minimum safe flying speed approaches its maximum operating speed, leaving pilots with an extremely narrow margin for maintaining control.

If an aircraft flies too slowly, it risks stalling. If it exceeds its safe speed, it can also become dangerously difficult to control.

Varsavsky speculated that the Learjet may have attempted to climb above two storm systems before encountering dangerous atmospheric conditions.



Comparing the possibility to previous aviation disasters, including Air France Flight 447 in 2009, he argued that pilots must maintain a substantial distance from powerful storm systems rather than attempting to fly through them.

However, investigators have not established weather, pilot error or coffin corner as the cause of the Florida crash.

The NTSB investigation will determine what happened during the aircraft’s final moments and why a flight carrying nine people ended in such a devastating loss of life.

Night-shift truck driver Armando Perez was in bed when a loud, supersonic boom suddenly startled him awake.

Perez said the powerful blast rattled him, comparing the sensation to standing next to an enormous subwoofer.



“I thought, ‘is this freaking Iran?'” Perez told local media.

News.title: Gunman accidentally shot hitman pal on their way to attack leaving him to take a taxi to hospital
News.content:
FIREARM FAIL Gunman accidentally shot hitman pal on their way to attack leaving him to take a taxi to hospital







Next

A GUNMAN accidentally shot his hitman pal as they were going to a planned shooting, leaving him to take a taxi to hospital.

Adam Liaqat, 19, and Asad Khan, 22, were parked up when their gun went off in St Paul’s Road, Smethwick, shortly before 4.30am on November 23 last year.



Liaqat, who was driving, fired the gun in error, leaving his accomplice with serious leg injuries, the West Midlands Police said.

The Mitsubishi Outlander the pair were in had been stolen from Rowley Regis the previous evening.



Both men have now been convicted of possession of a firearm with intent to endanger life.

Liaqat has been jailed for 15 years while Khan has been banged up for 13 years.

A third man, Yakuba Sawaneh, has been jailed for three-and-a-half years.

Khan was left to get a taxi to hospital where he initially claimed to be unclear about what had happened

During an investigation, cops discovered a message between Khan and someone else which indicated he and Liaqat were on their way to conduct a shooting “before their mishap”.

Police arrested Liaqat on December 2 after a pursuit with a Honda Accord, which he was driving despite only being a provisional licence holder.



His passenger was Sawaneh and items including Class A drugs and a burner phone were thrown from the windows as the car was pursued and then stopped in Oldbury.

Liaqat, from Sandwell, was jailed at Wolverhampton Crown Court on Monday, had also been found guilty of possession of Class A drugs with intent to supply.

Khan, also from West Bromwich, had already been sentenced for possessing a firearm with intent to endanger life/enable another to do so and possession of a Class A drug.

Sawaneh, 19, from Birmingham, was found guilty of possession of Class A drugs with intent to supply.

He was jailed in September for 42 months.

News.title: At least 24 dead after barbaric Putin bombs Ukrainian school in ‘utterly horrific’ strikes leaving huge crater
News.content:
Next

VLADIMIR Putin has unleashed a “horrific” attack on a school being used as an aid centre – killing at least 24 civilians.

Russian forces then launched a second twisted attack on a nearby shelter, Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky said, branding the barbaric attack a “double-tap” strike.



At least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha, southeastern Zaporihzhia, according to regional official Mykhailo Semikin.

Zelensky said: “The strikes targeted a school used for humanitarian purposes – people were receiving humanitarian aid there.



“After the first aerial bomb strike, there was a double-tap strike with nine more bombs, specifically targeting the shelter where people were taking cover.”

A double-tap strike involves blasting the same location at least twice, sometimes hours later, which can mean that emergency services responding to the initial bombardment are hit.

As well as the 24 people who were killed, five were injured and 27 people remain missing.

The Ukrainian president posted a video revealing the devastating aftermath of the attack.



A huge crater can be seen still smouldering from the strikes.

Rescue teams continue to scour the scene for survivors, as regional official Semikin said “people were still under the rubble”.



Zelensky raged: “The Russians could not have been unaware that every week residents who have remained in Komyshuvakha were receiving assistance aid right there.

“This is yet further proof that Russia does not want any kind of de-escalation, any real justice.

“After the humanitarian operation in Oleshky, there was a moment when the next steps could have shown that progress toward peace was possible.



“With these killings, Russia is sending an entirely opposite signal: Russia is counting on more killings.

“There must be a response to this – a response from the world. A strong and tough response.”

Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after a local ceasefire – the war’s longest truce to date – expired.

Elsewhere in Ukraine, at least 17 people were injured by Russian drone strikes, authorities said.

The Russian military has yet to comment on the blasts.



It comes after terrifying hoax emergency alerts warning of nuclear and chemical attacks were sent to millions of civilians across Russia and Ukraine.

Hackers reportedly issued several bogus announcements through official warning apps and text messaging services to spread panic among the two nations.

Putin’s emergency warning system was feared to have been infiltrated by a team of hackers overnight as Russians were sent messages about incoming nuclear warheads.

Russians were ordered to stockpile food for three weeks and hide in their cellars – or face being “blown to bits” by bombs at around 2.45am.

The panic-inducing alerts appeared on official channels of Russia’s Emergency Situations Ministry [EMERCOM] in Moscow, St Petersburg and multiple other regions.



Kyiv doesn’t possess any nuclear weapons but Ukrainian hackers are suspected of being behind the cyber attack.

Russia’s Emergency Situations Ministry publicly acknowledged the chaos calling it a “massive cyber-attack”.

It claimed the country’s sirens, loudspeakers, television and radio warning systems hadn’t been compromised despite the alert system’s humiliation.

The nuclear scare came just hours after a similar cyberattack breached Ukraine’s official Air Alert system.

Scared Ukrainians were warned of a radiation hazard followed by a serious incoming nuclear and chemical threat.



Four back-to-back messages read: “Radiation threat. Radiation threat declared in Kyiv.

“Don’t worry, an Oreshnik is overhead! A nuclear alert has been activated across Ukraine.

“Chemical threat. There is a threat of a chemical attack on Kyiv. Don’t go outside.

“Street fighting threat. Street fighting is taking place in Kyiv. Don’t go outside.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The Ukrainian authorities immediately confirmed their emergency alert service had been targeted by hackers.



The system is crucial for Ukraine as it acts as the main line of defence for civilians against Putin’s drone and missile strikes.

News.title: Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers
News.content:
ILR, also known as settlement, gives a person the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like and apply for benefits if they are eligible. They can also use it to apply for British citizenship.

Last November, Mahmood announced plans to delay settlements in response to concerns over the number of people approaching eligibility, in the wake of record post-Brexit net migration figures under the previous Conservative government.

The Home Office has said its figures show net migration - the difference between those entering and leaving the country - added 2.6m people to the UK population between 2021 and 2024.

The department estimates that between 2026 and 2030 between 1.3m and 2.2m people will settle in the UK, adding its central estimate has increased to 1.9m.

The home secretary faced criticism for proposing to apply the changes to migrant workers already in the UK, with Housing Secretary Angela Rayner previously saying this would "change the goalposts".

Several Labour MPs also described the retrospective approach as "un-British" and warned it could worsen the UK's skills shortage, particularly in the care sector.

Making a statement to the House of Commons, Mahmood said settlement "should not be automatic, it should be earned".

She said those who do not come under the various exceptions will be on a 10-year path to settlement status. This will still affect many people who came to the UK expecting to qualify after five years.

One of those affected is Ashfak Juned, a Bangladeshi chef working in Birmingham, who told BBC News he was "crying" when he heard the new rules, which will double his wait for settled status, pushing it from 2028 to 2033.

The changes will move those earning less than Â£50,000 a year onto a 10-year path to settlement status, unless they are exempt, so he will have to wait five more years than expected before he can qualify for permanent settlement.

Mahmood also told MPs the government would provide a five-year path to settlement for care workers who "answered our call when we needed them" following the Covid-19 pandemic.

Mahmood said: "Those who earn Â£25,000 a year working in the social care sector, which was the condition of their visa, will therefore be able to settle on their existing five-year path."

She added those care workers who did not meet the conditions of their visa will be offered "a second chance to make the contribution that they came to this country to make". They can apply for another five-year visa and seek settlement after this.

MPs were also told:

higher earners on salaries of more than Â£50,000 and those who have contributed in healthcare and education, such as doctors and teachers, will be able to qualify for settlement after five years

the highest rate taxpayers earning more than Â£125,000 will be able to apply after three years

refugees who arrived in the UK after crossing the Channel by small boat or another illegal route will have to wait 20 years if they work or study, and 30 years if they do not.

Mahmood said: "Our changes ensure those who are net contributors are encouraged to come to this country and stay here."

She added: "As a result, the Department for Work and Pensions estimates that our reforms will reduce the benefits bill by billions of pounds."

The original version of the plans announced by Mahmood last year would have delayed 799,000 people from gaining permanent residency.

Under the updated plans announced on Monday, that number will now drop to 517,000.

The Refugee Council's Imran Hussain condemned the plans for those who have travelled to the UK illegally or by small boat and do not work or study to wait 30 years for indefinite leave to remain as "unfair and unworkable".

He said: "These plans condemn refugees to decades of deep insecurity, unable to lay down roots in Britain and contribute their potential, and there is no evidence to suggest that harming refugee integration will act as a disincentive to refugees fleeing the Taliban or brutal conflicts like Sudan.

"It also creates another bureaucratic nightmare for a Home Office that already is struggling with poor quality initial decisions on asylum cases which is leading to avoidable costs and delays in the appeals system.

"The fairest reforms would be making fast and good quality asylum decisions, with those refugees granted protection being helped to rebuild their lives and to contribute, and those with no right to remain helped to leave with dignity."

News.title: 'All this food is now useless': Piles of rubbish after shop freezers hit by cyber-attack
News.content:
In dozens of supermarkets across several European countries, a huge amount of food has been dumped after refrigerators and freezers were targeted in a cyber-attack.

Belgium and Luxemburg saw some of the worst damage, with 40 Delhaize supermarkets affected, and incidents also took place in stores across Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.

In a branch of supermarket Delhaize in Hoeilaart, just outside the Belgian capital Brussels, the BBC's Europe correspondent Nick Beake found frozen pizzas and ice cream among a mountain of food having to be scrapped. News.title: Copilot in deadly Florida jet crash identified in reports as 20-year-old
News.content:
A 20-year-old copilot was among nine people killed when a small jet crashed and exploded in Florida on Sunday, according to US media.

Nathalia Filgueiras, who earned her pilot's licence when she was 17, is reported to have been one of two crew members aboard the Learjet 60 from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas when it crashed near West Palm Beach.

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) said it would investigate to what extent ice and turbulence may have contributed to the crash, and whether human error played a role.

One man on the ground sustained a leg injury when the aircraft nosedived on to a street near Cresthaven, nine miles (14 km) from President Donald Trump's Mar-a-Lago resort.

Images from the scene show a large fiery crater in the middle of a residential suburban street.

The debris was scattered across sports fields, businesses and homes in the area, officials told a news conference on Monday, possible evidence that the plane broke up before it hit the ground.

News.title: MP Carla Lockhart quits DUP in Drumcree row
News.content:
Carla Lockhart has quit the Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) in a row over its response to the Drumcree parading dispute.

The MP for Upper Bann had been calling for the party to withdraw Stormont's deputy first minister to force First Minister Michelle O'Neill from their joint office.

Lockhart said she was leaving the DUP on a "point of principle" and would continue in the House of Commons as an independent unionist.

The fall-out comes after unionist anger over Sinn FÃ©in's involvement in protests on Garvaghy Road, which blocked a contentious Orange Order parade from passing along the mainly nationalist street in Portadown, County Armagh.

O'Neill and several other senior Sinn FÃ©in figures have been interviewed by police investigating the demonstrations, with unionists accusing the party of acting unlawfully.

Last week the DUP, which shares power with Sinn FÃ©in in Northern Ireland's devolved government, announced it would block official engagements involving O'Neill in response to the fall-out.

The Sinn FÃ©in vice-president has defended her involvement in the protests, saying it was the "right thing to do".

DUP leader Gavin Robinson stopped short of Lockhart's call to force O'Neill from office.

In an open letter to colleagues last week, Lockhart said it was the "only one credible option" and any kind of "graduated response" would be "insulting to those who have trusted us".

In a statement posted on her Facebook page on Monday, the MP said: "My first responsibility remains to the people of Upper Bann.

"You placed your trust in me, and I will continue to work every bit as hard for you, your family and our community."

News.title: Two boys arrested after Halloween party stabbings
News.content:
Two teenage boys have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder after five teenagers were stabbed at a Halloween party.

Officers said they were called shortly after 22:30 GMT on Saturday to Park Road in Chandler's Ford, Hampshire, where an "unknown group" had gained entry to the event.

Police said two boys remain in hospital having suffered serious injuries, with one 17-year-old victim in a life-threatening condition. The others have been discharged from hospital.

A 17-year-old and 16-year-old, both from Southampton, have been arrested on suspicion of attempted murder and remain in police custody.

Two witnesses told the BBC a fight started after a group came in over a garden fence, although they said the motive for the stabbings was unclear.

One of the teenagers said: "I was [standing] in the hallway near the exit and I saw someone I know pull up their shirt and say 'I've been stabbed'.

"And then I later saw him lying outside the front of the house with someone compressing his wound."

Police cordoned off parts of Park Road and the adjoining Valley Road.

Det Ch Insp Elizabeth Pirie said: "Whilst the two arrests are a significant development in our investigation, which has moved at pace since the incident was first reported to us, we still urge our communities to contact us with any information, no matter how small it may seem."

She added: "If you were at the party and have not spoken with officers yet, or you have any CCTV, mobile phone, dash cam or doorbell camera footage covering Park Road and the surrounding area, then please get in touch."

News.title: Prosecutors hint at retrial for Lindsay Clancy on murder charges
News.content:
Warning: This story contains distressing details and discussion of attempted suicide

Massachusetts prosecutors have given their clearest indication yet that they plan to retry Lindsay Clancy for the murder of her three children in 2023.

At a hearing on Monday, Judge William Sullivan scheduled a 16 November hearing where he plans to rule on a handful of motions that could determine how a retrial would proceed, including a request to dismiss the first-degree murder charges.

Clancy faced a weekslong trial on those charges over the summer. It fell apart in early September after a 12-person jury failed to reach a verdict.

If there is a retrial, Judge Sullivan said, it could happen as soon as March 2027.

The prosecution did not say on Monday whether Clancy would face the same charges or amended charges in the event of a retrial.

When the parties meet again later this month, they will hear the judge's rulings on the motions argued in court on Monday, and potentially will discuss dates for a retrial, Judge Sullivan said.

Kevin Reddington, Clancy's attorney, pushed the judge for a spring trial.

"I am not going to have this woman sit incarcerated for the next year or two or three," he said. "I want a date and I want it this spring."

But prosecutor Jennifer Sprague said she wants to hear Judge Sullivan's rulings on Monday's arguments before the prosecution commits to a new date or specifics for a potential retrial.

When the judge asked for more details on how prosecutors planned to proceed with a potential retrial, Sprague responded: "This would be a retrial - as to what that looks like will depend".

But that appeared to frustrate Reddington.

"Why do we not know if the next trial is going to be murder in the first degree or a lesser charge, why do they need to wait for the motions? I need to know logistically."

Clancy was charged with three counts of first-degree-murder, which is the intentional and premeditated killing of another person.

Prosecutors could decide to bring lesser charges against Clancy in a retrial. For example, second-degree-murder charges, apply to unlawful killings committed with malice or extreme recklessness, but without prior planning.

News.title: Man who drugged and raped wife with strangers 'led double life'
News.content:
Warning: This article contains distressing content

A woman who believed she had not had sex for nine years had in fact been regularly drugged and raped by her own husband and a group of strangers "whose depravity knew no bounds", a jury has been told.

Her husband led a "double life", prosecutors said, regularly giving his wife a "stupefying cocktail" of drugs to make her "completely unaware" of the abuse.

He and four men have already pleaded guilty to a series of offences, but the trial of nine other defendants who deny all charges has begun at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court.

Opening the case for the prosecution, Louise Oakley KC said the wife had been "happy" but "the life she knew ended when the police knocked on the front door".

Before the case was opened, trial judge Maurice Greene warned jurors they would be expected to view evidence that could provoke feelings of "upset and anger".

As Oakley opened the case, they were shown videos of the woman being raped and sexually assaulted while, the prosecution said, she was unconscious.

The jury heard the husband and vicitim had the appearance of a couple looking forward to retirement, who "led busy lives, enjoying their home and garden, socialising with family and friends, holidays abroad â all very much together".

But Oakley said the husband, who is also in his 60s and cannot be named to protect his wife's legal right to anonymity, had since 2004 been sharing videos and images online of himself raping and assaulting his unconscious wife at their family home in the Stockport area of Greater Manchester.

"You may think it difficult to conceive how such offending could get worse, but it did," she told the court.

News.title: Parents' concerns to trigger urgent checks in A&E
News.content:
A similar "early warning" system to identify acutely ill adults, including those with sepsis, is already in use in emergency and general NHS hospital wards.

More than 90 hospitals across England have been using the alert system in children's wards, with different age-appropriate assessments available for babies through to teenagers.

The NHS has already said it will expand Martha's Rule to all hospital emergency departments in England. The rule gives patients, families and carers the right to request a rapid review if they are worried that a patient's condition is getting worse and their concerns are not being responded to.

The initiative is named after Martha Mills, who died aged 13 in 2021 after developing blood poisoning, or sepsis, in hospital following a bike accident.

A coroner ruled that her family's concerns about her worsening condition were not listened to and she would probably have survived had she been moved to intensive care earlier.

Martha's parents Merope and Paul came up with the idea of the rule in a bid to change the culture that contributed to her death.

A&E units will have a dedicated phone number that can be called to trigger an urgent review of a patient's care.

Duncan Burton, chief nursing officer for England, said the new early warning system for children in emergency departments was an "important next step in improving care for children and young people across England for this winter - and beyond".

He added: "In fast-paced emergency departments, staff need to spot quickly when a child's condition is deteriorating.

"This standardised approach will help them recognise the warning signs, communicate concerns, and make timely decisions when every moment matters."

The early warning system for children, PEWS, is a collaboration between NHS England and the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health and the Royal College of Nursing.

News.title: Train attacker said 'I am the baddest', trial hears
News.content:
A man accused of a mass train stabbing was heard saying "I am the baddest, no-one is as bad as me", on a different train the day before the attack, a court has heard.

Anthony Williams is accused of attempting to murder 10 people on a London-bound train which had to make an emergency stop in Huntingdon, Cambridgeshire on 1 November last year.

A passenger texted the British Transport Police reporting a male behaving erratically the night before, Cambridge Crown Court heard.

Williams, 33, of Langford Road in Peterborough, denies 14 counts of attempted murder over events on the train, and beforehand in Peterborough and London.

He is accused of trying to kill three people in Peterborough during the evening of 31 October. Later that night he boarded a train from the city's railway station, headed towards London.

In a statement read to jurors, another passenger, Keirah Lee-Oakman, said a male entered the train, sat down and "appeared to be talking and mumbling to himself".

She said he began walking up and down the carriages stating "boom and power", repeatedly saying things like "I haven't got it" as well as referencing the devil, jurors were told.

Lee-Oakman said he was "acting in an aggressive and intimidating manner... I felt unsafe" and while on the train she sent a text to the British Transport Police.

Jurors heard police officers attended Stevenage station but the male dropped down on to the tracks and officers eventually deemed it unsafe to continue following him.

News.title: Labour ends power-sharing with Greens in 11 councils over Zionism row
News.content:
The Labour Party has pulled out of power-sharing agreements with the Green Party in 11 local councils, after the national party adopted a policy defining Zionism as a form of racism.

Labour councillors will no longer be in coalition with the Greens in areas including Sheffield, Warwick and Lewes.

Labour Party chair Bridget Phillipson said: "Labour has been clear from the start that the "Zionism is Racism" policy crosses a line and we cannot work with any party that supports it â at any level of government."

Green leader Zack Polanski said the move would "backfire" on Labour and accused the party of wanting to "interrupt your local services and impose genocide support from it's local councils".

In October, Green Party members backed a motion, entitled "Zionism is racism", which said Zionism was an ideology that supported an "ethnonationalist Jewish State in historic Palestine". Israel has denied committing genocide in Gaza.

The motion also backed a "single democratic Palestinian State", including in modern-day Israel.

Having been backed by party members, the motion became Green Party policy, but it has left senior figures bitterly divided. Jewish groups and opposition political parties have condemned it.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham told MPs in October that Labour would not partner with the Greens over the "antisemitic" policy.

Labour then issued an ultimatum from Labour's head office to Labour-Green councils, demanding that local Greens disown the motion passed by members at their national party conference.

Green groups were also asked to call on their party's national leadership to reconsider the policy.

Labour said there were local agreements in place in 18 authorities. Of those, Labour said 11 had not met the criteria it demanded.

The areas are:

Arun District Council

Derbyshire Dales District Council

Havant Borough Council

Lewes District Council (The Green Party announced last week it was "mutually" ending its alliance with Labour)

Runnymede Borough Council (Labour says local co-operation had already ceased)

Sheffield City Council

Stafford Borough Council

Warwick District Council

Wealden District Council

West Devon Borough Council

West Suffolk Council

Labour said its conditions had been met in Broadland, Monmouthshire, North Somerset, Rother, West Oxfordshire and West Sussex. The party said that Coventry City Council does not have a formal arrangement in place and that no such deal will be made in the future.

It will continue co-operating with the Greens in the West of England mayoralty, where the deputy mayor is a Green member.

Green Party leader Zack Polanski has said the motion was "imperfect" but has defended its central premise, arguing that Israel's actions towards the Palestinian people are "clearly underpinned by racist ideology".

The collapse of co-operation at the local level could impact hundreds of thousands of residents through budgets and policy decisions taking longer to get voted through.

Green and Labour councillors in the impacted areas will now have to seek alternative coalition partners or try to govern as a minority administration.

In a joint statement, the Green Party and the Local Government Association Green Group said it was "hugely disappointed" that Labour had forced local leaders into "jeopardising successful progressive partnerships that are delivering benefits for residents".

News.title: Mother told to book appointment to give birth to baby who had died
News.content:
Warning: This article contains themes and images some readers may find upsetting.

A seven-month pregnant woman whose unborn baby died after she was discharged from hospital while suffering from a life-threatening condition was told by staff to make an appointment to give birth.

Danielle Brown, 31, from North Tyneside, said she was devastated to have to return home knowing the baby she was carrying was no longer alive.

She said no family should be put through the same experience and wants hospitals to offer alternatives for those grieving.

After she was discharged from hospital suffering with pre-eclampsia, Danielle insisted on returning to the maternity unit as she felt so unwell and was seen by doctors.

She was told her daughter had died but, instead of delivering the baby, the hospital sent her home and told her to ring to book a slot to give birth.

Her partner Anthony Miller, 34, described it as "horrible... lying in bed and holding that belly" knowing their baby was not alive.

The Newcastle Hospitals NHS Trust said it fully accepted "aspects of the care we provided fell short" and offered a "heartfelt apology".

News.title: Teen had leg amputated after stabbing on beach on bank holiday, court hears
News.content:
In the moment after the attack, the 17-year-old fell to the ground and looked pale, saying: "I am going, I feel myself going."

Ahmed then fled the scene and discarded the knife close to a nearby building, an act seen by an eyewitness who later identified the 19-year-old in an identity parade.

Before he threw the object Ahmed was heard saying: "I need to dash this."

He was also captured fleeing the scene by a woman who was taking selfies on the beach with her partner.

The court heard the 17-year-old was taken by air ambulance to the University Hospital of Wales in Cardiff, and had sustained an injury to the main blood vessel in his right leg, with one artery completely blocked.

Despite several transfusions, oxygen was not flowing properly to the leg and a decision was reached that an amputation was necessary.

The court heard the teenager had a through knee amputation - removing the lower half of the leg.

Ahmed was questioned by police shortly after the incident and responded "no comment" to most of the questions, but the court heard he denied stabbing anyone and said he knew nothing about the incident and was released.

Gobir said it was the prosecution's case that the defendant was the person responsible for stabbing the victim and "that he must have intended to cause him really serious harm by stabbing him to a vital part of his body with such a dangerous weapon".

The court was then shown CCTV from various cameras around Barry Island Pleasure Park area showing the groups of teenagers on the day of the incident.

On Tuesday afternoon, the jury were played a police interview with the victim where he explained more about the incident.

He said that some of his female friends had started talking to a large group of boys as they sat on the rocks.

He said that a male friend had started to get nervous, believing he "might have had a problem with these boys" but the teenager tried to calm the situation with the other group.

He said he did not know the reason why he was attacked, describing the sensation of being stabbed as "like a punch", adding "I knew straight away I had been stabbed".

He said it was a "sharp pain" but it "didn't really sting how you'd expect it to".

He described how he was in and out of consciousness as he was taken to the hospital but remembered seeing his friend being attacked by another man with a plastic shovel. He said in total he had to have four surgeries on his leg.

The trial continues.

News.title: Driver who dragged head teacher to his death jailed
News.content:
Warning: This article contains distressing content

A driver who dragged a head teacher to his death for more than a mile under the wheels of his car has been jailed for life for murder.

Simon Richardson, 35, crashed into 56-year-old Michael Mullins in Warburton, Greater Manchester, on 20 April as the married father-of-two cycled home from Stretford Grammar School in Trafford.

Jurors at Richardson's trial heard he then stopped to try to dislodge the injured but still-living cyclist before driving on with him still lodged underneath the vehicle.

The judge at Manchester Minshull Street Crown Court told Richardson that he would have to serve a minimum of 25 years in prison.

Richardson had previous convictions for 28 offences, with a "significant history" of driving-related crimes.

He was also on bail at the time of the murder for offences including affray and assault occasioning actual bodily harm.

Mrs Justice Brunner KC said Richardson, who looked straight ahead as he was being sentenced, "took away a life and in doing so you caused devastation to a family and a community".

She added: "You deliberately used your car as a weapon over a prolonged period.

"You have repeated convictions for a range of serious driving offences over a 15-year period.

"This demonstrates the complete contempt you have for the law."

The judge told the court she had to hand Richardson a lifetime driving ban to "protect the public".

News.title: Reform council leader quits after staff comments leaked
News.content:
The Reform UK leader of Leicestershire County Council has announced he is standing down after comments he made about staff redundancies were leaked online.

Dan Harrison announced on Monday that he would be stepping down from the role he has held since May 2025.

He said he had made the decision after taking advice from senior Reform colleagues, and added deputy council leader Kevin Crook had taken over as acting leader.

It comes after Harrison had apologised after being recorded saying 76 council solicitors would be made redundant, branding them "incompetent", before saying "what I want to look at now is the women", in remarks which were then released on social media.

In a statement, Harrison said it had been the "honour of his life" to lead the county council's first Reform administration.

Harrison has said he will remain as a councillor, representing the Ashby-de-la-Zouch division.

The Conservative opposition at County Hall had called for Harrison to resign after his comments about staff were leaked.

In the recording, Harrison said: "There's 76 solicitors will be made redundant.

"We'll buy in the service, because [they are] incompetent. They're not doing a good job.

"What I want to look at now is the women so it is ongoing, I would like it to be at great pace but I can tell you now if we suddenly drove massive redundancies the liberals would walk away."

News.title: British adventurer Karl Bushby completes 28-year journey
News.content:
As they had agreed years earlier, Bushby's mother, Angela, waited for him at her home in Sutton Park, where she raised him.

He appeared almost lost for words, telling the BBC moments after the meeting: âIt feels surreal. Itâs the end of a 28-year journey.â

His mother, who had not seen him for a decade, told Bushby: âWhere have you been?â

She told the media: âItâs good to have him home.

âI feel relieved.â

Bushby said he was "still processing" being home, admitting his head was "one big blurry mess".

Asked what is next for him, he said: "I have a story to tell."

As well as working with acclaimed German filmmaker, Werner Herzog, on a documentary, he confirmed he is working on a second book about his travels.

Bushby admitted he never expected such a homecoming.

Addressing a large crowd in the city centre, Bushby, when he was received by the lord mayor, Maria Coward, said: âThere has never been a welcome home like this, I am sure. It's madness. An enormous thank you."

He added: "The biggest team - Earth - got me back here.â

On Sunday, when he crossed the Humber Bridge into East Yorkshire, he was met by his 36-year-old son Adam, his 12-year-old granddaughter whom he had never met, his father and brothers.

âIt was amazing,â Bushby said of that reunion.

News.title: Ellen DeGeneres mourns unexpected death of her talk show producer Matthew Wright
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Ellen DeGeneres is mourning the death of her longtime talk show producer, Matthew Wright.

Wright, 52, died October 30 in what is described on GoFundMe as an “unfathomable tragedy” while working remotely in Los Angeles. He worked on Ellen for 16 years, until the daytime talk show’s 2022 conclusion.

Further details weren’t immediately available.

“So Matt Wright, who was our executive producer and was featured on our show a lot, died the other day,” a teary-eyed DeGeneres began in an Instagram video posted Monday.

“And he was an amazing guy,” she continued, growing emotional. “He was funny. God, he made me laugh. He would surprise me with things that he did all the time. He was smart. He was kind. He was the part of our show that — I mean, everyone loved him.

“I loved him. And it’s just shocking — it’s shocking,” she added.

DeGeneres said she and Wright were about to start a project together at the time of his death.

“We lost a good guy. He was a good guy,” she continued. “He and tWitch were so close, and now he and tWitch are together dancing and laughing,” she added, referencing the long-time DJ on her show who died in 2022 aged 40.

DeGeneres concluded the video with a montage of Wright’s moments on Ellen.

The comedian also donated $5,000 to the GoFundMe established to aid Wright’s family. At the time of publication, more than $42,000 had been donated, approaching the goal of $50,000.

open image in gallery Ellen DeGeneres is mourning the loss of her longtime producer ( Ellen DeGeneres/Instagram )

“His husband, father, sister and niece are in New York, desperate to be reunited for a proper goodbye. We’re asking for all of his friends, who Matt loved so fully, to help the family at this time,” the fundraiser description read.

“As many of you know, Matt & Justin were both laid off this summer. And the unexpected costs of getting Matt home, a funeral and a memorial are impossible for the family to bear.”

News.title: Kennedy Center announces honorees as Trump continues legal fight to get name on building
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The next class of Kennedy Center honorees has been announced as the storied institution remains in turmoil.

Singers Paul Anka and Barbara Mandrell, composer David Foster, actor Andy Garcia and writer David Mamet will be honored at a celebration held December 7 at the Capital One Arena in Washington, D.C.

Typically held at the Kennedy Center, the celebration has been relocated due to an ongoing legal battle being pursued by Donald Trump as he fights to have his name added to the building.

The center was temporarily shut to the public in September by its board of trustees. Still, the annual tradition of honoring Americans who have contributed to the performing arts will continue.

“We are recognizing amazing artists whose lifelong work has shaped American culture and inspired generations of audiences. We are proud to honor this year’s class and to continue a tradition that has defined the Center for nearly 50 years,” Trump said in a statement, per The Hollywood Reporter.

open image in gallery David Foster, a 16-time Grammy winner, will be honored ( Getty )

open image in gallery Paul Anka and Barbara Mandrell are among the new class of honorees ( Getty )

The actual celebration centers around tribute performances to the honorees.

Anka is arguably best known for writing the lyrics to Frank Sinatra’s classic “My Way,” though his own hits include “Diana,” “Lonely Boy,” “Put Your Head on My Shoulder” and “Having My Baby.”

Country singer Mandrell is known for her signature anthem “I Was Country When Country Wasn't Cool,” along with “Sleeping Single in a Double Bed” and “(If Loving You Is Wrong) I Don't Want to Be Right.” She retired in 1997.

Playwright Mamet, a known Trump supporter, is the writer behind “Glengarry Glen Ross” and “American Buffalo.”

Garcia, an Oscar nominee for his role in The Godfather Part III, had his breakout role in The Untouchables (1987) and went on to feature in the Ocean’s franchise.

Foster is a 16-time Grammy winner who has co-written songs including “The Prayer,” “After the Love Has Gone,” “You're the Inspiration” and “I Have Nothing.”

open image in gallery Playwright David Mamet is a Kennedy Center honoree ( Fox News )

open image in gallery Andy Garcia is an Oscar nominee for his role in 'The Godfather Part III' ( Getty )

Trump hosted last year’s ceremony, which honored Sylvester Stallone, Gene Simmons, Gloria Gaynor, George Strait and Michael Crawford. The event, aired on CBS and Paramount+, drew its smallest ever audience, with 35 percent fewer viewers than the previous year.

It is not yet clear if he will return to host this year. The Independent has reached out to the White House for comment.

Trump and his team are desperately trying to convince a federal judge to approve the center to close in order to complete a two-year, $257-million renovation. But Democratic Rep. Joyce Beatty of Ohio has challenged the closure with a lawsuit.

In September, a federal judge ordered the Trump administration to provide at least 30 days’ notice before making any physical changes to the Kennedy Center — including demolishing it — after the venue’s Trump-controlled board voted to shutter the venue for repairs.

Matt Floca, the venue’s Trump-appointed director, decided to “temporarily” close the Kennedy Center due to “acute risks to public safety resulting from continued structural deterioration” of the building, according to the Department of Justice.

However, members of the National Symphony Orchestra have continued to rehearse inside the shuttered facilities.

News.title: Bruce Springsteen endorses Abdul El-Sayed: ‘He’s a fighter against the anti-American leadership currently in the White House’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Bruce Springsteen has thrown his support behind progressive Democrat candidate Dr. Abdul El-Sayed in the competitive Michigan Senate race.

In a post on Instagram, the 77-year-old New Jersey rocker took a swipe at the Trump administration in announcing his endorsement.

Springsteen wrote: “Dr. El-Sayed is a fighter for our American Constitution, he’s a fighter for our American Democracy, and he’s a fighter against the corrupt, lawless, and anti-American leadership currently in the White House. That’s why I’m in his corner 100%.”

The Independent has approached the White House for comment.

El-Sayed has found himself at the center of Democratic party infighting after Rep. Haley Stevens, who he defeated in the party’s primary, endorsed his Republican Senate rival Mike Rogers.

Springsteen called Dr Abdul El-Sayed ‘a fighter against the corrupt, lawless, and anti-American leadership currently in the White House’ ( Getty )

Stevens announced her endorsement in a video over the weekend, withdrawing her support for El-Sayed after a falling-out over Israel.

“As you may have seen, our Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate, Abdul, said I was no longer welcome in his campaign and that I should stay away, and he's right,” Stevens said. “And that’s why I am endorsing Mike Rogers for the U.S. Senate today.”

Senate Majority Leader Chuck Schumer reacted with fury, writing on X: “This is a despicable betrayal from Rep. Stevens. Senate Democrats are united in our support for Abdul El-Sayed, because we know he will fight for the economic interests of working families in Michigan, unlike Mike Rogers, who is a tool of Donald Trump and billionaire donors.”

Former House speaker Nancy Pelosi was also angry, posting on the same platform: “Haley Stevens has chosen to dangerously betray Michigan families’ healthcare, freedoms and future with her horrific endorsement of Mike Rogers. Abdul El-Sayed must win – because Michigan and our country deserve better.”

President Donald Trump, however, was delighted and took to Truth Social to celebrate the endorsement.

“Wow, this is BIG,” the Republican wrote. “Stevens, a Highly Respected Democrat, who narrowly lost in the Primary to Abdul Mohamed El-Sayed, and who has been breathlessly wined and dined by the Dumocrats to help in their Michigan Campaign for the United States Senate against Mike Rogers, has just ENDORSED Mike Rogers for Senate!”

“Haley said what few people are willing to say,” he continued. “She showed great and almost unprecedented loyalty to the Great People of Michigan with what she did. It’s a thing called bravery, and few people have it like just displayed by Congresswoman Haley Stevens!”

Trump has endorsed Rogers and repeatedly attacked El-Sayed, the Michigan-born son of Egyptian immigrants, as a “violent jihadist,” urging voters to “send him back to where he came from.”

Springsteen, meanwhile, has been an outspoken Democrat, using his platform and talent to rally against the Trump White House.

Earlier this year, he released “Streets of Minneapolis,” a song dedicated to Renee Good and Alex Pretti, two civilians who were shot dead by ICE agents in the city.

He also used the lyrics to hurl insults at Trump and his ICE agents’ ongoing invasion of the Minnesota city with pointed lyrics about “King Trump” and his “private army.”

News.title: Liam Neeson reveals his most memorable stunt: ‘I was very, very concerned’
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Liam Neeson has revealed the most memorable stunt from his lengthy movie career, admitting he was “very, very concerned” when it was being filmed.

The 74-year-old Taken star is currently promoting his latest action film The Mongoose, which sees him star as a United States Army Special Forces veteran leading police in an epic car chase across Texas. Marisa Tomei and Ving Rhames also appear.

The movie is directed by Mark Vanselow, Neeson’s longtime stunt double.

Looking back on their years of collaboration in an interview with Entertainment Tonight, Neeson singled out the waterfall scene in 2006’s Seraphim Falls as being particularly memorable.

“There was a waterfall sequence,” Neeson said. “When we shot it, we had to have a waterfall that wasn’t frozen with ice and winter conditions. We found it, and Mark does a stunt coming over that waterfall. It was freezing cold water and I was very, very concerned.”

Liam Neeson, pictured at the Toronto International Film Festival in September 2026, says his most memorable stunt was in Western 'Seraphim Falls' ( Getty )

Vanselow added: “Yeah, it was dynamic. It was in Oregon, and it had rained for 30 days straight and it was raining all throughout the shooting, so the river was just engorged with water. I was actually underneath a helicopter going over the falls.”

He continued: “The best part about that story is the pilot, who worked with us on The Mongoose, Craig Hosking. At the end of it we had a warming tank, and landing area. He dipped me in the hot tub like a martini olive, then landed the helicopter next to it.”

Seraphim Falls was a 2006 revisionist Western set shortly after the American Civil War starring Neeson and Pierce Brosnan. Neeson starred as former Confederate Colonel Morsman Carver, leading a relentless manhunt against a former Union officer named Gideon (Brosnan).

Earlier this year, Neeson expressed significant apprehension regarding the future of cinema, pointing to the increasing trend of films bypassing traditional theatrical releases in favor of streaming platforms.

Speaking to the Press Association, Neeson articulated his worries about the evolving landscape of Hollywood, saying: “The movie industry is changing, streaming services are merging, companies are being bought out. We’re all very concerned about the state of Hollywood. What’s going to happen to feature films?”

Reflecting on his own career, Neeson added: “I’ve been very, very lucky. I have friends and acquaintances, actors, some of whom haven’t worked for months and months. It’s a profession filled with rejection. It really is.”

News.title: ‘It’s very scary’: Fridge temperatures soar in European supermarkets after suspected hack
News.content:

Supermarket giants across Europe have warned of a fresh string of cyberattacks as fridge and freezer temperatures unexpectedly spike.

An IT incident overnight hit fridges and freezers in dozens of stores across Belgium, Estonia and Luxembourg, retailers Ahold Delhaize, Carrefour and Colruyt said on Monday.

Swedish grocers ICA and Coop, as well as an Ikea superstore also reported similar temperature increases, with one store explicitly blaming a cyberattack.

In Ireland, refrigeration systems at 13 SuperValu stores were also impacted by a suspected cyberattack.

It comes after Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize reported a cyber security incident to police in October after detecting “suspicious activity” in its infrastructure. On Monday, the chain realised there were temperature increases in the cooling systems.

A spokesperson for the company said it is investigating the incident.

The potential attack follows a similar incident in France last month, in which police said hackers seized control of cooling units at hundreds of supermarkets, raising temperatures as high as 50C and causing fires and food loss.

open image in gallery A handful of Swedish supermarkets saw temperatures in their refrigerators and freezers soar early on 2 November, 2026, two chains said, forcing them to throw away spoiled food ( AFP/Getty )

CEO of Belgian refrigeration company Sabcobel, Stephan Moelans, which operates Delhaize’s systems, said the incident was a cyberattack, in which the units’ evaporators were switched to defrost mode. Moelans’ office declined to comment when contacted by reporters.

A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, ‌which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, said five shops had their fridge systems attacked.

One Swedish ICA store said on social media that the temperature of its refrigerators and freezers had been “hacked” overnight and set to 50C. It said later that the store had since reopened.

At an ICA Baronen store in Stockholm, a notice said all the shop’s freezers were broken due to a cyberattack. The store’s sales manager said the attack happened at 2am local time but wasn’t noticed until 5.30am.

“We’re aware that a limited number of stores were affected by an incident overnight, which impacted their refrigeration and freezer systems,” a spokesperson at ICA said over email.

Grocery retail group Coop told local news that ​six of its stores had been affected by similar incidents. It did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

An Estonian supermarket chain was also affected, with temperatures set to 50C, technology ​supplier Kitman Coldtech told public broadcaster ERR.

“This is very fresh, ‌it happened this morning,” Kitman CEO Jann Mutso said. He declined to name the affected grocery chain.

Luc De Laet, founder and owner of Belgian butchery chain De Laet & Van Haver, said he was woken at 3.30am by an employee telling him there was a problem.

He rushed to his store in Hove, south of Antwerp, and found the fridges turned up as high as 18C. He said it had ruined some €15,000 worth of meat.

“It’s very scary. They are hacking the system that is doing the registration of the temperature, and they can program it at a distance,” he told Reuters.

Mr De Laet said he felt the hackers were trying to destabilise European economies, adding that he had contacted police but didn’t know if there was an investigation.

He said: “I only have two words for them: wake up, please, because there’s something going on.”

News.title: Bill Murray has one-word answer on whether fame makes him happy
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

Bill Murray gave a pithy answer when asked if fame has brought him happiness.

The 76-year-old Ghostbusters star is asked the question in the fourth episode of his golf-based travel series A Course Called Ireland.

He replies: “In a word, no.”

The new show, which is based on author Tom Coyne’s bestselling book of the same name, follows Murray and Coyne as they travel through Northern Ireland and the Republic of Ireland playing every golf course and meeting locals.

In between the games, the pair reflect on life. The series also stars Irish stars including The IT Crowd’s Chris O’Dowd and comedian and recent Traitors competitor Joanne McNally.

Bill Murray, pictured in New York in October 2026, has reflected on whether worldwide fame has brought him personal happiness ( Bennett Raglin/Getty Images for Rivian )

In another scene in the series, O’Dowd asks Murray how he deals with constant requests for photographs, and the former Saturday Night Live star responds: “I come from the era where, like, I thought autographs were the worst thing that ever happened, and I’d give anything to have it back.”

He adds: “But, you know, I’ve done all kinds of things and tried to control it and do it according to my terms, and I find that it’s an enormous waste of energy to ever try to direct it. Now, I just jump in and go.… I take the camera. I take the picture.”

In 2022, Murray spoke to The Independent about his experiences with fame, and about being looked to for humor and comedy even while experiencing his own depressive episodes.

He recounted finding solace in the work of the late country musician John Prine, saying: “I remember my friend Hunter Thompson, who was another guy people perceived as sort of a dark force but who really had a wonderful sense of humour, talking about John Prine.”

He continued: “I remember at one of the moodiest… What did he used to call it? Broodingest! …at one of the broodingest moments of our long weekend, he said: ‘Well, we’ll have to rely on John Prine for the sense of humour.’ And he put on some, and it was dark out there in the mountains, and we did listen to John Prine for a while.”

Murray added: “There was a moment where I was the most miserable of my whole life, so I thought, I’ll go see if John Prine will help me here. His song ‘Linda Goes to Mars’ comes on and I just remember going: ‘Heh’. That was it. That was all there was, but it was a change of direction. I thought: ‘Goddammit, it worked!’ I hadn’t even ‘Heh’d’ in such a while.”

News.title: US dairy worker dies from bird flu as outbreak rages in cattle
News.content:
“People at greater risk include dairy workers and others who have close or prolonged contact with infected animals or environments contaminated with the virus. Transmission of avian influenza between humans is extremely rare and has never been documented in the United States. Public health officials are continuing to monitor individuals who had close contact with the patient for symptoms,” the health district said in a statement.

Experts say the US bird flu outbreak is not only costing the dairy industry millions of dollars but also raises the risk that the virus could mutate to spread more easily between mammals. They are also concerned that authorities are doing little to check the spread.

Marc Johnson, a virologist at the University of Missouri, told the Telegraph last week that the outbreak in dairy cattle was “completely preventable”.

“Cattle infections last only a few weeks before the animals recover. If infected herds were simply isolated until the outbreak fizzled out, it would stop.

“But cattle keep being moved around, spreading it into new states,” said Dr Johnson, referring to the way the US dairy industry operates, in which cows are routinely transported across state lines, whether to join new herds, for breeding, or to replace animals at large milk-producing operations.

A bird flu outbreak has also been raging on a mink farm in Utah for the last couple of months, according to news outlet ProPublica.

Jonathan Ball, professor of molecular virology at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, said allowing a virus to rage unchecked raises the risk of it mutating.

“Viruses like influenza are constantly exploring new hosts, and more often than not, it burns out. It’s not quite got the right combination of genetic changes to allow it to efficiently infect, efficiently replicate, and then efficiently transmit to the new host. But the longer these steps - adaptive changes, so genetic changes - are happening in these sporadic outbreaks, the more likelihood you’ve got of it mutating. It’s a bit like a one-armed bandit machine - if you keep pulling that handle, eventually you’re going to get three cherries,” he said.

News.title: First ever trial of long-acting injection against malaria to launch in Africa
News.content:
Dr Cristina Donini, executive vice-president of research and development at MMV, said the compound would be “complementary” to existing tools, rather than replacing them.

“The vaccine is doing a fantastic job in infants but if you could add onto that another tool that can cover a broader population with a longer regimen then we would be in a very good position to eliminate the disease,” she said.

Children in malaria-endemic regions are already given prophylactic drugs during the malaria season and studies have shown that these combined with the vaccine are highly effective. However, resistance has developed to these drugs and they have to be given monthly.

The malaria season in Africa varies by region but usually peaks after periods of rainfall. If the season lasts longer than three to four months it’s likely that people would need two injections. However, Dr Donini and her colleagues are working on a second generation LAI which they hope would provide year-long coverage.

Full costs have not yet been worked out but Dr Donini said affordability was an important factor in assessing the LAI’s suitability.

“It’s too early to say whether it will be cheaper than an injection - hopefully, yes. The beauty of it is that if you simplify it and decrease the number of injections needed you decrease the cost,” she said.

LAIs are gaining traction in the fight against infectious diseases - Lenacapavir, now being rolled out after being approved in 2025, provides almost 100% protection against infection from HIV and many believe it could help end the HIV pandemic. There are also LAI candidates in development for the prevention of tuberculosis, treatment and prevention of which usually relies on daily pills being taken over many months.

Lottie Renwick, global campaign director at Malaria No More UK, welcomed the launch of the trial.

“Thanks to sustained investment in malaria science including here in the UK, we are now on the brink of a number of breakthroughs which could turn the tide on the fight against the disease. And the long-acting injectable, specifically, could be a valuable addition to this toolbox as it has the potential to provide sustained protection from a single shot, avoiding the need for repeat doses.

“This phase of the trial also builds on earlier research conducted in the UK, highlighting the importance of the UK’s ongoing role as a malaria science superpower and the value of continued investment in malaria R&D. We look forward to the trial progressing further and eagerly await the results.”
