News.title: Arsenal nous frustrates Liverpool as 14-year Anfield hoodoo ends with statement win
News.content:
It is clear and obvious that Arsenal will be the team to beat in the Premier League title race, especially given that we do not yet know the fate of faltering Manchester City and their looming punishment.

A statement victory against Liverpool, their first in the league at Anfield since 2012, took Arsenal back to the top. And who would bet against them staying there and retaining their title?

Few would when they defend and manage a game – and it was game management in every sense – like this. From the formidable to the cynical – that was the statement. Against the Scousers, Arsenal had the nous.

News.title: Tears flow for Antonelli after becoming youngest champion in F1 history
News.content:
Welcome to our coverage for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez. Today could be the day for Kimi Antonelli, the day he becomes a Formula One world champion. In fact it is very likely. All he needs to confirm the drivers’ championship is to finish ninth or higher. If George Russell or Lewis Hamilton do not claim victory then he is champion whatever happens. Given his season so far, it is difficult to see the title fight going to Brazil next week.

What chance of a decent race here today? The first few laps are often entertaining as the pack bunches up and there are plenty of chances to overtake early on. Generally the top four teams have been close together (last week in Austin excluded) and it is possible to overtake here, though it is not exactly easy.

Qualifying yesterday as an intriguing and close session. Hamilton secured his first grand prix pole for Ferrari, by just 0.009sec from the Mercedes of George Russell, with Charles Leclerc of Ferrari a little behind him in third. Then came Max Verstappen, Antonelli, Norris, Hadjar and Lindblad. Liam Lawson was disqualified on a technicality.

Ferrari have been an up-and-down team this season but have been strong without really delivering on it fully in the last few rounds. Could they secure a third victory of the season today? They do not really need to worry about losing second in the constructors to Red Bull or McLaren and Mercedes are too far out of reach in any case.

In any case, the biggest story is likely to be Antonelli’s coronation in Mexico. Hamilton has won titles here before for Mercedes, will the Italian give the Silver Arrows another fiesta in Mexico City? The race starts at 8pm GMT and we will be here for all the build-up, live updates and reaction from it.

News.title: Lewis Hamilton becomes oldest driver to claim pole position in 44 years
News.content:
Welcome to our live coverage for qualifying for the 2026 Mexico City Grand Prix from the Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez in Mexico City, obviously. The big story this weekend is that Jimi Antonelli is almost certain to become the youngest world champion in Formula One history. To guarantee it he needs just two points, but if George Russell or Lewis Hamilton fail to win here then the title is his whatever he does. It has been a superb, strong and consistent season from the man who began the year as a teenager. He has not quite been faultless, but he has not been far away.

There are other stories floating around the paddock, too. Notably, Esteban Ocon has been dropped by Haas today for final practice, qualifying and the race, to be replaced by reserve driver Ryo Hirakawa for the weekend. Whether Ocon will continue in any other races has yet to be confirmed but you have to say that it seems extremely unlikely. More on that later.

Another line is the ongoing tension between Liam Lawson and Max Verstappen after their crash in FP2 yesterday. It was certainly a strange one in which neither driver backed down, which resulted in contact, debris being strewn across the track and a red flag. Both drivers seemed unrepentant, though admitted it was clumsy. Lawson and Verstappen each receive a one-place grid penalty for the incident, which feels about right given how silly and unnecessary it all was.

But what about the competitive order on track? Since the summer break, and a little before in fairness, things have been unpredictable at the top. Mercedes have still, on average, been the best team but Ferrari, Red Bull and McLaren have all had their moments.

What happened in final practice? It was Lando Norris who topped the timesheets by just 0.001sec ahead of Mercedes’ Antonelli. Charles Leclerc was a further tenth or so back for Ferrari followed by Oscar Piastri in the other McLaren, who was 0.195sec off his team-mate’s pace. Then came Verstappen, Hamilton, Russell, Isack Hadjar, Lawson and Arvid Lindblad. All drivers were within 0.6sec off Norris, which promises a close qualifying session. Let’s hope we get it.

News.title: Suzuki howler costs Aston Villa crucial points
News.content:
Tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

“If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery said. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”

In the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

News.title: Alex Mitchell injury blow for England but Northampton dig deep to win
News.content:
England were dealt a fresh blow ahead of their Nations Championship opener with Australia after scrum-half Alex Mitchell was forced off early in Northampton’s victory over Gloucester.

Mitchell left the field gingerly 20 minutes into the action after picking up a suspected hamstring injury following an innocuous coming-together with Gloucester winger Will Joseph.

The Saints scrum-half has suffered a series of hamstring issues this year – this would be a fourth time he has picked up a problem – and he looked visibly disappointed as he limped off.

He suffered a left leg hamstring tear during England’s Six Nations defeat to Ireland which left him sidelined for two months and, in a cruel twist of fate, sustained another on his right leg during an England three-day training camp in Bagshot last May. He suffered the injury for a third time in England’s 73-8 rout of Fiji in July.

With Mitchell’s club-mate, Archie McParland, nursing an unspecified knock that forced him to miss Saints’ high-stakes clash with Gloucester, Jack van Poortvliet is likely to start at nine against the Wallabies next Sunday. McParland was the third-choice scrum-half in England’s Nations Championship squad, but Steve Borthwick may be forced to look elsewhere if Mitchell’s prognosis is serious.

News.title: Spurs win three in row for first time in 616 days to pile pressure on Sage
News.content:
Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League encounter between Tottenham and Crystal Palace.

Last weekend, Spurs enjoyed a historic result, beating Chelsea 2-0 at Stamford Bridge for only the second time in the league for 36 years thanks to Mike Penders’ own goal and Mathys Tel’s stunning solo strike. This result, coupled with the 3-1 victory over Coventry City in their previous home outing, means that Tottenham have won back-to-back league games and are beginning to gather some momentum under Roberto De Zerbi.

In his pre-match press conference, when asked if he’s felt a change in atmosphere after the triumph at Stamford Bridge, De Zerbi replied: “We have not achieved our goal. We want our fans to be happy, not now, at the end of the season. Now we have to push, we have to stay focused, we have to increase the spirit, the appetite to win games in a row. To do that, we have to show if we are good enough. If we are good enough on the pitch, for sure we are ready. In the head, in the mentality, we have to show, because the step of this club is to win games in a row and to be angry day by day, game by game, win by win. One time or two times are not enough.”

Palace have endured a tricky and inconsistent start to the season under their summer appointment Pierre Sage, accumulating just seven points from their opening seven league matches while shipping 17 goals. The 1-0 League Cup victory over Fulham in midweek has momentarily eased the pressure on the Frenchman, but given their newfound success in recent campaigns, fan expectations have risen, with recent performances prompting some cause for concern.

Tottenham remain without the suspended Rodrigo Bentancur, while Xavi Simons, Wilson Odobert, Lucas Bergvall, Savio, Tosin Adarabioyo and Mykhaylo Mudryk are out injured. James Maddison was substituted early in the second half at Chelsea with an apparent groin strain, but De Zerbi insists he’s available for this one. Destiny Udogie could also be involved after recovering from a knee issue.

WEST HAM are reportedly weighing up whether to sack boss Nuno Espirito Santo after a poor start to the season.

The Hammers were seen as leading favourites to secure an immediate return to the Premier League after their relegation last season.



But Nuno’s men have stuttered so far and were beaten 3-1 at home to West Brom on Saturday.

That was their third defeat so far and they are now eighth in the table, six points off leaders Middlesbrough.



According to the Guardian, Nuno’s position is now “under threat” after back-to-back home losses.

The former Wolves and Tottenham boss is set to be given time to turn things around, the report says.



But Hammers chiefs are becoming “increasingly impatient” as they hope to clinch promotion at the first time of asking.

SunSport reported how Nuno was initially set to leave the London Stadium following the team’s relegation in the summer.

But he ended up staying on in the role after convincing officials he was the right man to bring the club back to the top flight.

However, it’s claimed West Ham aren’t happy after a run of two wins from six games.

Sports.title: Non-league clash abandoned after side losing 8-0 reduced to six men – because FOUR didn’t come back out for second half
Sports.content:

A NON-LEAGUE match was forced to be abandoned at half-time as FOUR players failed to come out for the second half.

Paulsgrove would have had better Saturda’s than their recent visit to Andover Town on the weekend.

The visitors were 7-0 down during the Hampshire Premier League Division One clash at the break and started the second half without FOUR players.



Andover scored another goal after half-time which saw another Paulsgrove player go down injured.



As a result, the match had to be abandoned due to the visitors having fewer than seven players.

Andover boss Robbie Skeates revealed that some of the opposition players decided not to come back to the pitch after half-time.

He labelled the situation a “complete farce” after the eighth goal went in.



He said: “I’ve been involved in football a long time and I’ve genuinely never seen anything like what happened today from an opposition side.

“All 11 of their players walked off perfectly fine at half-time with us 7-0 up.

“They eventually came back out with seven, so apparently four must have managed to get injured in the changing room.

“We scored pretty much straight away to make it 8-0 and from there it became a complete farce.”



Several posts on Paulsgrove’s official social media account claimed that all the players were actually injured.

The club even replied to Skeates’ post questioning the legitimacy of the injuries.

It read: “Sadly can’t make injured player continue. Thanks for asking how they are.”

Skeates has insisted that Andover would be submitting a report to the league.

Andover are mid-table while Paulsgrove are dead last after losing all 10 of their matches.

Sports.title: ‘About more than football’ – EFL club reveal shock plan to build 15,000-seater new stadium at airport
Sports.content:

CAMBRIDGE UNITED have unveiled plans to build a new stadium at the site of an airport.

The U’s have played matches at the Abbey Stadium since 1932.



But the League One side have lofty ambitions for the future and have been looking at ways to upgrade their current ground.

The club have now teamed up with The Hill Group, which just purchased the Cambridge East site for around £350million.



The firm bought the land from Marshall Group – the owner of Cambridge City Airport.

But Marshall Group has been told it must relocate its aviation operations by mid-2029 as the new owners plan a redevelopment.

A new 15,000-capacity stadium for Cambridge is among the ideas being discussed for the site after the club commissioned a report by Deloitte over possible projects.

The club are continuing to map out the proposals “without commitment from any party” and will conclude the process by Easter 2027.

Club chairman Godric Smith said: “We all love the magical place that is the Cledara Abbey Stadium.

“However, with sell-out crowds and an ageing stadium which significantly limits the club financially, it has become clearer than ever that our long-term future likely lies elsewhere.

Sports.title: Did Erling Haaland cost Man City the Premier League title? Liverpool vs Arsenal chaos is showing cheats prosper
Sports.content:
Next

CHEATS, we have long been told, never prosper… but it doesn’t stop them trying.

Players know that contact to the face or head can bring the ultimate on-field punishment — a red card.



When they are truly hit and hurt, it’s fair to go down. Sometimes accidental contacts are nasty and unpleasant.

Loose elbows — I’m talking to you Lisandro Martinez — dangerous play and retaliatory foolishness deserve to be sanctioned.



But I can’t be alone in thinking that if I want to see Oscar-winning acting I’ll go to the local cinema, not the Premier League.

It’s absolutely infuriating and a scandalous blight on the game.

And what is needed, as soon as possible, is a change in the FA regulations to stop it.

On Sunday at Anfield, there were two shameful attempts to con referee Andy Madley into sending off an opponent.

The first was Arsenal hardman Gabriel, collapsing, hand over his face, after minimal and accidental contact by Cody Gakpo. You can imagine there was a scream to go with it.

At my nearest Odeon screen there would have been a gallon of fake blood to make it look even more authentic.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

It’s not as if the big Brazilian hasn’t fallen dramatically a few times before.

Then, towards the end as sheer desperation took over the home team, we had Alexis Mac Allister hitting the deck quicker than a parachutist after going head-to-head with Noni Madueke.

Maybe no surprise — the Argentine also has form for it.

The intent of BOTH players was deception, pure and simple. They knew exactly what they were doing, a calculated attempt to persuade Madley or VAR Stuart Attwell to leave their opponents a man short.

Thankfully, neither were successful in their dodgy endeavours.



You didn’t need Gary Neville and Jamie Carragher to brand each of them “embarrassing”.

But when there is, as now, no comeback for trying it on, it will keep on happening. After all, why not give it a crack? It might work.

Already this season, we have witnessed Luke Shaw ensuring Rodrigo Bentancur was dismissed for Spurs at Old Trafford — no sympathy for the Uruguayan in this corner — while Liverpool’s Jeremy Jacquet equally made the most of minor, albeit very stupid, forehead contact from Brentford midfielder Yehor Yarmolyuk.



Indeed, there is an irony that the player who decided NOT to go down when he could have last season may have actually cost his side the title.

Players other than Manchester City’s Erling Haaland would have hit the deck rather than stay on their feet when Gabriel — yes, THAT Gabriel, the one who has evident balance problems — put his head in at the Etihad in April.

Had the 6ft 5in Norwegian striker been less resilient, Arsenal, rocking after surrendering a seemingly impregnable advantage, would have been without the Brazilian for the next three games.

That is not a criticism of Haaland.

But it turned out that doing the right thing became, for the impact on the battle for the crown, the wrong thing. That should never be the case.



Of course, there is a huge difference between being penalised for staying on your feet and getting away with giving gravity a helping hand.

VAR can intervene for a red card offence and referees do have the power to book players who dive to try to win a penalty or free kick.

But as it stands, there is no disciplinary comeback for those who over-egg minimal or even no contact in a bid to persuade a ref to reduce the opposition numbers.



The FA cannot overturn VAR protocols that prevent Stockley Park from urging a referee to book a player who has tried to have them on.

Wembley beaks do, though, have the power to act retrospectively in EFL and domestic, non-VAR, cup games, as they did when West Brom’s Aune Heggebo was handed a two-game ban for scoring a goal with his hand in the 2-1 win at Norwich earlier this season.

You can’t give a red card for simulation. It’s a yellow card offence.

But it’s time for the FA to intervene and hand out retrospective cards for attempted simulation.

And if that would mean a second yellow for the player, it should become a red and one-match ban.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Of course, plenty of players might still think it’s worth having a go, that the potential reward outweighs the risk.

But maybe not if they are a booking away from suspension, or have already been cautioned. It has got to be better than doing nothing.

Sports.title: Arsenal loan watch: Nwaneri Dortmund loan takes dismal turn after red card blunder as keeper has mixed day at Leicester

ARSENAL stormed three points clear at the top of the Premier League as they ended a 14-year Anfield hoodoo with a win at Anfield this weekend.

Kai Havertz’s first-half finish put the Gunners ahead, before a remarkable defensive performance ground out the result.



But Mikel Arteta’s Merseyside heroes were not the only Gunners in action this weekend.

Away from the Premier League, Arsenal loanees were getting valuable minutes under their belt.



Ethan Nwaneri, Charles Sagoe Jr, Tommy Setford and Ismeal Kabia are all currently on loan away from N5.

Here, SunSport Arsenal reporter Joshua Hall takes a look at how each loanee got on for the loan clubs last week.



ETHAN NWANERI

Nwaneri has featured in some way in every game since joining Borussia Dortmund on loan this summer.

But for their biggest game of the season so far, Der Klassiker against Bayern Munich, the 19-year-old was left on the bench.

It was a frustrating afternoon for Nwaneri, who was made to watch Dortmund’s 2-2 draw with Bayern from the sidelines.

The teenager has not started a game for Dortmund since October 17, the day he was mistakenly shown a red card before the referee retracted it against Union Berlin, and has been limited to just 42 minutes across the last four games.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

TOMMY SETFORD

Setford played his part in a big result for Stevenage in League One on Saturday as he helped The Boro earn a 2-2 draw with Leicester City.

Despite conceding twice, Setford made five saves to keep Stevenage in the game.

However, the 20-year-old will have been frustrated that it was his parried save into the box that led directly to Kamari Doyle scoring Leicester’s second.

CHARLES SAGOE JR

Sagoe Jr played 77 minutes as Kalmar FF continued their fight to stay in the Swedish top flight.



However, the 22-year-old winger was unable to help his side avoid a 1-0 defeat to GAIS, leaving Kalmar just two points off the relegation play-off spots with only four games remaining of the season.

ISMEAL KABIA

Kabia is expected to be out until after the November international break after suffering a calf tear during St Mirren’s 2-1 win over Dundee last month.

Sports.title: Spanish second tier clash abandoned with players in tears after star is knocked out by goalkeeper in 97th minute
Sports.content:
SHOCKING SCENES Spanish second tier clash abandoned with players in tears after star is knocked out by goalkeeper in 97th minute







Next

A SPANISH second-tier game was abandoned in stoppage time after a player was knocked out by the goalkeeper in a sickening collision.

Tenerife‘s Segunda Division clash with Andorra had entered the 97th minute with the score at 2-2 when a long ball was sent up the pitch.



Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel sprinted forwards to get on the end of it in a last-ditch counter attack.

But Andorra keeper Jesus Owono charged towards him near the half-way line and clattered him.



Owono was given a straight red card for the horrendous challenge, which saw him knee De Miguel in the head.

The forward initially writhed around on the turf in agony but then rolled onto his back and appeared to lose consciousness as his team-mates became distressed.



They called for urgent medical attention and some had their hands on their heads.

Several players were left in tears during the upsetting scenes before the referee opted to call off the match.

De Miguel – who is now in a stable condition – was taken to an ICU at the University Hospital of Nuestra Senora de Candelaria.

Tenerife put out a statement which read: “The #TenerifeAndorra match has been suspended due to medical reasons involving Jesus de Miguel. Our best wishes and full support.”



The club added: “CD Tenerife player Jesus de Miguel is admitted to the ICU at the University Hospital of Nuestra Señora de Candelaria, stable despite the severity of his condition.

“The medical services at said hospital will be present and will report when there are updates.”

Andorra also offered a heartfelt message following the unsettling scenes.

They wrote on X: “From FC Andorra, we want to send all our strength and best wishes to Jesús de Miguel after the serious incident suffered during today’s match.

“We hope he recovers soon. A very strong hug to the player, his family, and CD Tenerife.”



Owono’s red card was the third dismissal of the game after Tenerife’s Dani Martin and Andorra’s Lautaro de Leon were also given their marching orders just minutes earlier.

Tenerife had gone 2-0 up in the first half through Christian Gomis and Enric Gallego.

De Leon then scored penalty to pull one back – but he was bizarrely sent off after netting his spot kick having collided with Tenerife keeper Martin while picking up the ball.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And Martin was dismissed minutes later after picking up a second yellow.

Stefan Golubovic pulled Andorra level before the game was halted around 12 minutes later.

Sports.title: Edwards: Borthwick turned down my offer to work with England
Sports.content:
Renowned defence coach Shaun Edwards says England boss Steve Borthwick turned down his offer to work with the side at the 2027 Rugby World Cup in Australia.

Edwards ended a six-year spell with France - during which Les Bleus won three Six Nations, including back-to-back in 2025 and 2026 - earlier this year.

The 60-year-old worked with the England women's team on a short-term basis and has now moved onto Argentina's staff until the end of next year's World Cup, which runs across October and November.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports News' James Cole speaks with Borthwick ahead of the internationals this autumn

Speaking to the BBC's Rugby Union Weekly podcast, Edwards said: "I had a good chat with Steve [Borthwick] over the phone. I said he can make me assistant kit man and I'll be there, I'll be ready for work.

"He was very, very honest with me and I thanked him for that. He said he was happy with his staff and the way things have been going, and I respected him for that."

Edwards was Wales' defence coach from 2008-2019, helping the side to three Six Nations triumphs, while his success in club rugby union includes two Champions Cups and four domestic titles at Wasps, first as defence coach and then head coach.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Borthwick says his contract extension has not changed the focus on the 2027 World Cup

The former rugby league player has frequently been linked with the England set-up over the years but will not be joining for now at least, with Richard Wigglesworth currently in charge of defence.

Byron McGuigan, Joe El-Abd and Kevin Sinfield are other members of Borthwick's coaching staff.

England return to action in the Nations Championship on Sunday as they take on Australia at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium.

Borthwick's side go on to play Japan and New Zealand at the same venue on November 14 and November 21 respectively, before the finals weekend across November 27-29.

Sports.title: England to host South Africa live on Sky Sports in Netball World Cup prep
Sports.content:
England's Vitality Roses will host South Africa in a three-Test netball series in February, with all matches live on Sky Sports.

The games will serve as preparation for the 2027 World Cup in Australia across late August and early September.

England, currently third in the world rankings, will take on fifth-placed South Africa at Wembley Arena in London on February 6 and 7 before the series concludes at Leicester's Mattioli Arena on February 10.

The Vitality Roses edged the Proteas 58-54 in their final pool game of this summer's Commonwealth Games in Glasgow to reach the semi-finals at their opponents' expense.

South Africa had beaten England 2-1 in the sides' previous Test series in January 2026, winning the deciding match 65-50 in Johannesburg.

Before playing the Proteas early next year, England will face Jamaica home and away in the autumn.

Image: Anna Stembridge was recently appointed permanent England head coach having served as interim since Jess Thirlby's departure (Image credit: Ben Lumley)

Fran Connolly, the chief executive of England Netball said: "This international series against South Africa forms an important part of our preparations ahead of the Netball World Cup.

"We now have two opportunities to test ourselves against world-class nations, including fixtures at home and away, that will put us in the best position possible heading into the summer.

"We're looking forward to welcoming South Africa and feeling the support of a home crowd behind us."

Mami Diale, the president of Netball South Africa added: "Playing the Vitality Roses at a time like this is very important for us - this allows us to gauge our state of readiness ahead of the World Cup.

"We have faced England a few times recently and it is always a spectacle.

"Playing teams that are ranked in the top five is very important because it allows us an opportunity to measure in terms of how far we are, what we need to work on and what we are doing right."

Sports.title: Canelo could have ‘influenced’ referee, says Mbilli’s team
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez could have "influenced" the referee to take a point off Christian Mbilli during their world title fight, claims Mbilli's promoter Camille Estephan.

Canelo beat Mbilli by unanimous decision in Riyadh on Saturday to reclaim the WBC world super-middleweight title with scores of 115-112, 116-111 and 117-110 in the Mexican superstar's favour.

But in the eighth round, Mbilli's hopes of a late charge were stalled when referee Hector Afu docked a point for hitting on the back of the head after Canelo gestured to the official following an exchange on the ropes.

Image: Christian Mbilli lost out to Canelo Alvarez in their WBC super-middleweight title clash in Riyadh

"Close fight, hats off to Canelo - a great performance," Estephan said.

"As far as the ref, It seemed like he was influenced to take that point off. But I'm not in his shoes. I can't understand what went through his mind.

"Regardless, there will be many more big fights for Christian. He belongs."

Image: Terence Crawford stunned Canelo Alvarez in the Mexican's most recent fight last year

Canelo was returning to boxing a year after his stunning loss to Terence Crawford that cost him his undisputed super-middleweight crown and ended his reign as holder of the division's four major titles.

Mbilli was elevated to full WBC champion after Crawford's departure from the division, having previously held ⁠the interim title with his victory over Maciej Sulecki in June 2025.

Image: Christian Mbilli beat Maciej Sulecki in June 2025 to claim the WBC interim title

The 31-year-old Cameroon-born boxer had fought to ​a split draw against Lester Martinez on the undercard of the Alvarez-Crawford showdown, ending ​a run of 29 consecutive professional victories, while the loss now to Cancelo is his first as a professional.

In a post on Instagram, translated from French, Mbilli wrote: "Last night didn't go the way I wanted. I'll learn from this experience, get back in the gym, and come back stronger.

"Thank you to my team and to all of you for your messages of support."

Sports.title: Six England players in World Rugby's women's team of the year
Sports.content:
Six England players have been named in World Rugby's women's team of the year including prop Hannah Botterman, hooker Amy Cokayne and flanker Maddie Feaunati.

Backs Zoe Harrison (fly-half), Megan Jones (centre) and Jess Breach (wing) also make the 15 with England having more representatives in the side than any other nation.

The Red Roses stars are joined by five players from New Zealand and three from Canada with France's Lea Champon completing the team.

Image: England's Megan Jones is picked at centre

Champon's international colleague, Pauline Bourdon Sansus, won the try of the year award after a global fan vote for an effort against England in the Six Nations title decider in May.

The Red Roses, who beat France 43-28 in that crunch clash in Bordeaux in the spring, extended their winning streak to 39 matches before a 26-26 draw with Canada in Exeter in September.

England won their next match a week later, against New Zealand at Twickenham's Allianz Stadium, but then suffered back-to-back defeats against Canada prior to last weekend's thrashing of USA in New Jersey.

The Red Roses' opening game in the 2027 Women's Six Nations, a tournament they will be looking to win for a ninth time in a row, is against Wales on Saturday April 10.

Sports.title: Sherrock 'should not have been selected to play' for Beat Luke Littler show
Sports.content:
Sky Sports pundit Mark Webster says Fallon Sherrock "should not have been selected to play" for Netflix 'Beat Luke Littler' in which she claimed the winning prize of £501,000.

Sherrock overcame the double world champion in a one-off leg of 501 to claim the second biggest prize in darts history.

But this was not Sherrock's first foray into the limelight as she created history by becoming the first woman to win at the World Championship when she made the third round in December 2019, and she went on to break several other barriers in the game, including becoming the first woman to reach the quarter-finals of the Grand Slam of Darts.

The 32-year-old, who was presented to the crowd in Manchester as being a hairdresser from Milton Keyes, had made more darting history in 2023 when she became the first female to produce a televised nine-dart finish.

But her inclusion in the line-up for the TV show, attracted criticism given her stature in the game, even if she met the criteria for applicants because she does not hold a PDC Tour Card.

"The backlash Fallon got is nothing she's done wrong," Webster told Sky Sports. "Ultimately, I don't think she should have been selected to play, but then you can't blame Fallon for going to try and win half a million pounds in fair play.

"It was a good leg. But look, I don't think the backlash will bother her.

"She's got a few quid, hasn't she? So she'll just crack on. People forget about these things. She just needs to get herself ready for the rest of the year now.

"She'll be quite chilled. I'm not saying she has financial burdens, but that's going to really help going forward - doing things for her."

Was the format of the show unfair?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Irish student Pearse Mackie came agonisingly close to beating Luke Littler and claiming the £501,000 prize!

Darts prodigy Jayden Walker, 14, who has been labelled the next Littler by fans and has taken a leg off 'The Nuke' at an exhibition event, did get a shot over one leg, but lost, while WDF No 1 Mitchell Lawrie, 15, failed to get his chance despite all the pre-event hype.

Webster thinks the format of the show was unfair, saying: "I don't think she should have been able to play. I didn't like the way it was made as an amateur beats Luke Littler, and a lot of them weren't amateurs. Fallon's a professional player.

"I think Mitchell Lawrie was due to play as well, but he didn't get on. I do think they should have played out the remaining legs and then they could have chipped away at Fallon's money if they'd won. So one more win, they split Fallon's money, just for a bit of jeopardy.

"I thought it was a brilliant show. The production was fantastic.

"The concept of it was good. I just think the selection process is kind of a bit of a grey area."

Hearn: Sherrock is not a PDC Tour Card holder

Image: Barry Hearn defended the line-up

PDC chief Barry Hearn, who was involved in the audition process, defended the line-up.

Asked whether Sherrock's inclusion was unfair, he said: "No, not at all. She's not a PDC Tour Card holder. She's entitled to enter. Why should she be denied?

"She's a well-known player and she's a very good player. But Mitchell Lawrie is a very well-known player and an excellent player.

"Do you want just a series of 20 matches where someone can't even throw a dart? No, of course we want excellence competing against excellence, and that's what it was all about."

Sports.title: Stumbling block: Wirtz's and Liverpool’s costly struggles against tight defences | Andrew Beasley
Sports.content:
Liverpool failed to have a shot on target in their 1-0 defeat against Arsenal on Sunday, the first time they have drawn this type of blank in a Premier League game at Anfield since records began in 2003-04. They did not find the target in a goalless draw at the Emirates Stadium this year either, though in both games they struck the woodwork. The margins tend to be fine when recording statistical outliers.

If Alexis Mac Allister’s floated ball from 40 yards into David Raya’s waiting arms had actually counted as a shot, would Andoni Iraola’s side have delivered a markedly better attacking performance? Far more concerning for the Spaniard will be that his team had 52 touches in the Arsenal penalty area (which is good) to create only one Opta-defined big chance (which is bad). The Premier League average this season is five times more efficient; 10.3 box touches per big chance.

Credit to Arsenal for restricting the quality of Liverpool’s opportunities despite them getting repeatedly within range of their goal. Most teams have been able to do this, though. While 12 teams have had fewer touches in opposition penalty boxes than Liverpool, only Coventry with 11 have generated fewer big chances this season than Liverpool’s 12. Everton’s Thierno Barry alone has had 15, while Erling Haaland has also had more than Liverpool with 14.

Liverpool have not had this issue in Europe. They have 12 big chances in the Champions League in just three matches. As two of their opponents, Lask and Villarreal, are rated by Opta as being of lower standard than any side in the Premier League, this is little surprise. The relatively low-stakes of a given game in the league phase of the Champions League encourages those matches to be more open, too.

This has not been the case in the 2026-27 Premier League for Liverpool, who have spent more time building up against low defensive blocks than any other team. This is, in part, a problem of their own making as they have conceded first in five of their eight matches. Only against Ipswich and Brighton have they held two-goal leads, meaning opponents have rarely had compelling need to significantly loosen their defensive grip.

Iraola spoke of embracing the challenge set by deep-lying defences in his first Liverpool press conference. “I prefer to face low blocks in terms of: ‘OK, we will be in control of the game, probably we will concede less chances, we will spend a lot of time in the opposition half and those are the scenarios that we have to find,’” he said. Only four teams have had more touches in the opposition half or attempted more final third passes than Liverpool this season, but such dominance has not led to higher value chances.

This is where Florian Wirtz should be making an impression. He has the ability to unpick the tightest of backlines. Yet he has not created a big chance in the league this season. If his low total of five in his debut campaign was understandable with the problems Liverpool faced on-and-off the pitch, he trailed distantly behind Dominik Szoboszlai (14), Mohamed Salah (11) and Cody Gakpo (10). Wirtz is frequently involved in dangerous areas, as his ranking of ninth in the division for final-third passes completed will attest. His contributions have been far more geared towards ball retention and circulation rather than incision, however.

Iraola will want Liverpool to make more productive use of their high press. Most of their big chances in the league have come via corners or open play crosses. Bradley Barcola has had moments; he recovered possession to go clean through on goal at Brentford, before pouncing on an opposition mistake to assist Alexander Isak against Brighton. But Liverpool have only produced shots from 16.7% of their ball recoveries in the final 40 yards of the pitch, which is below average (18.4%) and the seventh-worst rate in the Premier League. Improvement here will help significantly.

Big chances account for 18.1% of shots in the Premier League this season but 59.5% of the goals. They are vitally important. Liverpool’s ambitions for Iraola’s first campaign will be severely limited unless they start fashioning them far more easily.

Sports.title: Andy Madley and VAR should take credit – they got major Anfield calls right | Chris Foy
Sports.content:
There was one incident that got everyone talking at the weekend, and that was the decision not to award Liverpool a penalty in their match against Arsenal after Alexander Isak had his shirt pulled by Jurriën Timber as he tried to get his head to a Bradley Barcola cross.

The on-field decision from the referee, Andy Madley, was no penalty and it was a call backed by the video assistant referee, Stuart Attwell. After the match the Liverpool manager, Andoni Iraola, said there had been a “clear, clear pull” and when footage is slowed down or freeze-framed, that looks to be true. But at full speed, the contact appears minimal and not sustained: Timber is using one hand and tugs briefly on the shirt, and the impact on Isak’s movement is arguable.

There is a high bar for penalising contact in the Premier League and that has to be taken into account by Attwell. Iraola said that he would encourage his players to go down in similar situations in future, but the incident was assessed by VAR and didn’t clear the bar in their opinion on the day. For the VAR to overturn an on-field decision there needs to have been a “clear and obvious error” and that is not the case here in my view.

Later there was a great piece of refereeing from Madley that got approval from a lot of pundits, and I agree with them. The moment came in the 79th minute after a foul by Alexis Mac Allister on Martin Ødegaard. There’s a coming together of a number of players and Noni Madueke squares up to Mac Allister. The pair’s heads touch with Mac Allister then falling to the ground as if seriously hurt.

It’s always been the case that players look to ask a question of the referee. This was how it was when I was refereeing in the Premier League and it hasn’t changed, with or without VAR. Here the question Madley had to answer was whether the contact by Madueke on Mac Allister added up to violent conduct. Clearly the answer to that was no. Madley gave a yellow card to Mac Allister but not to Madueke, who had been carded earlier and the VAR did not intervene to recommend a review given there was no evidence of a missed red card. Madley deserves all the compliments he received for the way he handled it.

This was the busiest weekend for VAR of the season, with seven overturns across the first nine games. One intervention helps to draw a contrast with what happened, or didn’t happen, at Anfield, and that’s the decision to send off Jean-Philippe Mateta after VAR upgraded a yellow card to a red.

View image in fullscreen Andy Madley booked Alexis Mac Allister but not Noni Madueke during their altercation at Anfield. Photograph: Phil Noble/Reuters

The situation followed a foul by the Crystal Palace striker early in their game against Tottenham. Mateta was trying to recover possession and tackled Micky van de Ven from behind. The Frenchman was awarded a yellow card by the referee, Michael Oliver, but when the VAR, Jarred Gillett, reviewed the footage he could see that not only was Mateta coming from behind, he was well away from the ball and made full contact with his studs on Van de Ven’s achilles. Gillett recommended that Oliver go to the monitor to review his decision and that resulted in an overturn, with Oliver sending Mateta off.

The VAR can initiate a review if they believe a “serious incident” has been missed by the referee. Here, Gillett has been able to see what Oliver couldn’t: that Mateta’s challenge was a case of serious foul play which occurs when a player endangers the safety of an opponent or uses excessive force. The contact with Van de Ven’s achilles was clearly dangerous. It clears the high bar for intervention in a way that the pull on Isak did not. It was a good piece of work by Gillett and Oliver.

Elsewhere, VAR helped to achieve the correct outcome in a number of crucial match events. An overturn in the Aston Villa v Fulham match rightly ended in Villa being awarded a penalty after the ball struck the arm of Sander Berge in an unnatural position. Chelsea were given a penalty against Manchester United after an aggressive challenge by Lisandro Martínez, who led with an arm, was initially missed on-field. Martínez was correctly handed a second yellow card, and a dismissal. At Stamford Bridge there were also two goals – one for each side – correctly overturned after they were assessed by the VAR using semi-automated offside technology.

View image in fullscreen Lisandro Martínez was penalised for leading with an arm against Wesley Fofana, conceding a penalty and being shown a second yellow card. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

Coventry conceded a penalty in their 3-1 win against Sunderland after the VAR spotted a handball by Ethan Pinnock. Leeds had a goal overturned at Bournemouth after Dominic Calvert-Lewin was found to have handled the ball on its way into the net, which has to be disallowed even if accidental under the laws of the game.

That’s a lot of activity at the Premier League’s VAR hub and the most notable thing was overall how quickly and smoothly it was dealt with by various sets of officials. Debate over the Isak decision may provide the main refereeing talking point before the next round of fixtures, but we should also take note when the system is working as it should.

Sports.title: Carrick not concerned about Martínez’s attitude as United prepare for Roma visit
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick has insisted he is not concerned about Lisandro Martínez’s attitude despite the defender’s recent outburst aimed at the Manchester United hierarchy which was then followed by his reckless sending off in the defeat against Chelsea at the weekend.

Martínez, who was fined for his comments about United’s director of football, Jason Wilcox, is expected to keep his place for the visit of Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday as United aim to end their worst run in 38 years, having failed to win any of their past nine matches.

“I’ve got no concerns about commitment at all,” Carrick said of the Argentina World Cup winner. “Things happen in football, sometimes you do things, sometimes you make a decision, sometimes you make mistakes, sometimes it goes well for you, but the commitment is not an issue.”

Away defeats against Atlético Madrid and Como have left United’s 21st in the Champions League league phase, with it felt that Carrick needs a positive result against Roma, as well as against Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday, to keep his job. Martínez is suspended for the visit of Unai Emery’s men following his red card at Stamford Bridge.

“I can’t look into the future, I don’t know what’s going to happen,” Carrick insisted. “That doesn’t change the way I feel, that’s how we’re preparing for the game tomorrow and I’m really looking forward to the game.

“You might think I’m crazy with the results we’ve had and what’s going on, but I genuinely can’t wait for the game tomorrow and that’s all I’m focused on. Whatever happens is going to happen after that, in whatever direction it goes in.”

United’s most recent home game was the 3-0 defeat against Bournemouth, which concluded with the players being booed by the Stretford End. “In these tough times you can’t expect the fans 100,000% of the time to be happy and cheering when we’re not putting out results,” Kobbie Mainoo said. “We owe it to them to put the results out there for them to cheer again.

“I feel like our way to repay that [the manager’s support] is to also be behind the manager on the pitch and off it and fight for us and fight for us as a team.”

Carrick will be without Luke Shaw, Marcus Rashford and Benjamin Sesko for the visit of Roma, while Patrick Dorgu has returned to training but is not fit enough to take part.

Sports.title: Arsenal have everything they need to repeat as Premier League champions | Jonathan Wilson
Sports.content:
Arsenal are three points clear at the top of the Premier League table. But given the team in second are Manchester City, who are likely to be facing at the very least a major points deduction, perhaps more significant is that they are five clear of Brighton in third. The season of domination that many anticipated from the champions appears to be coming to pass.

Liverpool challenged them on Sunday. There was a 20-minute spell before half-time when they swarmed all over Arsenal, and Anfield felt at least like it did in the golden years of Jürgen Klopp, when it buzzed with an energy that could overwhelm visitors. But Arsenal got through that, reset at half-time, and navigated the second half with relative comfort. For the second league game running, they denied Liverpool a shot on target.

If there is a lesson, it is that Liverpool, like Brighton, demonstrated that a very aggressive press can unsettle Arsenal. But then, a very aggressive press can unsettle anybody. In Arsenal’s loss at Brighton, Pascal Gross and Charalampos Kostoulas took difficult opportunities; at Anfield Liverpool were denied what should surely have been a penalty when Jurriën Timber tugged Alexander Isak’s shirt – another bad moment for VAR, in that the no-call essentially mandated players to go down and highlight contact. Later, Alexis Mac Allister put a free header over. That was the difference, and this Arsenal team will not give opponents many chances. They are good at closing games out. Ezri Konsa in particular was outstanding on Sunday.

They also have a strong bench. The policy has been to make the squad deeper rather than adding the very highest quality – which is why the links with Vinícius Júnior over the summer were so unexpected. That has frustrated some, but it has been successful. Arsenal on Sunday could bring on Myles Lewis-Skelly, Piero Hincapié, Viktor Gyökeres and Mikel Merino to protect their lead with very little diminution of quality. But it’s not just on a man-to-man level that Liverpool’s options suffer by comparison; their changes upset the balance. They never really had control of the game once Dominik Szoboszlai had come on for Trey Nyoni.

It’s been a recurring feature of this season that Arsenal turn half-time draws into full-time wins – it’s already happened seven times. Winning individual games, though, is only part of it; a deeper squad means there can be more rotation, which should help prevent fatigue as the season goes on, as well as providing additional cover when injuries do occur. That said, their depth was not sufficient to get them past Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup last week, although they will face few games in conditions as challenging as those on the Lancashire coast.

There are still three-quarters of the season to go, and Arsenal were in a similarly commanding position at this stage last season, four points clear of second-placed Bournemouth after nine games. The expectation then was for a procession that didn’t materialise and looked, amid a spring wobble, to have gone awry. Then as now the feeling was not merely that Arsenal were very good, but that none of their rivals looked especially threatening.

But this season they have the memory of winning the title; the insecurity of three successive second-place finishes should be lessened. There is a resilience to them that has already brought a first win at Anfield since 2012 and a victory at Nottingham Forest after successive goalless draws at the City Ground. They’re picking up points at grounds where they’ve stumbled.

Last season, City were more resilient than had been anticipated. It may be a different story this time, and not just because of the potential for a savage points deduction. After seven straight wins they have lost successive league games to Aston Villa and Brighton, but the vulnerabilities that have been exposed had been apparent earlier in the season: a high defensive line that can be exploited. Liverpool are starting to coalesce under Andoni Iraola but they haven’t clicked quite yet and are, anyway, nine points adrift. Chelsea are a point better off but still a work in progress. Brighton have probably been the best other side, but they don’t have the depth to be considered a title challenger.

Sunday made clear what was already widely suspected: Arsenal are the best team in the league by some margin. It’s not just their depth, their cohesion and the wide variety of situations from which they can score goals, it’s that they now have belief and are picking up points at places where they have often failed in the past. And if they do build up a substantial lead by Easter, that could be hugely beneficial to their European challenge, which remains the one unconquered frontier.

Sports.title: Nuno Espírito Santo under threat at West Ham after poor start to the season
Sports.content:
Nuno Espírito Santo’s future at West Ham is under threat after a disappointing start to the season. West Ham are struggling to live up to their billing as Championship favourites and dropped to eighth after losing 3-1 to West Bromwich Albion on Saturday.

West Ham are intent on an instant return to the Premier League after Nuno failed to save them from relegation last season, but the setback against West Brom put another dent in their promotion push. West Ham occupy the final playoff spot after consecutive defeats at home and are four points below second placed Swansea. Nuno is expected to be given time to turn the situation around but key figures have become increasingly impatient. The manager faced unrest from supporters during the West Brom game.

The initial expectation was that Nuno would be fired after taking West Ham down last season. Sources indicated that David Sullivan, the club’s largest shareholder at the time, wanted to part company with the former Nottingham Forest manager. Daniel Kretinsky, the Czech billionaire, was in Nuno’s corner and is understood to have argued for continuity.

Sullivan then resigned as a joint-chair and director of West Ham to fight what he described as “false allegations” concerning his personal conduct. Kretinsky became West Ham’s biggest shareholder in September, buying a stake of 46%. The agreement saw Sullivan, who is not on the board, increase his stake from 38% to 40%.

Any decision on Nuno’s future will be a collective board decision. Karim Virani, the interim CEO, and Nils Koppen, the director of recruitment, will have their say. West Ham, who visit Cardiff City on Wednesday, are unhappy after a run of two wins in six games and Nuno is likely to face difficult questions if he cannot inspire an improvement before this month’s international break.

View image in fullscreen Dejected West Ham fans depart early from the London Stadium during their team’s defeat to West Brom at the weekend. Photograph: Martin Dalton/Shutterstock

West Ham turned to Nuno after firing Graham Potter in September 2025. The 52-year-old’s tactics and signings did not convince last season and the problems have continued since relegation. West Ham sold Crysencio Summerville and Mateus Fernandes after going down but they held on to Jarrod Bowen and Tomas Soucek. They broke the EFL transfer record when they signed Arne Engels from Celtic for £22m.

The feeling within West Ham is that they have the best squad in the Championship and should be playing better. But Nuno has struggled to settle on his best 11 and various problems have emerged. West Ham have kept three clean sheets in 13 games. They have started games slowly, conceding the first goal on six occasions.

Their strikers – Joel Piroe, Pablo Felipe and Taty Castellanos – all joined under Nuno and have five league goals between them this season. Bowen is the top scorer with seven but West Ham lack a clear playing identity and have not found the right balance in midfield. The squad contains two holding midfielders but Soungoutou Magassa and Edson Alvarez are both out of favour.

West Ham still hope that Nuno can lead a push up the table. There have been some positive signs, including 6-0 wins over Wrexham and Lincoln, although the latter were reduced to nine men in the first half. West Ham’s best performance of the season was their gritty 1-0 win away to Swansea, suggesting they are better when there is less pressure on them to dominate games.

Sports.title: WSL talking points: Kang could have a problem and how long can Slegers hang on?
Sports.content:
Lionesses may present Uefa with problem

London City Lionesses may have lost 2-1 to champions Manchester City, but their performances and league position have shown their European aspirations are far from unrealistic. Aided by Arsenal’s poor start, London City are third in the WSL table and were frustrated to end the day with a six-point gap to the top two after dominating in Bromley. “It’s doubly frustrating, because I think the result was not the one we deserve,” said their coach, Eder Maestre. “Manchester City are more mature. They are more used to it. When you have this consistency and you are very used to playing these kinds of games, maybe you have more experience.” Maestre’s team have a three-point lead over fourth-placed Tottenham and if they continue their upwards trajectory and qualify for the Champions League, Uefa will be forced to tackle the possible scenario of two Michelle Kang-owned clubs, London City and OL Lyonnes, qualifying sooner than they perhaps anticipated. Suzanne Wrack

Gunners’ groundhog day

It was groundhog day for Arsenal against Aston Villa with the Gunners going a goal down for the fifth time this season. “We just said it feels like we’re playing the same game over and over again,” said the manager, Renée Slegers. “We go one goal down from a break and we don’t start with enough urgency.” The issue for Arsenal is that opposition teams can sense this lack of urgency. Get one chance early on, take it and then capitalise on the fact that Slegers’ side just cannot break down a low block. How Slegers, her staff and the squad arrest this malaise is the big unanswered question. The wins against Tottenham and Benfica felt like the seeds of a turnaround in fortunes, but they papered over cracks that will be exposed again until they make more of their dominance in the final third. SW

View image in fullscreen Arsenal’s struggles continue at both ends of the pitch. Photograph: Jody Demay-Davies/SPP/Shutterstock

James injury ruins Chelsea’s perfect day

There is significant concern over Lauren James’s fitness after she suffered another injury against Charlton. The 25-year-old was forced off the pitch after pulling up off the ball in the 35th minute. “It is difficult to say,” the Chelsea manager, Sonia Bompastor, said. “I can only say it’s her hamstring and we’ll assess her later to have more detailed information.” It is the latest fitness worry for the England international who, after being limited to just 11 and six league starts in the last two campaigns respectively, had started this season in superb form with four goals in the WSL. It was the only blemish on an otherwise enjoyable afternoon for the league leaders who ran out 6-0 winners at the Valley. Defender Nathalie Björn marked her first start after months on the sidelines with the opener. Substitute Aggie Beever-Jones ended her barren spell, scoring her first league goal since September 2025. There was also an emotional moment for the young Italian midfielder Giulia Dragoni who opened her Chelsea account after coming off the bench. Sophie Downey

Spence makes history in Spurs victory

As she led Tottenham out at St Andrew’s, Drew Spence wrote herself into the history books. Her start against Birmingham marked her 217th in the WSL, making her the competition’s new all-time record appearance maker. It is the latest accolade of a decorated career that has seen her win five league titles, four FA Cups and two League Cups. The 34-year-old Jamaica international featured in the inaugural WSL season back in 2011 with Chelsea where she spent 14 years before switching to Spurs in 2022. She was once again at the heart of Martin Ho’s midfield as Tottenham ended their three-game losing streak with a dominant 4-1 win over Birmingham. Spurs were back to their attacking best, registering 11 of their 29 shots on target, recording 61 touches in the opposition box and having four different goalscorers. The victory moves them up to fourth in the table. SD

Asseyi shines in Liverpool thrashing

Viviane Asseyi put on a performance Zinedine Zidane would be proud of as West Ham stormed to a dominant 4-1 victory against Liverpool. The 32-year-old scored twice for the Hammers on Sunday, the second goal a brilliant free-kick from the edge of the box which flew into the top-right corner. Asseyi told the Guardian recently that she grew up wanting to be like the former France international – and that excellent strike was Zidane-esque. Her double in east London took the forward up to five goals for the season, moving her to joint fifth in the Golden Boot race. “She missed a hat-trick unfortunately but I’m very happy,” the West Ham head coach, Rita Guarino, said. “She’s an incredible player. Very happy for her, very happy in the way the team help her to make this kind of performance.” Emillia Hawkins

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Everton and Manchester United need flair in window

Is creativity a problem for both of these sides? On Saturday’s evidence, yes. Both sides looked well-drilled from a defensive standpoint but this was about as textbook a 0-0 as you could imagine, with both sides registering an expected goals (xG) of under 0.5 and – according to the WSL’s official website – neither of them having any “big chances” in the game. Everton are now the joint-second lowest goalscorers in the division – only bottom-placed Charlton have scored fewer – and Manchester United are only two goals better off themselves. The leaders Chelsea have netted three times as many league goals as Manchester United’s nine already. Perhaps both of these clubs ought to be targeting inventive players with ingenuity and flair in January, to offer them a bit more unpredictability going forward. Tom Garry

View image in fullscreen Andrea Medina is challenged by Hannah Blundell in a low-quality encounter on Merseyside. Photograph: Ben Roberts Photo/Getty Images

Brighton make it three in a row at home

The Brighton head coach, Arturo Ruiz, praised the team’s togetherness after they came from behind to beat Crystal Palace 2-1. “It’s a team win. All the players deserve today,” he said. “I don’t think that there’s one player that was much better than the others, and that’s the best thing that a team can have.” The victory moves Brighton up to sixth and they now have three straight home wins for the first time since September 2021. “As I always say, we play for the fans, we play for our people, and the three points are for them because they always support us in the best way,” Ruiz added. Palace lost but it would be remiss not to mention Annabel Blanchard’s goal for the visitors, a superbly taken long-range effort in the 34th minute. Marcus Christenson

Sports.title: Aston Villa drop threat of legal action against Jamie Carragher after apology
Sports.content:
Aston Villa have dropped their threat of legal action against Jamie Carragher following an apology from the Sky Sports pundit.

Villa announced on Friday that they would be taking legal action against Carragher for “unacceptable insults about the club and its fans” on the Stick to Football podcast. The former Liverpool defender had told Villa supporters to “shut the fuck up” after being criticised for suggesting Unai Emery should consider taking the Manchester United job if Michael Carrick is sacked.

Carragher apologised on social media on Saturday, posting on X: “I’d like to apologise to Aston Villa, the owners and their fans. My language this week was clumsy and wrong. I can assure Villa fans it was tongue-in-cheek but I can understand it’s not come across that way, so apologies. Good luck today UTV [Up the Villa]!”
