Villa, who face Barcelona in the Champions League on Tuesday, have confirmed they will not be proceeding with the legal threat against the 48-year-old.

Sports.title: Spanish clash abandoned as footballer is rushed to hospital after being knocked out by sickening goalkeeper tackle - leaving team-mates in tears amid worrying scenes
Sports.content:
Spanish clash abandoned as footballer is rushed to hospital after being knocked out by sickening goalkeeper tackle - leaving team-mates in tears amid worrying scenes

Tenerife striker Jesus de ​Miguel has been admitted to intensive care after collapsing during a Spanish second division clash with Andorra on Monday.

The 30-year-old is in stable condition, the club has confirmed, after a horrifying collision with goalkeeper ‌Jesus Owono led to the fixture being abandoned deep into stoppage time with the scores level at 2-2.

A club statement read: 'CD Tenerife player Jesús de Miguel is admitted to the ICU at the University Hospital of Nuestra Señora de Candelaria, stable despite the severity of his condition.

'The medical services at said hospital will be present and will report when there are updates.'

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

It has also been reported that while the Spaniard is stable, he remains unconscious.

Tenerife's Jesus de ​Miguel was wiped out by Jesus Owono during a Spanish second tier match

De Miguel was rushed to the ICU following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch

The game had entered the seventh minute of stoppage time when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker appeared to be struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

The stadium has been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

Andorra also released a statement, which read: 'We want to send all our strength and best wishes to Jesus de Miguel after the serious incident suffered during today's match.

'We hope he recovers soon. A very strong hug to the player, his family and Tenerife.'

Despite remaining unconcsious in intensive care the player is believed to be 'breathing on his own'.

Sports.title: Remembrance silence at Arsenal interrupted as North London Forever anthem mistakenly plays ahead of WSL match
Sports.content:
Remembrance silence at Arsenal interrupted as North London Forever anthem mistakenly plays ahead of WSL match

Arsenal stars and fans were caught by surprise after the club's North London Forever anthem was mistakenly played moments into Remembrance silence before their Women's Super League match with Aston Villa.

Arsenal and Aston Villa had joined the WSL sides paying tribute to the Armed Forces community, past and present, with the fixture having been the Gunners' last women's match at the Emirates before Remembrance Day on November 11.

Players from both sides had gathered by the centre circle, with the stadium announcer then heard requesting fans join in with 'a moment of silence as a mark of respect'.

The silence, however, was unfortunately interrupted when their pre-match anthem The Angel – more commonly known as North London Forever – began playing around the stadium.

Arsenal players, who had bowed their heads for the minute's silence, could be seen quizzically looking at their team-mates as the anthem played.

Players eventually broke away from the centre circle as the anthem continued to play.

Arsenal players lined up for a Remembrance silence, but were visibly surprised when the club's North London Forever anthem played shortly after it began. Source: TikTok - Jodie-woso

Fans commented that they were left confused by the unfortunate interruption to the silence

Shirts from the match, featuring the poppy, are being auctioned in aid of the Royal British Legion

We will remember them. pic.twitter.com/okgfWrEDkQ — Arsenal Women (@ArsenalWFC) November 1, 2026

The unfortunate moment also caught out fans both in the stadium and watching on television.

'Very disappointed with the apparent mixup with playing north London forever during moment of remembrance, if it was indeed a mistake. All got a bit confusing. Crowd certainly looked confused anyway,' one fan commented.

'Well I’m not convinced North London Forever was supposed to start playing then but okay,' another posted.

'I was watching on tv and I was incredibly confused when NLF started playing, and too make matters worse people were actually singing along,' a third said.

'I was also confused looking around I didn’t know if to sing so I didn’t,' added another.

'As bad as it was, as mentioned it wasn’t going to be a full minutes silence. Also NLF is pre-programmed to play a minute before kick off. Awkward more than anything,' another fan said.

The Gunners shared an image of their players lining up for the tribute on social media, writing 'We will remember them.'

Daily Mail Sport understands Arsenal welcomed members of Islington Veterans Community to Emirates Stadium on Sunday as part of their moment of remembrance.

Arsenal are set to have a full Remembrance commemoration this weekend when their men's team face Hull City on Saturday. The women’s side will also observe a full commemoration at Anfield when they face Liverpool on Sunday.

Arsenal are also among the clubs to have been supporting the Royal British Legion's Poppy Appeal, which has seen poppies woven into their match shirts.

Match shirts are being auctioned on the MatchWornShirt website and app, with net proceeds going directly to the Royal British Legion to support their work with military service members, veterans and their families.

Shirts from Arsenal's WSL fixture against Aston Villa and their Premier League tie at Anfield, which also took place on Sunday, are among the items on auction.

Sports.title: 'We owe it to Michael Carrick': Kobbie Mainoo lays down the gauntlet for his Man United team-mates - and claims they are just ONE win away from transforming their season
Sports.content:
'We owe it to Michael Carrick': Kobbie Mainoo lays down the gauntlet for his Man United team-mates - and claims they are just ONE win away from transforming their season

Kobbie Mainoo says Manchester United’s stars owe it to head coach Michael Carrick and the fans to turn their season around – and believe it might only take one win.

United go into Tuesday’s Champions League tie against Roma at Old Trafford without a victory in nine games and hovering one place above the Premier League relegation zone.

It has left Carrick fighting for his job and led to fans turning on the players after the last home game against Bournemouth which ended with a 3-0 defeat.

Carrick has done his best to shield the squad from criticism, and Mainoo said: ‘I feel like our way to repay that is to also be behind the manager on the pitch and off it, and fight for us as a team.

‘In these tough times you can't expect the fans 100,000 per cent of the time to be happy and cheering when we're not putting out results, you know. We owe it to them to put the results out there for them to cheer again.

‘Of course, it's been a tough season. We've not had the results we've wanted, but you know we need to look forward now. There are big, big games ahead and I feel like we're one win away from changing that.

Kobbie Mainoo says Manchester United’s stars owe it to Michael Carrick and the fans to turn their season around

‘I've been at this club for a long time and I know there's always going to be ups and downs. It's never going to be plain sailing and smooth to the top. So you expect bumps and the best thing about them is you're able to bounce back from them.’

Mainoo signed a new five-year contract in April after re-establishing himself at his boyhood club under Carrick, having asked to leave under the previous head coach Ruben Amorim.

Despite the club’s fortunes taking a nosedive this season, the 21-year-old is determined to help restore the standards that made United great.

‘I'm very grateful to the boss for putting the trust in me as soon as he came in, putting that belief in me and giving me all the advice that he has,’ added Mainoo, who returned to action at Chelsea on Saturday after missing five games.

‘Knowing he's a player who's been at this club and knows the history of this club and knows what it takes to win, I take those words to heart and I try and apply them every day in training and in games.

‘United's a huge club, so I think a lot of people know the values that this club holds and that have been passed down through the people who've worked and played here. I feel like I take some responsibility in that and in spreading the word of what is Manchester United, coming up through the academy. I plan to send that message for hopefully as long as I can.

‘I've tried to take on more responsibility in the team. I want to impose myself more in games and they've definitely helped to do that, giving me more responsibility with taking the ball. There have been ups and downs, but I have to have belief in myself even in these tough times.

‘I feel like in every period of my career so far, I've tried to take positives from them. Even, you know, times that I'm not playing I've learned things and I'm still applying them to this day.’

Sports.title: Kevin Keegan's iconic Hamburg shirt from 1977 Super Cup against Liverpool sells for £84,500 at auction
Sports.content:
Kevin Keegan's iconic Hamburg shirt from 1977 Super Cup against Liverpool sells for £84,500 at auction

Kevin Keegan's iconic 1977 European Super Cup shirt has been sold at auction for a jaw-dropping £84,500.

The 1977 European Super Cup was contested between Liverpool, Keegan's former side, and his new club Hamburg. Despite drawing 1-1 in the first leg, Hamburg lost 6-0 in Keegan's first return to Anfield since his signing.

The much-loved legend's No7 shirt formed part of his former Liverpool team-mate Emlyn Hughes' collection. Hughes, who died in 2004, got it in a swap, and it was estimated at around £2,000 to £3,000 by BUDDS auctioneers.

The sky-blue and white adidas shirt features a v-neck style collar and embroidered badge.

The sale comes just months after the football world was plunged into mourning over the death of Keegan, who was regarded as one of the greatest players of his generation.

Keegan began his playing career at Scunthorpe United in 1968, before Bill Shankly signed him for Liverpool. There, he won seven major trophies including three league titles and one European Cup during a six-year spell.

The 1977 European Super Cup was contested between Liverpool, Keegan's former side, and his new club Hamburg

The much-loved legend's No7 shirt formed part of his former Liverpool team-mate Emlyn Hughes' collection

Ever ambitious, Keegan signed for Hamburg in 1977, and it was during his three-year spell in Germany that the 5ft 7in Englishman earned the nickname the 'Mighty Mouse', winning the league title in 1979 and reaching the 1980 European Cup final, where his side were beaten by Nottingham Forest.

It was also at Hamburg that he confirmed his world-class credentials, winning the Ballon d'Or in 1978 and 1979.

The following year he surprisingly joined Southampton before finishing his playing career with Newcastle, where his love affair with the Geordie fans was born during their 1984 promotion-winning campaign.

Keegan made 63 England appearances and captained his country over 30 times, although his only World Cup was an injury-scarred appearance in 1982.

In 1992, Keegan made his first step into management at his former club Newcastle, guiding them into the Premier League and to within touching distance of the 1995-96 title only to miss out to Manchester United.

After leaving St James' Park in January 1997, a brief stint at Fulham followed before he became England manager in 1999, having initially taken on the job following Glenn Hoddle's departure.

Having overseen a disappointing Euro 2000 campaign, Keegan resigned on the back of defeat by Germany at Wembley Stadium, the last match at the national stadium before it was rebuilt.

After his death, an extraordinary sea of flowers surrounded St James' Park to pay tribute to 'The Messiah' who led their charge back into the top-flight in 1984

After England, he managed Manchester City for four years before returning for a brief spell at Newcastle.

Following his death, an extraordinary sea of flowers surrounded St James' Park to pay tribute to 'The Messiah'.

The club wrote a moving statement at the time, which read: 'We are devastated to learn of the passing of Kevin Keegan, one of the most iconic, influential and deeply loved figures in our club's history.

'Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.'

Sports.title: JEFF POWELL MBE: I witnessed the unstoppable rot that caused Man United's last relegation - now the ghosts are resurfacing in alarmingly similar fashion for Michael Carrick and his rag-bag of players
Sports.content:
JEFF POWELL MBE: I witnessed the unstoppable rot that caused Man United's last relegation - now the ghosts are resurfacing in alarmingly similar fashion for Michael Carrick and his rag-bag of players

What more spooky time of the year for a fog of deja vu to be hanging over the haunted house of Old Trafford.

The ghosts of Halloween half a century past have materialised to foretell the doom of relegation.

The omens of 1974 are rewritten in the statistics cursing the current Manchester United team. No win in the first seven away games. A manager without a victory in nine consecutive matches. Perhaps coming up next, a run of only four wins in 20 league matches to match that of the relegation season 52 years ago.

And so to Gloomy Tuesday. If United fail to defeat Roma in the Champions League, they will equal their worst sequence of results in 75 years. The ominous portent for this one is much more recent. If they could lose 4-1 to lowly Como the other week, what chance of beating a major Italian club, unbeaten so far this season in Serie A? With this rag-bag of players, not much.

United’s class of ’74 included England’s Alex Stepney, David Sadler and Brian Kidd, Scotland stars Martin Buchan, George Graham, Lou Macari, Jim McCalliog and Willie Morgan. Graham recalls: ‘The club was going through a difficult time but we did our best.’

Of the team which self-destructed in defeat at Chelsea this Saturday, that could only be truly said of one man. Harry Maguire has survived more criticism than he ever deserved and once again he was alone in looking like he objected to losing.

Denis Law (second right), then of Manchester City, condemns his old club United to relegation in 1974

Following the 2-0 loss at Chelsea on Saturday, if United fail to defeat Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday they will equal their worst sequence of results in 75 years

One of his team-mates, the typically disgraceful Argentine Lisandro Martinez, made sure of defeat by getting himself sent off. Whether that act was deliberate only he can tell us but he looked as anxious to depart this great though ailing club as he had sounded when he criticised its executives after the Como loss.

As did the so-called captain. I voted for Bruno Fernandes as the Footballer of Last Year. Never again. By adding his voice to that of Martinez, he cheapened this great club in its hour of need. That he tried to recant relegates him to the same league of hypocritical back-trackers as Andy Burnham.

The damage to an already badly wounded Michael Carrick has been done. It became irreparable when he agreed to make the peace.

Sir Alex Ferguson would never have forgiven such a breach of trust. But then we are comparing pears with apples here. Fergie is a genius. Carrick simply an honest man out of his depth.

The unfavourable comparisons with the relegation of yesteryear don’t end there. Fernandes is a talented footballer but the idol of ‘74 was another genius.

George Best electrified not only Old Trafford but the world of football and beyond. Champions League glory, two English league titles, Wembley Cup finals, heroic if inevitably hopeless World Cup brilliance with Northern Ireland and a Ballon d’Or would have only been for starters had he not succumbed to his lust for booze and blondes which not only terminated his career but shortened his star-spangled but ultimately tragic life.

Bruno may become remembered as a footnote to Eusebio and Ronaldo in Portugal’s hall of fame. Besty will shine forever in the pantheon of football’s all-time greats.

Best knew when it was the right, self-destructed time to leave. Having torn himself away from Old Trafford in the summer of ’73 he allowed himself to be talked back by the retired Busby.

George Best (left) knew when it was the right time to leave. Having torn himself away from Old Trafford in 1973 he allowed himself to be talked back by the retired Matt Busby (right)

The damage to an already badly wounded Michael Carrick has been done. It became irreparable when he agreed to make peace with the players who spoke out against the club

After a dozen games he accepted that his best would no longer be electrifying enough to spark salvation and after an away defeat on New Year’s Day he said his last goodbye.

As sharp between the ears, surprisingly to some, as he was undeniably mesmerising on the pitch, he left behind words of wisdom gleaned from watching as boy and man as United fell into the turmoil of finding a manager to succeed Sir Matt.

They are as relevant in this time of crisis as they were those 52 years ago: ‘The fear of relegation starts in the boardroom, comes down to the managers and through to the players. The fans sense it.’

The faithful are, indeed, well aware of the origin of the rot besetting the Reds today. They detest the Glazers who brought their American opportunism and apparent greed to Manchester and have plunged the club into billions of debt. They are disenchanted already with Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Not least because this penny-pinching Englishman’s cost-cutting has broken the hearts of so many loyal servants by sacking them from jobs they loved as much as they do their team. No matter how badly it is playing just now. And, by the way, he can stick his big-top circus stadium in the proverbial orifice.

Manchester United, like Liverpool, belong to the people. Not some damn Yankees and an English fat cat.

Unless this one reclaims its heart, soul, very reason for existing – and damn quickly – the ruin may take decades to rebuild. If ever.

United were heading this way when they were running mindlessly through managers in the 70s and 80s – Dave Sexton was sacked after finishing second in the league for heaven’s sake – until they got lucky as Sir Matt came briefly out of retirement to find his own successor in Sir Alex.

Manchester United, like Liverpool, belong to the people. Not some damn Yankees and an English fat cat in Jim Ratcliffe (centre)

Alex Ferguson (centre, flanked by director Mike Edelson and chairman Martin Edwards) at his unveiling as United boss in 1986, thanks to the help of Busby

The next Greatest Of All Time may never be out there. Carrick accepts it’s not him but the sympathies of the Red Army for a good man doing his darndest for a club he loves as much as they do may keep him going long enough for the increasingly fearful men in the boardroom to make a proper, lasting appointment rather than yet another shot in the dark.

For this they need to take sensible advice from more experienced football men. Just as they must set aside their misguided belief that they know something about the game itself and let seasoned judges guide them towards the really, really best players in which to invest their millions.

Rather than the rabble among the present first team of whose names neither they, nor more importantly the Stretford End, had ever heard until they ambled into Old Trafford.

As the money men should know, if you buy cheap you end up having to buy again. If they don’t, they should follow senors Martinez and Fernandes out of the building.

Sports.title: Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy's TMRW Sports teams up with the NFL to launch brand new sports league
Sports.content:
The creative minds behind the popular simulator golf league TGL have launched a new flag football league in collaboration with the NFL.

TMRW Sports, the venture started by golf icons Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy – as well as former NBC Sports executive Mike McCarley, has officially revealed the name for their new league: Premier Flag Football (PFF).

According to ESPN's Adam Schefter, the league is set for a launch in the summer of 2027 – exactly one year before flag football is played as an event at the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles.

While the NFL announced the adoption of the league months ago, the name and logo for the PFF was revealed on Monday. The league's identity reveal added that there will be divisions for both men and women.

In addition, the league says stadium developer Populous is designing their 'inaugural stadium, which will be the first purpose-built stadium for flag football.'

'Flag football is exploding in popularity, and Premier Flag is establishing itself as the destination for the world’s top women and men competing at the highest level of the sport,' read a statement from Brendan Donohue, TMRW Sports' president of flag football.

Flag football has entered the professional level.



Introducing Premier Flag. The world’s best women and men coming together for a historic partnership with the @NFL.



See you in 2027 🏈 pic.twitter.com/Mu9OihJCRi — Premier Flag Football (@PremierFlag) November 2, 2026

The NFL and TMRW Sports have officially unveiled the identity of their flag football league

Premier Flag Football will host men's and women's pro competitions starting in 2027

TMRW, the venture started by Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods, won the rights in February

'The Premier Flag brand represents where flag football is headed -- elite, global and accessible -- while setting a professional standard for the sport’s growing ecosystem.

'When we launch next summer, fans will have the opportunity to see these amazing athletes perform at their best, supported by Premier Flag’s world-class training, strength and conditioning, nutrition and coaching programs.'

The NFL's Senior Vice President of Global Flag Football, Brian Flinn, also said: 'Premier Flag represents an exciting step forward in the continued evolution of flag football.

'Together with TMRW Sports, we're building a global platform to showcase the world's top flag football players and to engage fans in a premium experience.'

Flinn added that the league's first event will be a Premier Flag Showcase to be held in Los Angeles during Super Bowl LXI.

The league announced the venture this past February, revealing TMRW Sports as their partner after a competitive bid process featuring 'roughly a dozen other groups,' according to Sportico.

Flag football has grown in popularity in recent years. Not only have parents of boys and young men turned to the variant of the game for its lowered risk of injury, but girls and young women have picked up the sport as well.

Data from the Sports & Fitness Industry Association revealed participation in flag football grew 15 percent from 2019 to 2024.

Sports.title: Ex-Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United star Sebastien Bassong is fined for dodging £7 Tube fare by using someone else's travelcard
Sports.content:
Ex-Tottenham Hotspur and Newcastle United star Sebastien Bassong is fined for dodging £7 Tube fare by using someone else's travelcard

Former Tottenham Hotspur defender Sebastien Bassong has been fined for dodging a £7 Tube fare, after he was caught using someone else's train driver pass illegally.

The Frenchman, 40, who spent several seasons in the Premier League with Spurs, Newcastle and Norwich, was stopped by a Transport for London (TfL) officer after he was spotted tailgating a friend through the barriers at St Paul's station in May.

The ex-footballer was carrying the Oystercard of the friend's ex-girlfriend, which had been issued to her as a driver on the Docklands Light Railway (DLR), court documents showed.

The TfL officer was then told that Bassong, who was an £8 million signing for Spurs in 2009, had been using her travelcard because he was 'experiencing financial and personal hardship due to a divorce and unemployment'.

Bassong was convicted of using the rail network without a valid ticket at Wimbledon Magistrates Court on October 30.

Magistrate Graham Burbage fined him £220, ordered him to pay the £7 fare for his journey from Arnos Grove to St Paul's, and directed him to pay £250 in prosecution costs and an £88 victim surcharge.

Bassong did not enter a plea to the charge, and was convicted behind closed doors in a Single Justice Procedure hearing.

Adebukola Anifowose, a revenue control officer for TfL, told the court in a statement she spotted Bassong at 1.08pm 'pretend to tap an Oystercard enclosed in a white wallet before tailgating through the wide-aisle gate behind another male'.

Bassong in action during a Premier League match between Chelsea and Tottenham at Stamford Bridge

Bassong attended the 2026 PFA Awards at the Manchester Opera House

Sebastien Bassong playing for Spurs during the UEFA Champions League match between BSC Young Boys and Tottenham Hotspur

She said Bassong offered up a TfL staff nominee pass when challenged, which allows free travel on London transport.

'System checks later confirmed that the pass did not belong to him and had last been used in October 2025,' she said.

'The accompanying male was spoken to – this individual later informed me that he was assisting Mr Bassong, who was experiencing financial and personal hardship due to a divorce and unemployment, by providing him with the nominee pass.

'It was subsequently established that the pass was registered to an ex-girlfriend of this male, who reportedly claimed to be a DLR driver.'

A notice about the prosecution was sent to Bassong's north London home, and he did not respond before the court hearing.

Bassong, who now runs a motivational coaching business, has been given 28 days to settle the court bill totalling £565.

Sports.title: This is the England starting XV Steve Borthwick should pick to beat Australia - all the key selection battles from flying full-backs to race for No10, and what to do with Henry Pollock
Sports.content:
Steve Borthwick yesterday named a 36-man squad for England’s crunch Nations Championship opener with Australia on Sunday at Twickenham.

It was one without injured scrum-halves Alex Mitchell and Archie McParland but it did include first-choice No10 Fin Smith, despite the Northampton man's calf worry.

England are preparing for four crucial matches this month which will start the countdown for next year’s World Cup, with a raft of selection battles across the starting lineup.

Here, Daily Mail Sport’s ALEX BYWATER assesses how Borthwick’s party is shaping up for the Wallabies on Sunday - and picks his starters to take down the Wallabies.

Steve Borthwick as named his 36-man squad for the autumn slate of the Nations Championship

Front row

Promising 21-year-old hooker Kepu Tuipulotu suffered a leg injury in England training last week and has been replaced by Saracens' Theo Dan.

England’s front row has significant experience otherwise and pretty much picks itself - Jamie George is the likely starting hooker with Ellis Genge and Joe Heyes propping up the scrum either side of him.

Luke Cowan-Dickie and the fit-again prop pair Fin Baxter and Will Stuart provide strong options from the bench.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Ellis Genge, Jamie George, Joe Heyes

Second row

After missing the summer as part of a scheduled rest period, Maro Itoje is back in the England squad and is close to certain to start at lock against Australia as captain.

Even though his club side Saracens have struggled so far this season, Itoje demands inclusion. The question is who partners him.

Ollie Chessum, fresh from signing a new Leicester deal, has been in regal form and is now one of England’s best and most important players. But despite him playing lock at club level, it seems Borthwick wants him to provide extra physicality and another lineout jumping option in the No 6 jersey, where he starred in the Stade de France in March.

That leaves a space for either Alex Coles or George Martin. Martin’s grunt is invaluable, but Northampton's Coles has shown more so far this term.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Maro Itoje (captain), Alex Coles

Second-rowers Ollie Chessum, Alex Coles and Maro Itoje have been in fine form, and Chessum's versatility means he should slide over to No6

Back row

England have a wealth of resources in this area but also questions to answer.

Chessum excelled on the blindside flank in the Six Nations finale with France. But in their recent struggles, England have struggled to get their breakdown firing.

Borthwick has pointed out the difference between the way the ruck is refereed at PREM level and internationally and that his team has to adapt better. Issues there have led to England conceding too many penalties and subsequently, yellow cards.

Australia are dangerous but inconsistent. They do, however, play with pace and are battle-hardened from a busy summer schedule, which included beating a weakened South Africa side. England, by contrast, only arrived at their Pennyhill Park base on Monday night and haven’t played since July.

‘Facing Australia is an exciting challenge,' said Borthwick. 'They have played a significant amount of Test rugby in recent months. We know the quality and experience they will bring,’ Borthwick admitted.

To slow down the Wallabies, Borthwick’s most sensible bet is to go with the experience of Tom Curry in the No7 jersey, alongside Chessum and Ben Earl who is an automatic pick at No8. That can leave Henry Pollock to bring his athleticism and dynamism from the bench in a battle with a team he scored against this time last year.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Ollie Chessum, Tom Curry, Ben Earl

Half-backs

This is where England’s problems begin. Mitchell and McParland were two of England’s three scrum-halves in training last week, alongside Jack van Poortvliet.

Mitchell is awaiting the results of a scan on a hamstring injury suffered in club action for Northampton against Gloucester, but won't face Australia as he wasn’t named in Borthwick’s squad for the game. Neither was McParland who suffered a calf problem in England camp last week.

Leicester's Jack van Poortvliet and Northampton's Fin Smith (both centre) got to grips in their recent PREM clash - now they need to put England on their back and lead them to victory

That leaves Leicester's Van Poortvliet as the man to start, with one of Ben Spencer or Harry Randall – who have both had late call-ups – in reserve.

There is also a lack of clarity at No10. England are hopeful Smith will recover from a calf injury of his own to start against Australia. Marcus Smith and George Ford are the other options. Fin Smith has to start if fit. But if not, namesake Marcus is in better form than Ford and would deserve a chance.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Jack van Poortvliet, Fin Smith

Centres

This has been England’s big problem for a long time now. Seb Atkinson is the man in pole position at inside centre and played well for Gloucester at Northampton at the weekend, proving he is over his knee issue.

Who starts in the No 13 shirt is a bigger question. After missing the 2023 World Cup, Henry Slade is now back in favour.

One of Will Joseph or Joe Marchant would be bolder picks and the former, who has just one cap, has been a form horse in the PREM. But Borthwick places a great deal of emphasis on cohesion. Slade is the right call for this game.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Seb Atkinson, Henry Slade

Borthwick places a great deal of emphasis on cohesion and the returning Henry Slade is the right call for this game

Back three

Immanuel Feyi-Waboso has shown defensive frailties for Exeter, but his game-breaking ability means he has to start on the wing after he played club rugby last week following a hamstring worry.

Borthwick has dallied with Tommy Freeman at outside centre, but he has to start on the other wing to Feyi-Waboso. It's not rocket science - pick your best players in their best positions.

Full-back is a straight shootout between George Furbank and Freddie Steward. Furbank has had rotten luck at Test level, summed up by the appendicitis that forced him to miss South Africa in July. His ball-playing ability makes him perfect to help what has been a stuttering England attack.

But Freddie Steward is pushing him hard, after revitalising his game at Borthwick’s request. Whichever Smith starts at fly-half, Furbank knows both well as team-mates past and present, so that’s an extra tick in his box.

Daily Mail Sport’s starters: Immanuel Feyi-Waboso, Tommy Freeman, George Furbank

George Furbank is in a tight race for the No15 shirt with Freddie Steward but his partnerships with Fin and Marcus Smith may just settle the matter

Sports.title: Ex-Premier League boss Pepe Mel in intensive care after suffering stroke
Sports.content:
Ex-Premier League boss Pepe Mel in intensive care after suffering stroke

Pepe Mel had a brief stint as manager of West Bromwich Albion during the 2013-14 season, one of 16 different clubs he's taken charge of across his long coaching career

View Image Pepe Mel needed surgery after his stroke (Image: Rafa Babot/Getty Images)

Former West Bromwich Albion manager Pepe Mel is recovering in intensive care after he suffered a stroke. Mel, 63, had to undergo surgery after having the stroke on Sunday.

‌



The Spaniard underwent a successful operation and is now recovering at Virgen del Rocio Hospital in Seville. Real Betis, who Mel managed twice, announced the news at the request of his family.

"From Real Betis, we send all the support in the world to Pepe Mel, whom we wish a speedy recovery," the La Liga side posted on social media platform X. "We're with you, Pepe."

A product of Real Madrid's academy, most of Mel's career has been in Spain. West Brom were one of 16 different clubs that he's managed over a 27-year period, starting in 1999.

Mel took over at the Hawthorns in January 2014, with Steve Clarke having been sacked the previous month. At the time, West Brom were hovering four points above the relegation zone and there was growing discontent inside the dressing room.

Although the Baggies survived under Mel, they only finished one place above the drop. He oversaw just three wins in 17 matches while drawing six and losing eight.

Mel was sacked the day after their final game of the season. West Brom sporting and technical director Richard Garlick explained that decision was made due to events both 'on and off the field'.

Mel's most recent position was in Morocco with IR Tangier. Mel left his post in March to bring to an end a brief seven-game spell.

Alongside Betis, more of Mel's former clubs have sent him messages of support. "From Rayo Vallecano, we want to convey all our support and affection to Pepe Mel, after suffering a stroke for which he has had to undergo surgery. We wish him a swift and complete recovery," the Spanish club posted.

Another message read: "From La Liga we send all our affection and a speedy recovery to Pepe Mel. We're with you, Pepe."

Sports.title: Arsenal plotting double January transfer swoop as Mikel Arteta identifies forward targets
Sports.content:
Arsenal plotting double January transfer swoop as Mikel Arteta identifies forward targets

Mikel Arteta wants to bolster his Arsenal forward line in order to keep competing for trophies domestically and on the continent

View 2 Images Arteta wants to add to his Arsenal squad in January (Image: Getty)

Mikel Arteta is pushing to make a move in the January transfer window to bolster Arsenal’s double glory hunt.

‌



‌



Gunners boss Arteta has made a top-class forward his No.1 priority and wants to strengthen the squad as they look to retain their Premier League title and win the Champions League.

‌



They have Bournemouth forward Junior Kroupi in their sights but the Cherries do not want to sell in January and Arsenal are also likely to face competition from Paris Saint Germain and Bayern Munich.

‌



Arsenal also remain interested in Juventus winger Kenan Yildiz but there is a feeling that Arteta wants to strengthen in January in the forward area as he sees it a necessity to compete on two fronts.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



They tried to sign Morgan Rogers and then Vinicius Junior in the summer but missed out on both and ideally they want to strengthen the left flank but also want a versatile forward who can play in multiple positions.

The hope was that they would have enough options this season but Arteta is keen on reinforcements in January to maintain their push for glory.

‌



Arsenal have made a strong start to their title defence as they are three points clear at the top and carry on their push for European glory with a trip to Slavia Prague in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

That could mean a start for teenager Max Dowman, 16, who is eligible in Europe despite his three-game domestic ban as Arsenal were unsuccessful in their appeal against his red card for the sending-off at Fleetwood.

‌



View 2 Images Dowman was dismissed against Fleetwood Town (Image: Getty Images)

Arteta was blunt in telling Dowman that “we are not in Disneyland” and he must adapt to the rigours of top-level football.

‌



However, Arteta has been quick to reassure Dowman who could start on Wednesday night or be an option from the bench. There will be no hangover from the Fleetwood red card as the Gunners look to rotate through a tough run of three games in seven days.

There will be changes from Arsenal’s win at Liverpool for the Champions League game on Wednesday night while they face Hull City on Saturday.

‌



William Saliba has been training back on the grass and the France defender has been stepping up his progress and he is closing in on a full comeback with the first team squad.

Arteta has said that Saliba will be ready to return once they get the all-clear from medical checks on the back injury which has kept him out since the World Cup.

Sports.title: Leeds fan dies after medical emergency at Man Utd clash as club pay tribute
Sports.content:
Leeds fan dies after medical emergency at Man Utd clash as club pay tribute

A Leeds supporter suffered a medical emergency during their 1-1 draw with Manchester United last month, leading to him being rushed to hospital and put on life support

View Image Leeds have paid tribute to the supporter (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

Leeds have paid tribute to a fan who sadly died after suffering a medical emergency in the stands during their game against Manchester United last month. Colin Westby, 68, was watching the Premier League clash which took place at Elland Road on Sunday, October 18 before being rushed to hospital.

‌



‌



Upon his arrival, Westby was placed medically induced coma. Leeds said in a statement that after a 'period of unresponsiveness', the decision was made to withdraw life support.

‌



The club posted on their website: "Leeds United are heartbroken to learn of the passing of supporter Colin Westby at the age of 68. Colin was a long-standing Season Ticket Holder at the club, attending matches for over 50 years.

‌



"We will pay tribute to Colin in the 68th minute of our next Premier League fixture with Tottenham Hotspur, on Saturday 7 November."

Sports.title: The 4 Man Utd stars Michael Carrick should be pointing his finger at after Chelsea farce
Sports.content:
There are two alternative angles of Morgan Rogers' opening Chelsea goal that are being played on a social media loop - and both make for an excruciating watch for Manchester United fans.

One is from Peter Bankes' Refcam. It is a seven-second horror show as United players appear to bounce off an invisible forcefield around the Chelsea forward. The other, from the Premier League's own account, makes it look as if Rogers is clean through on goal, such is the absence of United bodies anywhere near him.

Seven seconds, four mistakes, and two viral clips to add to the United locker of embarrassment this season. We break down what went wrong...

Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Mistake 1 - Mbeumo

Bruno Fernandes played an aimless pass and Moises Caicedo's heavy touch saw the ball fall to Bryan Mbeumo's feet. He attempted to hold and shield the ball from Caicedo but he conceded possession, and so the move started.

Mistake 2 - Baleba

Carlos Baleba was the closest red shirt to Mbeumo. The midfielder tried to quickly win the ball back but was too slow to react and made a late challenge on Romeo Lavia.

The turnover left United in a difficult position. Leny Yoro was out of position having pushed up from right-back, leaving Rogers to run against Harry Maguire, Lisandro Martinez and Diogo Dalot.

‌



How should Man Utd line up against Roma? Let us know your XI in the comments section.

View 3 Images Bryan Mbeumo surrendered possession before Carlos Baleba failed to retrieve it (Image: Sky Sports)

Mistake 3 - Santos

Andrey Santos' role in Chelsea's opener is perhaps the most bemusing. He sprinted back when Rogers picked up the ball and managed to close him down to get to within a few yards, but what he did next was inexplicable.

The Brazilian attempted a slide tackle when he was a few yards off Rogers. It seems like Santos was trying to block a short pass from Rogers to Cole Palmer on the right rather than trying to tackle the man, but even if that were true, it would still have been the wrong decision. Refcam footage shows Rogers is firmly set on heading towards the United goal rather than playing in a team-mate, so Santos was trying to block a pass that was never likely to be made.

‌



Once Santos had failed to stop Rogers' run, it was over to the backline.

View 3 Images Morgan Rogers was allowed to score with ease (Image: Sky Sports)

Mistake 4 - Martinez

Maguire and Martinez have been disastrous as a pair this season and the goal sums up their form. There were no tricks or feints; Rogers simply ran through the gap between them.

Maguire had Estevao making a run over his right shoulder and so he could almost be forgiven for not dealing with the threat at hand, but Martinez has no such excuse. He had Palmer making a similar run over his left shoulder, but Dalot was there to deal with him. With Yoro out of position, Maguire could not pass on the man to his full-back.

‌



Martinez failed to commit and Rogers soon had the whites of Lammens' eyes in his sights. The Belgium shot-stopper tried to stay as big as he could but the damage had been done. Lammens should have berated his teammates for their amateurish defending, but there was very little reaction from the goalkeeper as United found themselves behind once again.

If ever a reaction summed up the feeling around United right now, perhaps it was that.

Sports.title: Truth behind Mikel Arteta's comment on 'incredible' Eberechi Eze after Liverpool win
Sports.content:
Truth behind Mikel Arteta's comment on 'incredible' Eberechi Eze after Liverpool win

Eberechi Eze did not get off the bench for Arsenal at Anfield but even making the matchday squad was a huge bonus for boss Mikel Arteta

View 2 Images Eberechi Eze in action for Arsenal (Image: News Images/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

Eberechi Eze was a surprise name on Arsenal’s team sheet at Liverpool on Sunday. In fact, Mikel Arteta said it was “incredible” that Eze was in the squad for Arsenal’s win at Anfield.

‌



‌



That is because at one point last week there were fears that Eze could be missing for a while - and yet his determination to be ready for his team speaks volumes about his character.

‌



Eze’s presence and availability has only served to further enhance the way the England star is viewed behind the scenes at the Emirates for his attitude and mindset.

‌



That Arteta remark got slightly lost because it was in an answer to a question about Christos Tzolis and the risk in throwing the winger straight into the starting XI after injury.

Gunners boss Arteta said: “It’s the energy that he had in training. When I asked him the question, how convinced he was. We had an issue with Ebs as well, it was incredible that he was in the squad.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

“I want to give credit to all the medical and performance team. What they are doing with those boys is incredible. Every three days, to keep everybody at this level.

‌



“These are the margins sometimes when you win a football match, whether you have somebody available or not. They deserve that credit.

“With Christos, incredible. He didn’t want to come off, he wanted to complete the game. We took some risks, but at a point we decided enough was enough.”

‌



It is fair to say that Eze has had a mixed start to the season because he was excellent from the bench at Aston Villa but has struggled from the start in games when he has played from the left.

But then he scored at Bayern Munich - a brilliantly taken goal in an epic Champions League tie - and then was pretty ineffective and frustrating as a substitute in Arsenal’s humiliating exit at Fleetwood in the Carabao Cup.

‌



However, Eze was actually playing with some niggles and injury issues which have bugged him this season. After that Fleetwood game, he underwent some checks and there were fears he could be out for a few games because of injury.

But Eze shrugged off pain and fitness issues last season to help Arsenal when they needed him most - and has stepped up again this time.

‌



View 2 Images Eberechi Eze celebrates Bayern Munich goal (Image: Adam Davy/Press Association)

Eze battled on, trained ahead of the Liverpool game and made himself available because he knew the team was short on numbers and options.

‌



Bukayo Saka is out injured while Max Dowman was suspended after the club’s unsuccessful appeal against his red card at Fleetwood.

Even though Eze did not get off the bench at Anfield, his willingness to make himself available, to be ready to step up should he be required has earned him not just glowing praise from his manager but also a lot of respect among the coaching staff.

‌



Some players have to be just right to deem themselves fit to play. Tzolis pushed himself to be back and fit to start and he is known as being tough, resilient and determined.

Eze is also showing those same qualities in abundance to ensure that he is ready to support his team. It has definitely been noticed - and marked him out as a special character.

Sports.title: Jockey Brendan Powell taken to hospital from Plumpton after "horrible" fall at first fence
Sports.content:
Jockey Brendan Powell taken to hospital from Plumpton after "horrible" fall at first fence

Powell, one of the top jump jockeys in the UK, was unseated from Diamond Days in the 2.00 race won by Walk In The West. There was a delay while he was treated at the course

View Image Brendan Powell (Image: Getty Images)

Top jockey Brendan Powell has been taken to hospital after he suffered a "horrible" fall at the first fence in a race at Plumpton.

‌



‌



The rider of 26 winners in the 2026-27 season came off Diamond Days when the Joe Tizzard-trained chaser made a mistake in the 2m 3f novices' handicap chase.

‌



Powell tried to stay aboard the 5-1 chance but ended up slipping out of the saddle and appeared to catch his mount's reins and the pair went into the rails.

‌



Plumpton's next race was delayed while medical staff gave assistance and moved him into the ambulance.

Sky Sports Racing presenter Hayley Moore said: "The doctors have informed me he is conscious and he is off to hospital. I know that's not exactly positive news but I think we will all take that when a jockey has woken up. We know how risky it is and the injuries that can suffer.

‌



"It was one of those falls that didn't look like it was going to be much and then he pulled the horse down on top of him, knocked himself out. It was pretty horrible to watch. I just hope he is going to be home soon and back to his family."

While the incident was ongoing, the next runners were kept in the parade ring and the 2.30pm race went off 11 minutes later than scheduled.

Article continues below

Powell had been booked by Tizzard to ride JPR One in Friday's Grade Two Haldon Gold Cup which is being run at Aintree instead of Exeter.

In a social media clip the rider, operating at a 27 per cent strike rate, said he had been looking forward to riding Diamond Days for the trainer and owners the Coral Racing Club.

Sports.title: Declan Rice insists Arsenal's Liverpool win owes to Mikel Arteta's internal message
Sports.content:
Declan Rice insists Arsenal's Liverpool win owes to Mikel Arteta's internal message

Arsenal ended their long way for a win at Liverpool on Sunday with their battling victory stemming from the message their head coach has hammered into them

View 2 Images Declan Rice continues to be a leading presence in Arsenal's bid to defend their Premier League crown

Declan Rice has insisted Arsenal are ready to grind out more hard fought wins - because it is the mark of champions. The Gunners midfielder revealed Mikel Arteta has been “drilling” in the importance of battling victories to ensure Arsenal retain their Premier League title.

‌



‌



Arsenal won their first Premier League game at Liverpool in 14 years to go clear at the top but it was a gritty and defiant performance which is unlikely to win over the critics.

‌



But Rice says winning at Anfield - and another 1-0 to the Arsenal - just underlines the determination within the squad to retain their title this season. It is now eight wins out of nine and six clean sheets in the Premier League.

‌



When asked whether beating Liverpool was a performance of champions, Rice said: “For sure, it’s just drilled into us. What this manager has built at this club and the togetherness of the lads – you don’t get that performance without the lads being altogether.

“The way the manager has everything under control, the way everyone works towards everything he wants is not like anything I’ve ever seen before so credit to us for what we have been doing for the last few years.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

“Now it’s a massive thing to deliver again this year and keep pushing. We’ve set those demands on ourselves and it’s up to us to keep delivering that and this adds towards that. Really good, really happy. First win here in 14 years so that’s what the manager has been drilling into us all week so to come here and deliver we’re really happy.

‌



“Yeah, I think any team who has won here in the past has never had it easy, it’s always going to be tough coming to Anfield so we had to dig in, we had to give it everything because they throw so many attacks at you. We had to be resilient and strong. It was a great win and in the end we’re really happy and now we go onto Wednesday in the Champions League as that’s another massive one.”

There was a big debate over whether Arsenal should have won with more flair at Nottingham Forest last month while winning at Liverpool is surely a tougher task.

‌



View 2 Images Mikel Arteta ended Arsenal's 14-year wait for a win at Anfield (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

But Rice says every game is a challenge and yet insists that the win at Liverpool was a statement as he believes Andoni Iraola is building a team to be reckoned with.

‌



Rice added: “What I’ve learned in this league is that every game is different, no game is plain sailing it is always going to be tough. Looking back at that Forest game, it wasn’t the best performance but we ground it out and we won and there’s going to be more of that this season. But results like this just make it that extra bit special so we are delighted.

“Look at Liverpool. They have secretly gone under the radar, their attack is incredible, the defence is really good, Man City have started really strong, Chelsea are there or thereabouts so I’ve learned in this league November means nothing.

Article continues below

“You just have to win as much as you can and in February or March if you are there or thereabouts you are in with a chance. So just keep winning and take each game as it comes and see where it takes us.”

Sports.title: Tyson Fury makes worrying decision for huge Anthony Joshua fight
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury makes worrying decision for huge Anthony Joshua fight

Former two-time heavyweight champion Tyson Fury is expected to pile on the pounds for his fight with Anthony Joshua - a tactic which has backfired in the past

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua (Image: Getty Images for Netflix)

Tyson Fury looks set to weigh a whopping 280lb for all-British showdown with Anthony Joshua - a move which could prove costly.

‌



‌



Fury and Joshua will finally settle their decade-long feud on December 11 at the Principality Stadium in Cardiff. The 'Gypsy King' comes into the contest off the back of forcing Mariusz Wach to quit on his stool back in July, while Joshua survived two knockdowns to stop Kristian Prenga.

‌



Prior to stopping Wach over in Thailand, Fury officially weighed in at 265lb. But for his meeting mouthwatering meeting with Joshua, he expects to weigh MORE. During a recent post uploaded to Instagram, the 38-year-old expects to tip the scales at 280lb. “Big boy 280lbs incoming. Not your average build! However, the love handles are used for energy," he wrote.

‌



Most notably, it's still 1lb shy than what he weighed in for his rematch with Oleksandr Usyk two years. The Morecambe brawler put on the pounds in a bid to stop his foe early, but would go on to lose on points for a second time.
