World.title: 3 Arrested in Connection With Deadly Blast in Central Athens
World.content:
The Greek authorities on Friday arrested three men in connection with the theft of copper gas pipes from a building in a central tourist district of Athens last month, saying their actions led to a massive explosion that killed six people.

The three men — who were identified only as two Greeks, ages 37 and 55, and a 34-year-old Albanian — faced an investigating magistrate at an Athens court complex and were granted an extension until Monday to prepare their defense, according to a fire service spokesman, Vassilis Vathrakoyiannis. Investigators have not announced what charges they will pursue.

“According to the findings of the investigation, the three individuals are alleged to have sabotaged the pipe work of the natural gas installation in an attempt to steal copper pipes,” the fire service said in a statement. “Investigating their actions and establishing their connection to the explosion formed a central part of the inquiry.”

The explosion early on Sept. 25 in the Plaka district brought down the two-story building, killing a Greek woman, her British husband and two American siblings, along with their spouses.

World.title: Russian bombing kills 24 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
World.content:
The Russian military has not publicly commented.

Zelensky initially put the death toll at 18, but Ukraine's state emergencies service DSNS later said 24 people, including two rescuers and four police officers, were confirmed to have been killed.

"The Russians could not have been unaware that the local residents who remained in Komyshuvakha received humanitarian aid there every week," the Ukrainian president wrote in a post on social media.

"This is yet another proof that Russia does not want any de-escalation."

He said that after a recent successful joint Russian-Ukrainian operation to evacuate civilians from the Russia-occupied southern city of Oleshky during a temporary ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump "there was a moment when the next steps could show that peace is possible".

"With such killings, Russia is sending the exact opposite signal - Russia is counting on further killings," Zelensky said.

Meanwhile, Semikin described the Russian attack as a "terrible tragedy" for the village, confirming that "people are still under the rubble".

He said rescue teams were working at the scene, but they had been forced to halt their operation a number of times because of Russian drone attacks in the area.

A day of mourning has been declared for Tuesday across the entire Zaporizhzhia region.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

World.title: Fake nuclear warning from hacked app sparks unease but not panic in Ukraine
World.content:
Ukrainians have grown weary of the relentless alerts blaring from their phones and echoing through their streets, day and night, warning of Russian drones and missiles.

On Sunday night, the system delivered something to make them sit up and take note â a succession of more extreme threats that quickly escalated to impending nuclear strikes, chemical attacks and combat on the streets.

But many in the country did not take them seriously and doubted the veracity of the messages.

Sofia Kochmar, 34, a mother-of-one living in the western city of Lviv, said she was initially concerned but quickly questioned the authenticity of the alerts.

"The first thing I saw was the word 'nuclear' and that made me pretty nervous and scared. So my first thought was that something nuclear was actually flying toward us."

"But then the notification mentioned 'street fighting in Kyiv', and I thought, wait, no, that's impossible."

The alerts included some messages written in Russian, and one included a link to a Telegram channel apparently owned by a hacker group.

Within 15 minutes, Ukraine's Air Force issued a statement saying the alert app had been compromised and clarifying there was no radiation threat. But it took more than an hour to issue "all clear" messages.

Anastasiia Romanytska, a 29-year-old ballerina living in Kyiv, said she does not have the alert app installed but friends forwarded her the warnings.

"My first reaction was, 'Is this some kind of joke?' But then my body reacted as if I was under stress. My heart started racing, and my stomach tightened up."

"Still, somehow I immediately realised that it wasn't something serious. Or maybe I just really wanted to believe that."

There are a number of apps delivering phone notifications of air raid warnings, with maps showing areas under threat, all using the same data as the official government-backed app.

World.title: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
World.content:
Stephan Moelans, the CEO of Sabcobel, which operates Delhaize's systems, on Monday told the Belga news agency that the incident was a cyber-attack and that the company had been "working all night and morning to disconnect the affected units from the network".

He said since the French attack in early October, the company had been working to "protect our customers fridges against this vulnerability" but that the units needed physical modifications, not just software updates.

Most supermarkets across Europe are linked to the internet, and maintenance and troubleshooting can be done remotely.

"The simplest solution is to manage the fridges over a secure internet connection. Most of our customers switched to that after the attack in France," Moelans added.

The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C (122F).

It is unclear who is behind the latest apparent attack.

In the US, authorities are investigating what caused refrigeration malfunctions at a number of American military bases in August and working together with French officials to examine whether the incidents could be linked.

Both Belgium and Sweden's national cyber-security agencies said they were monitoring the incident.

The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said it was working with international partners and industry to "fully understand details of an incident". No incidents have been reported in the UK.

In Flanders, northern Belgium, a Delhaize branch in Hoeilaart told news website Het Laatste Nieuws it had lost â¬100,000 (Â£83,500) worth of produce.

The manager said that estimate did not even take into account further losses that would result from closing the shop.

Carrefour, a French-owned supermarket, said the incident had only affected 15 of its Belgian stores, adding that measures had been taken immediately to ensure all shops remained open.

A spokesperson for Colruyt Group, which operates Spar stores in Belgium under a franchise system, told Reuters news agency five shops had their fridge systems attacked.

Sweden's budget furniture retailer Ikea said refrigeration systems of its store in the western Belgian city of Mons were affected, with a spokesman quoted by Reuters as saying "we cannot rule out that additional locations may be affected".

World.title: Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire
World.content:
Fighting has resumed in Ukraine's Kherson after a six-day truce brought quiet to the front-line region for the first time in years.

The ceasefire - the longest since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 - allowed hundreds of people trapped in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky and its surroundings to be evacuated.

On Monday morning, local authorities confirmed that strikes had resumed, saying Moscow had hit a medical facility in Kherson city centre. They also said a 62-year-old woman and a 73-year-old man were injured when a Russian drone attacked the car they were travelling in.

Ukraine also accused Russian forces of using the humanitarian ceasefire to strengthen their military positions, rotate units and deliver ammunition.

"The enemy used the humanitarian pause to set up their positions," said Ukraine's General Staff, adding they had recorded rotation of Russian units, expansion of anti-drone equipment on the roads, and delivery of ammunition.

The Kremlin appeared to corroborate this when spokesman Dmitry Peskov said it was "reasonable to assume that the Ukrainian army also used this period for the necessary regrouping".

"It is a completely standard practice in such situations," he added.

The ceasefire had been brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Both Kyiv and Moscow thanked her repeatedly, though no details of her involvement were shared.

An unusual show of cooperation came from Russia's human rights ombudsman Yana Lantratova and her Ukrainian counterpart Dmytro Lubinets. The pair oversaw the ceasefire, travelled into Oleshky and were filmed speaking to residents together. They publicly thanked each other for their work, often highlighting that no violations of the ceasefire had been observed.

Both Lantratova and Lubinets called for the initiative to be repeated elsewhere, and Ukraine repeatedly said it would be prepared to observe similar ceasefires on a national level too.

But many have questioned whether this will lead to more cooperation and further truces.

In fact, the Kremlin swiftly dismissed the idea even as the ceasefire was under way, calling Oleshky "an isolated case" which would not affect the "settlement process" â a euphemism for the stalled peace talks. "There are no similar plans or initiatives," Peskov reiterated on Monday.

And although last week the guns fell silent in Kherson region, elsewhere in Ukraine Russia's air strikes continued, killing scores of civilians and destroying crucial infrastructure.

The decision to observe an unusually broad and comparatively lengthy ceasefire in and around Oleshky was therefore a notable exception.

The ceasefire's observance appears, at least in part, to have been linked to Melania Trump's reported involvement. By violating the truce, Moscow would have risked undermining its own efforts to cultivate the crucial relationship with her husband, US President Donald Trump.

Some commentators have argued that Trump himself would be interested in presenting the Oleshky ceasefire as a foreign policy achievement scored days before the US midterm elections on Tuesday.

"I totally get why our official representatives need to 'play along' with the US first lady on Oleshky," said Artyom Sheynin, a prominent figure on Russian state TV.

"I understand why it's so important to create a 'success story' ahead of the elections for the US president, whose wife 'achieved a ceasefire' in Oleshky."

Kyiv, too, had its reasons to be fully compliant. Although relations with the US and its president are often fraught, Ukraine continues to rely heavily on US intelligence and US-made Patriot air defence missiles to counter Russian aerial attacks. Ahead of another tough winter of war, continued American support is essential to protect Ukrainian skies from Russia's assaults.

But though the ceasefire may have been born out of political calculation rather than purely humanitarian compassion, it also resulted in hundreds of civilians escaping.

There were emotional scenes when hundreds of Oleshky residents arrived in northern Ukraine on Saturday. Many were met by tearful relatives they had not seen in years. To the journalists waiting, the evacuees told of years of hunger and hardship in a destroyed town.

The hundreds of residents who decided to stay behind will receive monthly humanitarian aid deliveries, Lantratova said, adding that decision too was the result of Melania Trump's mediation.

Yet the troop rotations and resupply efforts show that neither side is expecting Oleshky to be a blueprint for lasting respite in the future.

As Kherson came under fire again, Ukrainian drones hit several energy facilities across four Russian regions. In Samara, residents reported hearing explosions and seeing black plumes of smoke rising into the sky as an oil refinery was hit for the fifth time in a month.

If the truce brought a rare moment of relief to Oleshky, it has done little to alter the wider trajectory of a war that grinds on for now.

World.title: Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord
World.content:
Dutch authorities have offered a record award of â¬2m (Â£1.7m/$2.24m) for information leading to the arrest of Jos Leijdekkers, one of Europe's most-wanted men.

The 35-year-old, who is also known as Bolle Jos (Chubby Jos), was previously accused of being "one of the key players in international cocaine trafficking" by Dutch police.

Commenting on the decision to increase the reward ten-fold, Dutch justice minister David van Weel said it was "necessary given the threat that Leijdekkers poses to national security, our democratic rule of law, and the international legal order".

Dutch prosecutors said capturing Leijdekkers was their "highest priority" and any information shared would be kept secret.

World.title: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured
World.content:
Warning: This article contains graphic details that some people may find distressing

South African police have arrested five people in connection with a brutal attack on a cattle farmer, who was assaulted and tortured in what has been described as a "senseless and barbaric" act.

Donovan Marx, 50, was attacked during a house robbery on his farm in Ventersdorp, a small town in South Africa's North West province, last Wednesday.

Marx was ambushed as he returned home, shot and stabbed and had his ears cut off in the horrific ordeal, police said.

All five of his alleged attackers were arrested over the weekend, a move welcomed by Marx's wife and family.

They added that the "legal process must [now] take its course".

The horrific attack has caused widespread outrage in a country which is used to high levels of violence.

Police last week explained how the attack on Mark happened.

A group of masked men armed with guns approached a worker at Mark's house as he was mowing the lawn, they said in a statement.

The attackers then demanded to know where Marx was before tying the worker's hands and feet with cable ties.

When Marx returned home, police said two of the suspects allegedly approached him and shot him in the upper body.

"They [then] dragged him inside the house, tied his hands and feet with cable ties, and allegedly stabbed him."

The suspects then ransacked the house and took three firearms from a safe before escaping with Marx's van.

The ordeal ended after the farm worker managed to free himself and call for assistance.

Marx was rushed to hospital, where he remains, but may need prosthetic ears after surgeons were unable to save his own, local news site IOL reported.

South Africa's Agriculture Minister Willie Aucamp condemned the attack on Marx, adding there was no "place in our country for such senseless and barbaric acts".

The chair of parliament's police committee, Ian Cameron, praised police for the swift arrests and called for a "strong, properly investigated case" to follow.

The five suspects, aged between 26 and 56, will appear in local courts on Tuesday and face house robbery, attempted murder and illegal possession of firearms and ammunition charges.

Some right-wing groups have used such attacks on white farmers, who are often from the Afrikaner community, to say there is a genocide against white people in the country - a claim that has been widely discredited.

Although the claims have been dismissed by every political party in the country, including those representing Afrikaners, US President Donald Trump has repeated them and has offered white Afrikaners asylum in the US.

South Africa's latest crime statistics, covering the period between April and June 2026, do not specify how many attacks took place on farms and only recorded one robbery in a rural area.

However, police data show most victims of crime in South Africa, including on farms, are black.

World.title: Wizz Air flight from Luton in emergency landing after bomb threat
World.content:
A Wizz Air flight travelling from London Luton Airport to Sofia has been escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet to Budapest after a mid-air bomb threat.

The aircraft was forced to make an emergency landing at Budapest Liszt Ferenc International.

Authorities there "carried out the necessary security checks on the aircraft and passengers", a spokesperson for Wizz Air said.

The airline later confirmed an inspection had been "completed and nothing was found", adding that the plane would depart again shortly. Hungarian Defence Minister Romulusz Ruszin-Szendis confirmed his country provided the fighter jet to escort the flight.

According to flight tracking website FlightAware, Wizz Air flight 4302 departed Luton at 08:33 GMT and was due to arrive in the Bulgarian capital at 13:25 local time (11:25 GMT).

But the website said it landed in Budapest at 12:09 local time (11:09 GMT).

World.title: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
World.content:
Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff and confirmed airfares will be "materially higher" next summer because of a sharp rise in fuel costs following the US-Israel war with Iran.

The airline said it expects fuel prices to remain high "well into 2027" unless there is a "swift resolution" to the conflict.

Ryanair said its fuel bill is forecast to be â¬2bn (Â£1.6bn) higher in the short-term and its boss, Michael O'Leary, said airfares would have to rise by "double-digits" to help cover the cost.

But the firm said that was unlikely to be enough and it is looking into pay freezes. Unite, the union representing Ryanair staff, said it had not been told of "any such proposals".

O'Leary also said the company would slow down hiring as airline's costs rise.

The airline said its pre-tax profits fell by 16% to â¬2.4bn during the six months to the end of September, largely due to fuel costs jumping by 15%.

The company said that although 80% of its fuel bill had been "hedged" â in effect, bought in advance at fixed prices â the cost of the remainder was elevated.

O'Leary reiterated forecasts from earlier this year Ryanair would "need a 20% fare increase" to cover the cost of jet fuel.

"I'm not sure we'll get to 20%," he said. "But we're certainly looking at double-digit fare increases across Europe from all airlines in 2027."

Aviation fuel prices have surged this year as a result of the US-Israel war with Iran, which has dramatically reduced the supply of refined products coming from the Gulf and increased competition for those produced elsewhere.

Ryanair also said it was weighing up whether to freeze pay, as multi-year wage deals with unions come to to an end. The policy could be implemented from April next year.

Oliver Richardson, national officer at Unite, said the union "hasn't been advised of any such proposals and we have a multi-year pay deal in place which covers next year. A number of Unions across Europe have the same".

He said: "Our pay agreement was not attached to, nor dependent on company performance. This was something that the Ryanair was at pains to emphasise. As such we would expect it to be honoured."

Ryanair also said it would increase its use of artificial intelligence within its back office and support functions.

Meanwhile, Ryanair has cut back on winter flights and said on Monday there would be more to come. It said this was happening across the airline industry, particularly with short-haul carriers.

O'Leary said: "We believe those cuts will continue into the summer of 2027. Over the medium term, we expect short-haul capacity will remain constrained out to the early 2030s."

World.title: Police arrest man for pushing teenage girl off two-storey building
World.content:
The police in Imo State have arrested a 26-year-old man, Ifeanyi Chukwu, for allegedly pushing a 17-year-old girl from a two-storey building in the state.

The police spokesperson in the state, Henry Okoye, disclosed this in a statement on Monday.

Mr Okoye, a deputy superintendent of police, said the suspect allegedly pushed the victim, Chiamaka Chukwuokore, from the building on Sunday in Owerri, the Imo State capital.

He said the victim was said to be the niece of the suspect’s unnamed girlfriend.

“The incident reportedly occurred on November 1, 2026, at about 1300 hours, following an alleged altercation between the suspect and the victim.

“The victim sustained serious injuries and was immediately rushed to a nearby hospital, where she is currently receiving medical attention and remains in critical condition,” he said.

Rescue from angry mob

The police spokesperson said an angry mob mobilised to lynch the suspect after the incident, but that police operatives promptly rescued him.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He said the suspect was subsequently taken into police custody.

PREMIUM TIMES sighted a video clip which showed three armed police operatives running to their waiting vehicle with the suspect in handcuffs while the angry mob pursued them vigorously until the suspect successfully entered the vehicle.

“The suspect is currently undergoing investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the incident and facilitate necessary legal action,” Mr Ndukwe said.

He said police authorities in the state have urged residents, particularly social media users, to refrain from spreading unverified information about the incident.

“The public is advised to exercise restraint and rely on official sources for accurate updates,” he said.

Mr Ndukwe said the Commissioner of Police in Imo State, Audu Bosso, has assured residents of the state that the incident was being “thoroughly investigated.”

Mr Bosso added that all necessary steps would be taken to establish the facts and ensure that justice was served in accordance with the law.

The commissioner also appealed to the residents to remain calm, refrain from taking the law into their own hands and allow the police to carry out their duties professionally.

“Further developments will be communicated in due course,” he assured.

World.title: Governor seeks death penalty for kidnappers, sends bill to state assembly
World.content:
Governor Francis Nwifuru of Ebonyi State says his administration has forwarded an executive bill to the state House of Assembly to make kidnapping a capital offence punishable by death without an option of alternative punishment.

Mr Nwifuru said this on Friday during the funeral of the slain traditional ruler of Ndufu-Alike Community in Ikwo Local Government Area, Francis Igwe, Vanguard reported.

“This should serve as a deterrent to those planning a kidnapping, whether for political reasons or otherwise,” the governor said.

Mr Igwe, father of the immediate past Deputy Governor of Ebonyi State, Kelechi Igwe, was abducted on 1 March 1 while on his way to church.

He was found dead a day later.

‘Youths’ future is bleak’

Mr Nwifuru, while speaking at the traditional ruler’s funeral, decried the moral deterioration among Nigerian youths.

“I am worried about our present-day youths taking up leadership positions tomorrow. Some of our youths are not well informed, and they act so irrationally.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“I am concerned because, with some of their attitudinal dispositions, there seems to be no future for our youths.

“The youths need to have a rethink concerning certain actions of theirs, especially as concerns their attitudes towards community leaders,” he said.

“They should desist from treating their leaders as holders of their destinies.”

Mr Nwifuru vowed to implement any court decision against those arrested over the traditional ruler’s murder, stressing that the proposed legislation was intended to deter kidnapping in the state.

He maintained that the traditional ruler’s murder should be the last of such incidents in Ikwo and other parts of the state.

The governor described the late traditional ruler as “a forthright, vocal and astute parliamentarian” who represented his people effectively in the old Anambra State.

He said the traditional ruler attracted development projects to his community, including the popular Folk Technical College, which has produced prominent Nigerians.

In their tributes, former governors of the state, Sam Egwu and Martin Elechi, as well as former Senate President, Pius Anyim, described the deceased as a statesman, peacemaker, renowned educationist, administrator and passionate leader who left enduring legacies.

They urged the family and the Ikwo people to take solace in his contributions to society.

Speaking in his tribute, the slain traditional ruler’s first son and former deputy governor, Kelechi, described his father as a devoted family man and role model who guided him on family life, religion, politics and culture.

He said the circumstances surrounding his father’s death remained difficult for the family to comprehend.

The former deputy governor said the family was confident that the legacy of the slain traditional ruler would endure for generations to come.

What the applicable laws say

Kidnapping is illegal in Nigeria.

The offence attracts severe penalties, including life imprisonment and, in certain circumstances, the death penalty.

Criminal Code Act and the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022 are the two principal laws that outlaw kidnapping and hostage taking.

While the Criminal Code Act prescribes imprisonment of up to 10 years, the Terrorism (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022, which addresses the offence in the context of terrorism, prescribes severe punishment, including death, where the offence resulted in the death of a victim.

However, the punishment for kidnappings varies across the states in the country.

In Ebonyi State, kidnapping is a serious criminal offence.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the applicable legislation on kidnapping is the Ebonyi State Internal Security Enforcement and Other Related Matters Law, 2009 (Cap. 55, Vol. 2).

World.title: Jailed couple sentenced to fresh 10 years’ imprisonment for property fraud
World.content:
The Lagos State Special Offences Court in Ikeja has sentenced convicted couple, Harry Uyanwanne and Oluwakemi Odia, also known as Kristein Uyanwanne, to at least 10 years’ imprisonment each for fraud involving N67.6 million.

Trial judge Mojisola Dada delivered the judgement on Monday and ordered the defendants to refund the to the petitioner, Olusola Odemuyiwa.

The couple were prosecuted by the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) on charges of conspiracy, stealing and obtaining money by false pretence. EFCC spokesperson Dele Oyewale disclosed this in a statement on Monday.

They were discharged on a separate charge of forgery.

The charges arose from the alleged fraudulent sale of a property at No. 19, Murtala Mohammed Way, Ebute Meta, Oyingbo, Lagos, belonging to beneficiaries of the estate of the late Moshood Babatunde Odemuyiwa.

The prosecution alleged that the defendants sold the property in 2010 for N16 million, falsely claiming they had the authority of the estate’s beneficiaries to sell it.

According to the EFCC, the defendants knew they had no such authority but presented themselves as authorised to dispose of the property.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The couple pleaded not guilty to the charges. During the trial, prosecution counsel, Fadeke Giwa, called three witnesses and tendered several documents, while the defence called one witness.

In her judgement, Ms Dada held that the prosecution had proved its case beyond reasonable doubt.

She sentenced the defendants to three years’ imprisonment for conspiracy, one year for stealing and 10 years for obtaining money by false pretence, without the option of fine.

EFCC’s statement did not disclose if the judge ordered the sentences to run concurrently or consecutively. The prison time for each of the couple will amount to 14 years, if the sentences were ordered to run consecutively, and 10 years if ordered to run concurrently.

But the statement said the judge ordered that Uyanwanne’s sentence be suspended until he is apprehended.

The conviction is not the couple’s first encounter with the court over fraud allegations. In December 2024, the same court sentenced Mr Uyanwanne to 10 years’ imprisonment and Ms Odia to six years over a separate N52 million fraud involving the sale of a property in Magodo, Lagos. The sentences were ordered to run concurrently.

In that case, the court also ordered the closure and deregistration of Temple International Church, which was a co-defendant, and directed the couple to pay N31 million in restitution to the complainant.

World.title: EFCC arraigns man, company for N12.5bn fraud in Lagos
World.content:
The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) has arraigned Adonu Kingsley Ifeanyi and his company, S Mobile Netzone Limited, for alleged N12.5 billion fraud.

In a statement on Monday, EFCC spokesperson Dele Oyewale said the defendants appeared before trial judge Yellim Bogoro of the Federal High Court in Lagos.

The statement noted that he faces five counts of obtaining money by false pretence and stealing.

The commission put the amount involved at N12,556,837,842.

S Mobile Netzone Limited was among 58 companies the EFCC named in March 2025 in a public alert on alleged illegal investment schemes.

The commission warned Nigerians against dealing with the companies, saying they were not registered with the Central Bank of Nigeria or the Securities and Exchange Commission.

According to one count, Mr Ifeanyi received N1.24 billion through a bank account belonging to the company between 4 June 2021 and 31 October 2022.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The EFCC alleged that he knew the money was part of proceeds of unlawful activity involving obtaining money by false pretence.

In another count, he was accused of receiving N6.79 billion through the same account between 15 January 2020 and 14 April 2022, knowing that the money was proceeds of stealing.

The defendants pleaded not guilty to all five counts.

Following their pleas, prosecution lawyer, Suleiman I. Suleiman, asked the court to fix a date for trial.

Mr Bogoro granted the request and admitted the defendants to bail on the same terms and conditions earlier granted by another judge C. J. Aneke on 8 July 2025.

The case was adjourned for the commencement of trial.

World.title: Lagos to host All Nigeria Rotary Peace Summit this November
World.content:
Lagos State is set to host the All Nigeria Rotary Peace Summit, bringing together international peacebuilding experts, academics, security professionals, policymakers and civil society leaders to discuss practical approaches to conflict resolution and peacebuilding in Nigeria.

The organisers disclosed this in a statement Ehi Braimah issued on behalf of the summit’s Media and Communications Committee and sent to PREMIUM TIMES on Monday.

According to the statement, the summit will take place on 7 November at the Victoria Garden Event Centre, Alausa, Ikeja.

With the theme “Good Governance, Justice and Equity: Foundations for Sustainable Peace”, the summit will focus on developing practical recommendations, building stronger partnerships and obtaining stakeholder commitments to promote lasting peace.

The organisers said they would use the summit to translate discussions into concrete actions under the sub-theme “From Dialogue to Action: Forging a Sustainable Peace Legacy in Nigeria”.

Keynote address

Lea Perekrests, director of partnerships at the Institute for Economics and Peace (IEP), will deliver the keynote address, titled “Global Perspectives on Good Governance, Justice and Equity as Foundations for Sustainable Peace”.

She will discuss the role of effective institutions, inclusive governance and equitable societies in building sustainable peace.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Her presentation, scheduled for 12:35 a.m., will examine Nigeria’s peacebuilding challenges and opportunities from an international perspective, with particular attention to social cohesion and resilient communities.

Beyond the keynote address, the summit will host two high-level panel discussions. The first, titled “Governance, Justice, Equity and National Cohesion”, will feature Joseph Ochogwu, Director-General of the Institute for Peace and Conflict Resolution (IPCR), as moderator.

Its panellists include Rear Admiral (rtd.) Elkana Jaiyeola, an intelligence practitioner, naval officer and security expert; Diamond Nebechukwu, director of the Abdulmalik Abubakar Institute for Peace and Sustainable Development Studies (AAIPSDS); and Richard Aborishade, professor of criminology at Olabisi Onabanjo University (OOU).

They will assess the relationship between accountable leadership, access to justice, fair development and national unity.

The discussion will also draw on their professional experience in security, peace studies and criminology to address institutional accountability, governance shortcomings and declining public confidence in national institutions.

The organisers said the session would combine presentations, moderated discussions and audience contributions before producing recommendations to strengthen national cohesion.

Second session

Furthermore, Ibim Semenitari will moderate the summit’s second session, which will examine “Security, Inclusion and the Future of Peace in Nigeria”.

Semenitari, an entrepreneur, administrator, farmer, communications specialist, journalist and Rotarian, will lead conversations with Kaltumi Abdulazeez, who champions the rights of women, girls and marginalised communities; Oyebisi Oluseyi, executive director of The Nigeria Network of NGOs; and Samuel Ajiye.

The session will explore practical ways to promote peace through inclusive participation, stronger community involvement, civil society partnerships and effective security interventions.

It will also consider the contributions of women, young people, vulnerable communities and NGOs to sustainable peacebuilding efforts.

Convener

Meanwhile, Yinka Babalola, the summit convener and president of Rotary International, will deliver the opening address before formally declaring the event open.

He will speak on peacebuilding in Nigeria, while his participation will reinforce Rotary’s commitment to conflict prevention, dialogue, peaceful coexistence and international understanding.

Representatives of youth organisations, women’s groups, security agencies and the diplomatic community will also deliver goodwill messages at the summit.

They include Abisogun Akinbode, National President of JCI Nigeria; Kunbi Wuraola, Convener of Women on a Mission; Inspector-General of Police Olatunji, IGP; Rilwan Disu; and Sweden’s Ambassador to Nigeria, Anna Westerholm.

Highlight

A key feature of the summit will be a session titled “From Dialogue to Action— Key Recommendations from Stakeholders, Commitments and Peace Legacy Agenda”, which PDG Wole Kukoyi will coordinate, according to the organisers.

The session will bring stakeholders together to develop practical commitments from the issues and recommendations raised during the summit.

The programme will also feature the signing of a Peace Legacy Accord and Agenda, as well as the unveiling of a summit declaration and communiqué detailing the participants’ agreements and proposed actions.

The organisers said these steps would help move the conversations beyond the summit by establishing a basis for sustained collaboration and implementation.

They noted that the gathering would bring together Rotary leaders, government representatives, peacebuilding practitioners, security experts, development groups and civil society organisations to strengthen cooperation.

The summit will also promote the idea that lasting peace depends on effective governance, justice, fairness and the inclusion of different groups in decision-making.

World.title: Nasarawa SDP governorship candidate gifts 163 women leaders cars, cash, equipment
World.content:
Muhammad Adamu, the Social Democratic Party (SDP) governorship candidate in Nasarawa State, has distributed vehicles, cash and household equipment to women leaders across the state as he prepares for the 2027 governorship election.

Mr Adamu, former Inspector-General of Police, said the empowerment programme, held on 31 October, covered women leaders across the 13 local government areas and 147 electoral wards in the state.

In a statement announcing the exercise, his campaign said the beneficiaries received cars, refrigerators, grinding machines, generators, solar-powered fans and cash support.

Mr Adamu also confirmed the distribution in a post on his official Facebook page.

“The programme featured the distribution of vehicles, generators, refrigerators, grinding machines, solar-powered fans and cash support to women leaders,” he wrote.

He said the initiative reflected his commitment to promoting women’s economic empowerment and strengthening grassroots participation.

According to the campaign statement, each of the 13 local government women leaders received a Sharon car, a solar-powered fan and N200,000.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The three zonal women leaders also received cars and solar-powered fans. The statement said they were allocated N600,000 each, but later said each received N200,000.

The 147 ward women leaders received a refrigerator, grinding machine, generator, solar-powered table fan and N100,000 each. The campaign allocated a total of N14.7 million in cash to the ward leaders.

The statement described the exercise as an effort to strengthen women’s participation in politics and improve their economic independence.

Political ambition

Mr Adamu is running for governor on the SDP platform in the 2027 general election.

His campaign activities have included engagements with political supporters and interventions in communities across the state.

In October, he mourned Baba Alhaji, his coordinator in Alagye Electoral Ward, Doma Local Government Area, who was reportedly abducted and later found dead.

READ ALSO: Nasarawa SDP coordinator killed after abduction in Doma

In a condolence message posted on Facebook, the former police chief called on security agencies to investigate the incident and bring those responsible to justice.

His latest empowerment programme comes as political parties and their candidates prepare for the 2027 elections.

Other interventions

The women’s empowerment programme followed another intervention by Mr Adamu in Keffi, where he commissioned two solar-powered borehole projects.

In a separate Facebook post, he said the projects were located at Angwan Lambu Phase II and the High Court area of Keffi.

He said the boreholes were sponsored by his wife, Rukayya Adamu, and were intended to address water needs among students of Nasarawa State University, Keffi, and residents of surrounding communities.

Mr Adamu described the projects as practical interventions aimed at improving the welfare of residents.

The SDP candidate has presented the empowerment programme and the borehole projects as part of his efforts to support communities and strengthen grassroots participation ahead of the 2027 election.

World.title: Health Review: Ebola case, child malnutrition, medicine security, other developments that shaped October
World.content:
October brought major developments across Nigeria’s health sector, with the confirmation of an Ebola case in Abuja prompting renewed disease surveillance, contact tracing and emergency response measures.

The month also saw growing concerns over Nigeria’s dependence on imported pharmaceutical ingredients, child malnutrition and challenges affecting maternal and child healthcare.

Beyond Nigeria, the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) continued to raise concerns about regional health security.

PREMIUM TIMES reviews some of the major health developments that shaped October.

Nigeria confirms first Ebola case in over a decade

Nigeria confirmed its first Ebola case since 2014 on 20 October, involving a 42-year-old Ugandan-born woman living in Abuja who recently returned from Uganda.

The confirmation prompted contact tracing, heightened surveillance and infection prevention measures across healthcare facilities.

The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) initially identified 44 close contacts, with the number increasing as investigations continued.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Read full article

Ebola patient evacuated to Switzerland

Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola patient and her husband were medically evacuated to Switzerland on 26 October after the patient received treatment in isolation in Abuja.

The patient was transferred to Geneva University Hospitals, while her husband was placed in isolation at University Hospital Zurich.

Following the evacuation, the World Health Organisation (WHO) said Nigeria had no active confirmed Ebola case, although surveillance and monitoring of exposed contacts continued.

Read full article

NCDC expands health declarations for international travellers

The NCDC expanded the health declaration requirement to all international travellers after confirming Ebola in Abuja.

The agency said the measure was intended to strengthen screening at points of entry and support the early identification of potential infections.

It also urged healthcare facilities to isolate suspected cases promptly and strengthen infection prevention measures.

Read full article

Suspected Ebola cases in Adamawa test negative

Two suspected Ebola cases identified in Adamawa State tested negative after two rounds of laboratory testing, the NCDC announced on 31 October.

The suspected cases involved a 34-year-old pilot and his wife, a medical doctor, who were admitted to an isolation facility at the Modibbo Adama University Teaching Hospital in Yola after developing symptoms suggestive of Ebola.

The agency said the Abuja case remained Nigeria’s only laboratory-confirmed Ebola infection during the outbreak.

Read full article

FG clarifies N10 billion emergency disease response funding

The NCDC said the N10 billion emergency intervention fund approved by the federal government was intended to strengthen preparedness and response to Ebola, Lassa fever and other emerging infectious diseases.

The agency explained that the funding would support surveillance, laboratory diagnosis, protective equipment, emergency operations and rehabilitation of isolation facilities.

The clarification came amid questions over how the emergency allocation was being utilised following the confirmation of Ebola in Abuja.

Read full article

Child malnutrition admissions rise in North-east

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) reported an 18 per cent increase in malnutrition admissions at 10 supported health facilities in North-east Nigeria.

The facilities recorded nearly 20,000 admissions between January and September 2026, compared with about 17,000 during the same period in 2025.

Children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers were among those most affected, highlighting the continuing impact of insecurity and food shortages on vulnerable communities.

Read full article

FG partners US foundation to mobilise $1 billion against malnutrition

The federal government announced a partnership with the US-based Operation End Starvation initiative to mobilise more than $1 billion to address child malnutrition and starvation-related deaths across sub-Saharan Africa.

Nigeria was identified as a priority country under the initiative, which aims to mobilise funding over two years.

The government said the partnership would complement existing interventions addressing hunger and acute malnutrition among children, pregnant women and breastfeeding mothers.

Read full article

Imported drug ingredients raise medicine security concerns

Health and pharmaceutical stakeholders warned that Nigeria’s dependence on imported active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs) could undermine medicine security and expose the country to global supply disruptions.

At a meeting organised by Nigeria Health Watch in partnership with the World Bank Group, stakeholders called for increased domestic production of essential pharmaceutical ingredients.

They identified inadequate infrastructure, unreliable electricity, financing constraints and regulatory challenges as major barriers to local manufacturing.

Read full article

WHO warns of widespread undiagnosed diabetes in Africa

The WHO raised concerns over the growing diabetes burden in Africa, warning that about 75 per cent of people living with the condition in the region remain undiagnosed.

The organisation said an estimated 24.6 million adults aged between 20 and 79 were living with diabetes in the African region.

The findings renewed concerns about limited screening, delayed diagnosis and access to treatment for non-communicable diseases.

Read full article

Ebola outbreak worsens in DR Congo

The Ebola outbreak in the DRC continued to spread during October, with confirmed cases surpassing 10,000 and deaths approaching 5,000.

The WHO reported 10,274 confirmed cases and 4,992 deaths in the country as of 28 October.

The outbreak, which also affected other African countries, intensified concerns about cross-border transmission, surveillance capacity and regional preparedness.

Read full article

World.title: Campaign, no campaign, By Dakuku Peterside
World.content:
Nigeria’s political parties can tell us who will coordinate their campaigns, mobilise their supporters and deliver their strongholds. They owe us comparable clarity on who will deliver safer communities, functioning hospitals, and an economy where work pays. As preparations for the 2027 elections gather momentum, the machinery for winning power is becoming visible. The case for exercising it deserves much closer examination.

Campaign, no campaign. That is the paradox of an election season in which political activity can outpace public understanding. There are appointments to announce, alliances to celebrate and opponents to attack. But after the speeches, a voter should be able to explain what separates the competing programmes—and what those differences would mean for everyday life.

Consider the Nigeria Democratic Congress. Reports on 26 October detailed its newly constituted National Campaign Council, chaired by Seriake Dickson, with Peter Obi as co-chairman and Ibrahim Abdulkarim as campaign director-general. The party promised a “people-centred and issue-based campaign”. Its appointments establish who will organise the electoral effort. The promised campaign must now establish how its candidates would govern. A persuasive coalition for winning an election is not automatically a coherent coalition for running a country.

The All Progressives Congress faces the same distinction. President Bola Tinubu inaugurated its Presidential Campaign Council on 14 October. According to the State House account, the party’s national chairman called for a contest of ideas, records and policies, acknowledging that the campaign must show how reforms translate into practical improvements in daily life. That is a sound standard. Nigerians should hold the party to it.

Fairness requires us to resist an easy exaggeration: that the opposition has no policies and the governing party offers nothing beyond the word “reform”. The evidence does not support that sweeping dismissal. The more consequential question is whether published commitments have become clear, credible choices that citizens can compare.

The African Democratic Congress unveiled policy proposals in May, after adopting them at its April convention. They included a living wage, independent electoral management, preventive healthcare and a production-driven economy. In August, its Orange Book set out commitments, including abolishing opaque security votes and reducing the cost of governance. These are identifiable positions. They should be examined, not erased for the convenience of an argument.

Examination, however, means going beyond the announcement. What would a living wage mean for public finances, small employers and workers outside formal employment? How would a government replace opaque security spending with arrangements that preserve operational confidentiality while permitting scrutiny? Which expenditure would be cut, by how much and through what authority? A proposal becomes more convincing when its advocates confront its difficulties.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The Allied Peoples’ Movement also publishes positions on security, the rule of law, federalism and foreign policy. Its commitment to genuine federalism invites practical questions: which powers would move, which revenues would follow and which responsibilities would remain shared? Its promise of an efficient security system requires an account of personnel, funding and accountability. These principles provide a starting point. Voters need to see the governing arrangements they would produce.

The APC, meanwhile, has identified subsidy removal, exchange-rate unification, tax reforms and local government autonomy among the achievements it intends to campaign on. It also cites student loans, consumer credit and healthcare initiatives. The question is therefore not whether it has policies. It is whether the results justify renewed confidence — and whether its next programme responds adequately to what has fallen short.

For an incumbent, this is an obligation to account. What was promised? What changed? Who benefited, who bore the costs and what remains unresolved? A programme’s existence cannot establish its effectiveness. Disbursed money does not necessarily create opportunity; a commissioned project does not necessarily sustain a service. Government must show the connection between its actions and the improvements it claims.

“Reform” is especially inadequate as a final answer. It describes a process whose value depends on its consequences. A policy may address a genuine structural problem while being poorly sequenced or insufficiently protective of vulnerable people. Citizens are entitled to question those choices. A household struggling to afford essentials should not have to apologise for asking when adjustment will produce relief. Economic credibility requires both a defensible destination and a convincing account of the journey.

Opposition parties are not exempt from this discipline. Public frustration creates an opportunity to be heard; it does not establish governing competence. Challengers must explain what they would retain, reverse or redesign. Where they promise reversal, they must disclose its costs. Where they accept the broad direction of policy, they must identify the decisions they would change. Otherwise, voters may mistake a change of personnel for a change of programme.

Food provides a useful test. Every party can promise to end hunger. A credible programme must connect farm security, inputs, irrigation, storage, transport and market access. It must also confront the tension between immediate relief for consumers and incentives for producers. Would temporary imports form part of the response? Under what conditions would they end? How would the government prevent emergency measures from becoming permanent privileges for favoured businesses?

Employment promises deserve similarly persistent questioning. Which enterprises will employ the proposed millions of workers? What will those enterprises produce, and who will buy it? Training matters, but a certificate is not a vacancy. Credit matters, but a loan cannot rescue a business with unreliable power and insufficient demand. Candidates should explain how their interventions would support viable enterprises and sustained employment, rather than simply announce large beneficiary targets.

Healthcare exposes the difference between visible projects and functioning government. A hospital building can be photographed. Reliable treatment depends on staff, medicines, maintenance, management, and a way to pay for care. Who will meet those continuing obligations? Education raises the same issue. New classrooms matter, but voters should also hear how teachers will be supported, attendance improved, and learning assessed. Campaign speeches should include the recurring costs of public services alongside capital projects.

Security demands clarity about power and its limits. Candidates advocating decentralised policing should explain recruitment, financing, professional standards and safeguards against political abuse. Those promising better intelligence must address coordination and responsibility when warnings are ignored. Protecting citizens from criminals and from unlawful state coercion are both public obligations. A convincing security programme must take both seriously.

Then comes the question that disciplines every other promise: what will it cost? Parties should distinguish immediate commitments from those dependent on additional revenue. They should identify what they would postpone or discontinue. Savings from waste and corruption cannot serve as an unlimited funding source; they require specific measures and realistic estimates. Borrowing needs a repayment argument. Private investment needs conditions that make it plausible. A campaign that acknowledges limits offers voters a more honest basis for trust.

Personal integrity must also lead to institutional commitments. A leader’s reputation matters, but citizens need arrangements that can expose wrongdoing even when the offender is politically connected. What procurement information would be published? How would oversight bodies obtain records and enforce consequences? Would the proposed safeguards remain effective under a less scrupulous successor? That is the test of reform built to outlast its author.

The media should help make these distinctions unavoidable. Appointments, defections and endorsements are news, but they should not consume the election’s intellectual energy. Every major promise deserves follow-up on financing, authority, implementation and likely obstacles. An interviewer should not accept a second slogan as an answer to a question about the first. Citizens need scrutiny that is consistent across parties and persistent beyond a single broadcast.

A practical demand would be for every serious contender to publish five priority commitments, each with a starting baseline, estimated cost, funding source, responsible institution and deadline. These would give voters a manageable basis for comparison and a record against which to judge the winner. Governors and legislators should face scrutiny commensurate with their offices’ responsibilities.

Nigeria does not need less political enthusiasm. It needs more public understanding to accompany it. Campaign councils can organise the pursuit of office; candidates must explain how they will use that office.

At the end of this election, Nigerians should know more than who joined whom and which rally drew the largest crowd. They should know what their leaders have undertaken to deliver, what sacrifices those choices entail and how failure will be judged.

Until then, there may be campaigns everywhere — and still too little case for governing.

Dakuku Peterside is a leadership and management turnaround expert.

World.title: INEC pledges inclusive voting for PwDs
World.content:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has pledged to strengthen electoral accessibility for persons with disabilities (PwDs) ahead of the 2027 general elections.

The commission said it would provide assistive materials, improve polling unit accessibility and train electoral officials to ensure inclusive participation.

Gombe State Resident Electoral Commissioner, Alhaji Umar Gajiram, gave the assurance on Monday during a sensitisation workshop in Gombe.

Gajiram, represented by the Administrative Secretary, Hajiya Fadimatu Bakari, said every Nigerian deserved equal opportunities to participate in democratic processes.

He stressed that disability should never prevent eligible citizens from exercising their constitutional voting rights.

According to him, INEC recognises that persons with disabilities have equal rights and that their votes, voices and contributions matter.

He said the commission was implementing measures to remove barriers preventing PwDs from participating fully in elections.

These include providing assistive materials, ensuring accessible polling units, training electoral officials and collaborating with disability organisations.

Gajiram stressed that disability inclusion must be integrated into every electoral activity rather than treated as an additional responsibility.

“Disability inclusion should not be treated as an additional responsibility but as an important part of our work,” he said.

He urged Disability Desk Officers (DDOs) to maintain regular engagement with PwDs and communicate their challenges to the commission.

He also encouraged participants to speak openly about their experiences and recommend improvements to electoral arrangements.

“As we look forward to 2027, our goal is simple: to ensure that no eligible Nigerian is left out of the electoral process because of disability,” he said.

He said INEC wanted wheelchair users to access polling units easily and visually impaired voters to receive appropriate assistance.

Similarly, he said, persons with hearing impairments should have access to election information, enabling every eligible voter to participate with dignity and confidence.

Also speaking, Gombe State Chairman of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPwD), Mallam Gambo Ahmad, commended INEC for organising the workshop.

He described the arrangements as exceptional compared with previous engagements, particularly the provision of accessible communication materials.

Ahmad specifically appreciated INEC for providing Braille materials for visually impaired participants and an interpreter for effective communication.

He said the arrangements ensured participants could understand the discussions and contribute meaningfully to the proceedings.

He identified intellectual disabilities, hearing impairments, physical disabilities, visual impairments, spinal cord injuries and leprosy-related disabilities among conditions represented in Gombe.

Others, he said, included persons with albinism, adding that people with different disabilities remained members of the same community.

“We are all part of this community, although we face different challenges,” Ahmad said.

He, however, urged INEC to ensure adequate representation of persons with disabilities among its temporary electoral personnel during the elections.

Ahmad said many PwDs possessed the necessary qualifications and capacity to serve in different electoral positions.

“Some can serve as electoral officers, while others can perform different supporting roles,” he said.

He argued that employing PwDs in election administration would encourage greater participation and strengthen public confidence.

According to him, seeing persons with disabilities administering elections would demonstrate INEC’s commitment to genuine inclusion.

Ahmad urged the commission to sustain and strengthen its disability inclusion initiatives beyond the 2027 general elections.

Also, the Gombe State Director of the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Hajiya Maimuna Abubakar, commended INEC for organising the workshop.

She described the initiative as an important step towards promoting justice and equal opportunities for persons with disabilities.

Abubakar maintained that electoral participation was a fundamental right, not a privilege.

She said every eligible Nigerian, including persons with disabilities, had the right to register, vote and participate in choosing national leaders.

She encouraged PwDs not to isolate themselves because of their conditions but to register and participate actively in elections.

The NOA director also pledged the agency’s readiness to collaborate with INEC in providing necessary information and support.

She said the collaboration would help ensure persons with disabilities were adequately informed and equipped to participate in the electoral process.
