World.title: Video: ‘Let Toluwanisings have a befitting burial’ – Woli Arole makes appeal
World.content:
By Adegboyega Adeleye

Comedian and preacher Woli Arole has appealed to those involved in the burial dispute surrounding late gospel singer Olayemi Bayonile Bolaji, popularly known as Toluwanisings, to allow him a befitting burial, urging them to end what he described as unnecessary public arguments.

Arole made the appeal in a video shared on Instagram on Monday, describing the late singer as a great talent whose death had left friends and colleagues grieving.

“I want to speak on behalf of Toluwanisings’ demise, and this is what God asked me to say. We’ve lost a great guy, a great gift to a generation. Even we, his friends and colleagues, have not recovered. For some of us, he is so close to us, and his death is really painful. A big elephant has gone,” he said.

He also criticised people he accused of using the controversy to attract attention on social media, saying public discussion should instead focus on Toluwanisings’ wife and children.

“It’s saddening and sad that a lot of people are now beginning to want to start to use it as a means for social media traction. You are m***. I have a right to say it. A young man had died in almost his prime, and the discussion is not even about the wife left behind and two kids? No. What you want to start doing is unlicensed, ungoverned, unnecessary talk, interviews and nonsense. A lot of people speaking about him this way never spoke about him while he was alive, about his music, please, please,” Arole said.

He urged those involved to let the burial arrangements proceed and allow the singer to be laid to rest with dignity.

“This is why it is a burden in my spirit, and I have to speak, and this is what the Lord is laying in my heart. The Bible says: Let the dead bury their dead. Whatever process, anything that needs to be done within that corner, let it be done. Let the young man be given a befitting burial,” he said.

Woli Arole added that the burial dispute could not erase the singer’s musical legacy and called on the public to support his family and preserve his work through his children.

“Nobody can ruin his legacy; he lived a good life, please. He sang songs that are eternal; his songs rang in our hearts. Whichever way he is buried, Toluwanisings is in our hearts forever; his sound is forever. So, please, I want to beg us in the name of Jesus, you should focus our energy on what is left: how his legacy will be preserved in his children and the wife,” he said.

He concluded: “God bless Toluwanisings’ legacy, God bless his wife and his children, let the noise and unnecessary nonsense die down in the name of Jesus.”

Toluwanisings’ family announced that the singer died in the early hours of October 14, 2026, but did not disclose the cause of death.

The singer’s burial arrangements have drawn public attention following disagreements over where he should be laid to rest.

Vanguard previously reported that a family representative rejected a cemetery burial and threatened to exhume the singer’s remains if he were buried there. His paternal grandmother also said she opposed a cemetery burial and wanted him buried at his home.

Vanguard News

World.title: US to exclude S. Africa, Rwanda from Africa duty-free trade deal
World.content:
Photo by SAUL LOEB / AFP.

The United States Trade Representative on Monday said Washington would exclude South Africa and Rwanda from a major Africa-US duty-free trade deal, a blow to both economies, over practices “inconsistent” with the deal’s eligibility criteria.

“These concerning and pervasive practices include, but are not limited to, barriers that undermine American trade and investment and practices that pose a threat to US national security and foreign policy interests in the region,” Jamieson Greer said in a statement.

The exclusions will take effect from January 1, the statement said.

The African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA), which grants eligible sub-Saharan African countries preferential access to the US market, has been renewed until the end of 2028, but is reviewed annually.

South Africa is the program’s largest beneficiary but its eligibility has come under scrutiny as Washington steps up criticism of Pretoria, including false allegations of discrimination against white Afrikaners that South Africa rejects.

On Thursday, South Africa’s trade minister said the country hoped for a favorable decision from Washington on the issue, arguing that continued market access would be in the best interest of both countries.

A little over a week earlier, however, South African President Cyril Ramaphosa said the country should “prepare” for an adverse decision.

The US president reviews countries’ eligibility for AGOA annually.

Any removal requires 60 days’ notice to Congress and the country concerned.

South African Trade Minister Parks Tau told reporters in Johannesburg last week that regardless of Trump’s decision on AGOA, his country’s economy would remain stable as it seeks other international markets.

– Increasing pressure on Rwanda –

Washington has been increasing economic pressure on Rwanda over its alleged backing of the armed M23 rebel group in neighboring Democratic Republic of Congo.

Last week, the United States sanctioned the Rwandan defense ministry over those ties, which the Rwandan government denies.

With Rwandan help, the M23 movement has seized swathes of the eastern DRC — home to valuable minerals coveted by world powers — since it took up arms again in 2021.

Rwanda’s foreign minister told AFP last week that his country should not be a “scapegoat” for events in DR Congo.

“The situation in the DRC, the political situation, the security situation, is mainly a Congolese issue,” Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe told AFP on the sidelines of a Russia-Africa summit in Moscow before the US sanctions were imposed.

“Rwanda must not be held as a scapegoat for what is happening in Congo forever,” he added.

World.title: Nigerians, others to face 10-yr wait for UK permanent residency
World.content:
United Kingdom

United Kingdom, UK has revised its proposed immigration reforms, retaining plans to double the waiting period for most migrants seeking permanent settlement from five to 10 years while exempting hundreds of thousands of care workers from the extended requirement.

The revised policy, announced on Monday, follows opposition from trade unions and members of the governing Labour Party over the potential impact of the changes on low-paid foreign workers, particularly those employed in the care sector.

The British government had initially proposed last year that lower-skilled foreign workers should wait between 10 and 15 years before qualifying for permanent residency, officially known as indefinite leave to remain.

However, under the revised arrangements, hundreds of thousands of care workers will be exempt from the longer waiting period, retaining a five-year route to settlement, subject to eligibility requirements.

The exemption is significant for Nigerians working in Britain’s health and social care sector, which relies on foreign workers to fill staffing shortages.

Despite the concessions, the reforms will still double the standard qualifying period for permanent settlement from five to 10 years. The changes, expected to take effect next year, will also apply retrospectively to migrants already living and working in Britain.

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the revised policy was designed to reward migrants who contribute to British society while imposing tougher conditions on those who violate immigration rules.

“Those who contribute most will settle fastest,” Mahmood said. “Those who don’t play by the rules ‌will be refused or wait longer.”

Under the new rules, migrants earning at least £50,271 annually and certain skilled public-sector workers will be eligible to apply for permanent settlement after five years, while those earning more than £125,000 can qualify after three years.

Meanwhile, refugees who entered Britain illegally, particularly those who arrived by small boats, will face significantly longer waiting periods, potentially extending to decades.

The government estimates that despite the exemptions, the reforms will reduce by 500,000 the number of migrants who arrived in Britain from 2021 and would otherwise have qualified for permanent settlement by 2030. As many as 1.4 million migrants are still expected to qualify within the same period under the revised arrangements.

Vanguard News

World.title: NUPRC opens bidding for 40 oil, gas blocks Nov 20
World.content:
File image

By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

The Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) has announced that bidding for 40 oil and gas blocks under its 2026 licensing round will commence on November 20.

The Commission Chief Executive, Mrs Oritsemeyiwa Eyesan, disclosed this on Monday during a roundtable discussion at the 2026 ADIPEC Exhibition and Conference in Abu Dhabi.

The discussion was titled, “Energy Sovereignty in an Interconnected World: Aligning National Priorities, Markets and Global Security.”

In a statement by the Commission, Eyesan urged international investors to take advantage of opportunities in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry, saying improved security, attractive fiscal terms and incentives had made the country more competitive.

She said the Commission would open its bid portal on November 20 and expressed optimism that the investment conditions would attract interested investors.

“We are expecting investors to turn to Nigeria. We are going in for another licensing round and we will be launching our bid portal on November 20. We expect to see interested investors because the environment is a lot more competitive.

“We have set a very attractive fiscal framework for investors. The entire environment is a lot more secure. We have been able to manage costs with a lot of incentives for investors and we expect to see investors take up the offer when we open the portal,” she said.

Eyesan attributed the improvement in Nigeria’s investment climate to the Petroleum Industry Act (PIA), enacted in 2021, and executive orders signed by President Bola Tinubu.

She said the Commission had conducted at least four successful licensing rounds between 2021 and 2026, attracting investments into the country’s oil and gas industry.

According to her, the development marked a departure from the pre-PIA era, when licensing rounds were less frequent, adding that the reforms had strengthened Nigeria’s competitiveness in attracting upstream investments.

On the country’s gas potential, Eyesan said Nigeria had an estimated 215 trillion cubic feet of gas reserves but was producing barely seven billion cubic feet per day, leaving significant opportunities for investors.

She said recently completed and planned gas infrastructure projects would help unlock supplies, improve domestic availability and position Nigeria to serve regional and international markets.

Eyesan cited the Nigeria-Morocco Atlantic Gas Pipeline and the Trans-Sahara Gas Pipeline as two major projects being considered to transport gas to regional markets and Europe.

She said the projects, alongside other infrastructure developments, would help Nigeria meet domestic demand and supply gas to other markets.

The NUPRC chief executive noted that global competition for investment had intensified as more countries discovered petroleum resources and sought to attract international capital.

She said Nigeria was addressing concerns investors consider before committing funds, including execution risks, operating costs, project delays and policy uncertainty.

“We understand that investors will prize execution risk, cost, delays and also uncertainty and so what we have done in Nigeria is to ensure that we guard against these risks and then attract the investment required to enable us unlock the huge resources we sit on,” she said.

World.title: 17 abducted Kaduna worshippers died in captivity – CSW
World.content:
By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo

No fewer than 17 worshippers abducted during an attack on churches in Ariko community, Kachia Local Government Area of Kaduna State, reportedly died in captivity, while eight others were released after spending five months with their abductors, Christian Solidarity Worldwide (CSW), Nigeria, has disclosed.

The Chief Executive Officer of CSW Nigeria, Rev. Dr Yunusa Nmadu, disclosed this during a presentation at ECWA Goodnews Church, Kaduna, to mark the International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church (IDOP).

Nmadu said the victims were among 37 worshippers abducted when gunmen attacked three churches in the community during Sunday services on April 5, 2026.

He said 12 of the abducted worshippers escaped at different times, while 17 died in captivity and eight were eventually released.

Speaking on the theme, “Light in the Darkest Places,” the CSW chief executive also disclosed that 11 people were abducted in Awon village, also in Kachia LGA, on April 20, 2026.

According to him, one of the victims escaped, six were confirmed dead, while four others remained in captivity six months after their abduction and were reportedly in critical condition.

He also recalled the abduction of 177 worshippers from three churches in Kurmin Wali, Kajuru LGA, during Sunday services on January 18, 2026.

Nmadu said the government initially denied the incident but later acknowledged it following interventions by organisations, including CSW.

He said the victims were eventually released after spending 18 days in captivity.

The CSW chief executive described the incidents as part of a disturbing pattern of attacks, killings and mass abductions across Kachia, Kajuru, Kauru, Kagarko and other parts of Kaduna State, which he said had forced thousands of residents to flee their ancestral communities.

He expressed concern that persistent insecurity had restricted freedom of worship in several affected communities, leaving some Christians unable to attend church services without fear of attacks or abduction.

Nmadu alleged that Christians constituted about 99 per cent of victims in several affected communities, adding that religious activities had become increasingly difficult in settlements facing persistent security threats.

He also raised concerns over the alleged treatment of abducted victims, particularly women and children, who he said were subjected to sexual violence, starvation and other inhumane conditions.

According to him, male and female captives were separated into different camps, where their movements were restricted and access to basic necessities, including drinking water, controlled by their abductors.

He alleged that some women, including nursing mothers and elderly women, were repeatedly sexually assaulted, while some who regained their freedom reportedly returned home pregnant.

He added that captives sometimes spent several days without food and had limited access to soap and other basic hygiene materials.

Nmadu also drew attention to the continued captivity of Leah Sharibu, who was abducted in February 2018, describing her case as a reminder of the prolonged ordeal of people held because of their Christian faith.

He further alleged that in some parts of the North-East, Christian passengers were singled out and abducted during attacks on commercial vehicles, while passengers of other religious backgrounds were allowed to go.

Calling for greater solidarity with victims of religious persecution, Nmadu urged Christians to remember those in captivity and support efforts to secure their freedom.

He said CSW had worked in Nigeria for more than 17 years to promote freedom of religion or belief through documentation of human rights violations, support for victims and survivors, training of human rights defenders and engagement with government institutions.

“Behind every report and every statistic is a person: a widow, a child, a pastor, a family who has lost a home or a loved one. They are not numbers to us. They are our brothers and sisters, and when one part of the body suffers, we all suffer with it,” he said.

He urged Christians to remain steadfast in their faith and show solidarity with persecuted believers, drawing inspiration from John 1:5, which says that the light shines in darkness and the darkness has not overcome it.

World.title: CBN appoints eight agents for crude oil exports
World.content:
By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief

The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has appointed eight Pre-Shipment Inspection Agents (PIAs) to monitor the country’s crude oil and gas exports.

The appointments were announced in a circular issued by the Director of Trade and Exchange at the apex bank, Aderinola Shonekan, dated October 28, 2026, and published on the CBN website.

The appointed agents include Trexem Energy Services Limited, assigned to Egina, Qua-Iboe and Tuja terminals; and Dakee Engineering and Construction, which will cover LNG, Escravos (Gas), Bonny River Terminal and EGTL.

Others are Geospace Limited, assigned to Escravos, Odudu and Crawthorne; 617 Limited, covering Bonga, Brass and Usan/Eae; Robinson Energy International Limited, assigned to Ugo-Cha, Pennington, Oyo Aje, Ima and Nembe; and Trobell International Nigeria Limited, covering Forcados, Bonny and Okwori.

Integrated Shipping Services was assigned Akpo, Antan, Okoro, Anyala-Madu and Ebok, while Nephron Business Limited will cover UK Politics, Staple, Yoho, Abo, Agbami, Ajakpa, Okono, Okwok and additional marginal field streams designated by the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC).

The CBN also appointed two Monitoring and Evaluation Agents (MEAs) to supervise the activities of the PIAs. They are Q&Q Control Services and Arlington Security Services.

The circular was addressed to authorised dealer banks, the Nigeria Customs Service, terminal operators, the NUPRC, the Nigerian Midstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission, the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited and oil and gas companies.

The appointments took effect from the date of the circular, October 28, 2026.

World.title: UNICROSS in turmoil as ASUU resumes strike after 104-day suspension
World.content:
By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR

The Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, University of Cross River State (UNICROSS) chapter, on Monday, resumed its strike after 104 days, accusing the government of failing to honour agreements that ended the last one.

The chapter Chairman, Dr Patrick Ushie, who disclosed this in an interview with Vanguard in Calabar, said the decision to resume the strike was taken at a union meeting today (Monday) following the government’s failure to honour agreements that led to the suspension of the industrial action on July 21, 2026.

His words: “It is true that we have resumed the strike we initially called off on July 21 following a series of meetings with the government and its representatives.

“However, certain agreements reached before the suspension have not been implemented as agreed by the government.

“They have not only breached the timelines for implementation but have also failed to respond to our notices.

“This time around, we are not going to suspend or call off the strike until our grievances are addressed,” he said.

Recall that the UNICROSS chapter of ASUU embarked on an indefinite strike on May 19, 2026, over welfare concerns and the non-implementation of agreements reached with the union’s national body.

The union had listed 11 demands as the basis for the industrial action, including the implementation of the salary structure and other welfare benefits of academic staff.

Other demands included the immediate implementation of the non-financial components of the 2025 ASUU-Federal Government renegotiated agreement and increased government funding for the university.

The union also demanded prompt payment of monthly salaries not later than the third day of each succeeding month.

It further called for the payment of outstanding salaries and arrears of the 35 per cent and 25 per cent wage awards implemented in public universities since January 2023.

The union also demanded the remittance of outstanding check-off dues owed to ASUU-UniCross and its national body since 2017, amounting to N11.9 million, as well as deductions for December 2024 and November 2025.

Other outstanding demands included the payment of promotion arrears and earned academic allowances accrued between July 2011 and December 2017 under the 2009 Federal Government-ASUU agreement.

World.title: INEC Sensitises Adamawa PWDs Ahead of 2027 Polls
World.content:
Daji Sani in Yola

The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has organized a one-day sensitization programme for Persons with Disabilities (PWDs) in Yola ahead of the forthcoming national elections.

The sensitization workshop, held on Monday in Yola, was aimed at educating PWDs on the electoral process and addressing barriers they face during elections.

Speaking at the event, the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) for Adamawa State, Alhaji Nura Mohammad, said the commission is committed to ensuring that no eligible voter is disenfranchised on account of disability.

He said the workshop was designed to educate PWDs on their rights and to prepare them to overcome challenges usually encountered at polling units during elections.

“We are ready to provide accessibility to all people with disabilities to polling units where they are to cast their votes,” the REC said, adding that INEC is aware of various forms of disabilities and has made adequate provisions.

According to him, the commission has educated participants on the need to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) before proceeding to their respective polling units to vote.

He disclosed that INEC has made available Braille ballot guides for voters with visual impairments, as well as magnifying glasses, while Form EC30 PWD with written instructions and posters has been provided for those with hearing impairments.

The REC further noted that the commission is in partnership with Organizations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) and Cluster Heads who now serve as a bridge between institutional provisions and community awareness for voters with disabilities.

Speaking to journalists after the workshop, the Chairman of the Joint National Association of Persons with Disabilities (JONAPWD), Sani Sabo, thanked INEC for considering the plight of PWDs in its preparations for the elections.

Represented by his Vice-Chairman, Mohammad Dalatu, Sabo said the association will take the sensitization to the grassroots to educate its members, adding: “We are happy that INEC has taken us into consideration and we will come out to vote.”

World.title: Paciencia X Cute Saint: A Shared Vision Of Craftsmanship at Lagos Fashion Week 2026
World.content:
Paciencia brings handcrafted artistry to Cute Saint’s ‘MO SA, MO WO’ collection in a collaboration rooted in creativity, craftsmanship and storytelling.

Some of fashion’s most remarkable collaborations begin not with a sketch, but with a conversation. For Paciencia and Cute Saint, it was a series of creative exchanges that brought two distinct design perspectives together on the runway at Lagos Fashion Week 2026.

Presenting his latest collection, ‘MO SA, MO WO’ — ‘I Ran, I Watched,’ Femi Ajose, founder and creative director of Cute Saint, collaborated with Joy Fache James, founder and creative director of Paciencia, to create a series of uniquely handcrafted handbags designed exclusively to complement the collection.

The partnership was the result of numerous artistic meetings between both founders, during which ideas were exchanged, concepts refined and design possibilities explored. Every conversation brought them closer to a shared understanding of how the handbags could become part of the collection’s visual narrative rather than simply accessories accompanying the garments.

For James, whose work at Paciencia centres on the art of handmade bags, the collaboration presented an opportunity to explore craftsmanship through another designer’s creative lens while retaining the individuality that defines her brand.

Working closely with Ajose, she developed handbag designs that reflected the character, mood and artistic direction of ‘MO SA, MO WO.’ The resulting pieces brought their own identity to the runway while remaining in conversation with Cute Saint’s designs.

The collaboration also found a natural connection with this year’s Lagos Fashion Week theme, ‘Crafted.’ Beyond the finished garments and accessories, it drew attention to the creative process itself: the time spent developing ideas, the hands involved in bringing them to life and the thoughtful decisions that give each piece its character.

In an industry often driven by what comes next, Paciencia and Cute Saint chose to celebrate what goes into making something meaningful.

The handbags were not an afterthought. They were part of the collection’s development, shaped through the same creative dialogue that informed the overall runway presentation. This approach allowed both designers to bring their individual strengths into a unified expression of contemporary Nigerian fashion.

For Paciencia, the showcase marked another expression of its commitment to creating handbags that carry more than personal belongings. Each design reflects a dedication to artistry, individuality and the enduring appeal of things made by hand.

At its heart, the collaboration between Ajose and James was a meeting of creative minds, built on mutual respect for design and the understanding that fashion becomes richer when different forms of craftsmanship come together.

On October 29, as Cute Saint’s ‘MO SA, MO WO’ collection took to the Lagos Fashion Week runway, Paciencia’s handcrafted pieces became part of that story, demonstrating how a handbag can contribute to the language, emotion and identity of a collection.

Two designers. Two creative perspectives. One shared commitment to the art of making.

And in a season dedicated to all things ‘Crafted,’ that shared commitment was a story worth telling.

Founded by Joy Fache James, Paciencia is a fashion accessories brand specialising in uniquely handcrafted handbags. Rooted in creativity, craftsmanship and individuality, the brand approaches every design as an opportunity to bring artistry and function together, creating pieces with distinctive character and timeless appeal.

Founded by Femi Ajose, Cute Saint is a Nigerian fashion label known for its expressive design language and artistic approach to contemporary fashion. Through distinctive collections and thoughtful storytelling, the brand continues to explore fashion as a medium for creativity and personal expression.

World.title: Army, DSS Arrest Suspected Kidnapper While Collecting N200,000 Ransom in Nasarawa
World.content:
Troops of the Nigerian Army, in collaboration with operatives of the Department of State Services (DSS), have arrested a suspected kidnapper while collecting a N200,000 ransom from a female resident in Nasarawa State.

The suspect, identified as Mukaila Iliyasu, was arrested at Akwaba in Eggon Local Government Area of the state during a joint security operation involving troops of Sector 2, Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke, and DSS operatives.

The arrest followed intelligence reports that Iliyasu had allegedly threatened to abduct a woman unless she paid the sum of N200,000.

The Acting Media Information Officer of the Joint Task Force Operation Whirl Stroke, Lieutenant Ahmad Zubairu Zubairu, confirmed the arrest in a statement.

According to the statement, DSS operatives alerted the military to the alleged threat on October 29, prompting the deployment of a coordinated operation to track down the suspect and prevent the planned abduction.

As part of the operation, a soldier reportedly went undercover and posed as the person assigned to deliver the ransom.

The suspect was subsequently apprehended while collecting the money, with security operatives recovering N200,000 believed to be the ransom demanded from the intended victim.

The military described the operation as a successful intelligence-led intervention that prevented a possible kidnapping and underscored the importance of cooperation among security agencies in tackling criminal activities.

Following his arrest, Iliyasu was handed over to the DSS for further investigation and possible prosecution.

The Force Commander of Operation Whirl Stroke and General Officer Commanding 5 Division of the Nigerian Army, Major General Moses Kolo Gara, commended the troops and DSS operatives for their professionalism, courage and effective coordination.

Gara urged security personnel to sustain their collaboration and strengthen intelligence sharing to tackle kidnapping and other security threats across their areas of responsibility.

He also emphasised the need for continued inter-agency cooperation to protect lives, safeguard communities and maintain peace in the region.

World.title: 184.5kg Cocaine Trial: KC Luxury Seeks Judge’s Recusal Over Court Record Irregularities
World.content:
Wale Igbintade

Businessman and social media influencer, Afolabi Kazeem, popularly known as KC Luxury, standing trial over alleged 184.5 kilogrammes of cocaine trafficking and money laundering, has asked Justice Musa Kakaki of the Federal High Court in Lagos to recuse himself from the case over alleged irregularities in court records and his deteriorating health.

Kazeem, through his counsel, Chief Emefo Etudo, accused the court of failing to reflect its October 28, 2026 ruling on his client’s bail application in the record of proceedings and alleged that a reply affidavit filed by the defence had gone missing.

The application for the judge’s recusal followed the court’s refusal last Wednesday to grant Kazeem bail on medical grounds, with Justice Kakaki holding that the defendant had failed to establish special circumstances or provide sufficient evidence to justify his release.

At the resumed proceedings on Monday, Kazeem, who was absent from court, sought the judge’s withdrawal through Etudo, who appeared alongside Mrs Charity Etudo.

The senior lawyer told the court that repeated efforts to obtain a copy of the October 28 ruling from the court registry had proved unsuccessful.

According to him, the defence was informed that the ruling had yet to be signed by the judge, a development he said could prejudice his client’s right to appeal within the prescribed period.

Etudo also expressed concern over the alleged disappearance of a reply affidavit filed by the defence, questioning the safety of documents submitted to the court.

He said, “The record of proceedings did not reflect that any ruling was made on October 28, 2026, by this honourable court. And we don’t feel so safe that our evidence, like the reply affidavit that got missing, is safe in the court.”

He further criticised the Federal High Court’s inadequate recording facilities, arguing that the provision of verbatim recording equipment would ensure that statements, submissions and decisions made during proceedings were accurately captured.

Etudo maintained that the alleged discrepancies in the court records had further eroded his client’s confidence in the judicial process.

The lawyer also questioned the prosecution’s evidence, insisting that the documents tendered before the court did not establish a connection between the first, second and third defendants and the alleged offences.

He disclosed that he intended to file a separate application challenging the sufficiency of the prosecution’s evidence but wanted the court to first determine the recusal application.

Opposing the request to take the application immediately, prosecution counsel, Ibrahim Abu, argued that the matter was scheduled for trial and that the defence had failed to explain the absence of the first defendant.

Abu said the prosecution had six witnesses in court and was ready to commence the trial in compliance with the court’s earlier directive for accelerated hearing.

He also informed the court that he was served with the recusal application during the stand-down and argued that it was not ripe for hearing.

The prosecution requested five days to respond to the application instead of the seven days ordinarily allowed under the rules.

Abu further described allegations of judicial bias as serious, insisting that the court had been fair to all parties.

He argued that the trial had not commenced and that the refusal of bail could not, in itself, establish bias against the judge.

“Refusal of bail is the discretion of the court. That is not bias. There is an opportunity to appeal the decision, which has not been taken,” he said.

The prosecution also opposed the suggestion to sever the charges, arguing that the first count involved an allegation of conspiracy among the defendants.

However, counsel to the second defendant, Augustine Audu, SAN, urged the court to hear and determine the recusal application before proceeding with the trial.

Audu, who confirmed that his client was also served with the application during the stand-down, said the pending proceedings had stalled the trial and undermined the purpose of the accelerated hearing order.

He urged the prosecution to amend the charge and separate the defendants to enable the second and third defendants to proceed with their trial independently of Kazeem.

According to him, his client should not continue to suffer the consequences of proceedings involving another defendant, particularly when he was willing to face trial and clear his name.

“We do not want the fate of the second and third defendants to be tied to the first defendant, because we are stuck,” he said.

The senior advocate argued that the conspiracy count did not prevent the prosecution from proceeding against some defendants while others were unavailable.

“The fate of the second and third defendants cannot be left hanging. The first count is conspiracy, and people can be tried while others are at large,” he submitted.

Audu also urged the court to consider bail for the second and third defendants, maintaining that they should not remain in custody while the first defendant’s application stalled the proceedings.

He, however, said he would not oppose the recusal application, noting that it was a matter between the first defendant and the prosecution.

Responding, Etudo said he had reluctantly filed the application because his client had lost confidence in the court.

“My client has lost confidence in this court, and that is why I have had to bring this application, although I was reluctant to do so,” he said.

The defence counsel also raised fresh concerns about Kazeem’s health, disclosing that his condition had deteriorated.

To illustrate his concerns, Etudo recounted a previous case at the Ikeja High Court in which he had sought the release of a client suffering from prostate cancer to enable him to obtain medical treatment.

He said the court declined the application and the defendant died before the next adjourned date.

Etudo said the experience informed his apprehension about Kazeem’s deteriorating health and the possible consequences of keeping him in custody.

He maintained that his client was in a sorry state and no longer had confidence in the court.

Justice Kakaki adjourned the case until November 25, 2026, for the hearing of submissions on the application.

World.title: Former Kwara APC Guber Aspirant Doles out N4bn Empowerment Package to Support Residents, Tinubu’s Re-election Bid
World.content:
A leading former governorship aspirant of All Progressives Congress(APC) in Kwara State, Ambassador Yahaya Seriki, at the weekend in Ilorin doled out over N4billion empowerment package to support the residents of the state ahead of 2027 general elections.

Seriki, a founder and Managing Director of Kursi Investments Limited, Abuja said that, “the empowerment programme is also meant to ensure the re-election of President Ahmned Bola Tinubu and vice president, Kashim Shettima in 2027 elections in Kwara State”.

Seriki disclosed this in Ilorin while unveiling the empowerment package titled, “Yahaya Seriki Empowerment and Enterprise Colloquium” held in Ilorin, the state capital.

The package comprises N1bn in cash and about N3.2bn worth of equipment and other items, including 150 vehicles, modern sewing machines and others.

He said that, the empowerment package was designed to help beneficiaries improve their livelihoods and achieve economic independence.

He said the programme was motivated by his desire to give back to society and create opportunities for people to make progress through different means of livelihood.

“The purpose of this empowerment is to help people progress in their own way. All I am doing is giving back to the society that brought me this far,” he said.

“When God blesses you and you have enough, failing to make other people smile means you are poor in spirit. Making other people happy is something I strongly believe in and enjoy doing.”

He said he believed that individuals who had attained financial success should use their resources to improve the lives of others and provide opportunities for those who needed support.

On the 2027 elections, the APC guber aspirant declared his support for the re-election of President Bola Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima, describing the President’s policies as necessary for Nigeria’s development.

“This empowerment programme is in support of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. I believe we have never had it this good in the history of Nigeria.

“We have a President who believes in building a better country and changing the narrative for the better,” he said.

Seriki urged Nigerians, particularly young people, to support Tinubu’s second-term ambition, insisting that the country should rally behind the President.

Also speaking at the event, the senator representing Kwara Central senatorial district at the Upper House and now the PDP senatorial candidate for 2027, Senator Saliu Mustapha lauded the humanitarian gestures of Ambassador Seriki for the teeming masses of the state.

He said, “My brother, Ambassador Yahaya Seriki-Gambari, today demonstrated yet again his remarkable commitment to humanity through a one-of-its-kind empowerment programme, during which he distributed vehicles, tools and equipment for artisans, and other valuable items worth billions of naira.

“This is certainly not his first intervention of this magnitude, and I sincerely hope and pray that it will not be his last.

“For me, this is particularly heartwarming because it reflects a philosophy of service that I have consistently believed in and practised over the years, first through the Saliu Mustapha Foundation and now under the auspices of my office as the Senator representing the Kwara Central Senatorial District.

“Time and again, I have challenged my principal rival in the forthcoming senatorial election to point to just one tangible, enduring contribution he made to infrastructure or human capital development before assuming public office.

“Something verifiable, something impactful, something that has stood the test of time. Till today, neither he nor his supporters have provided a convincing answer to that challenge.

“And therein lies the fundamental difference between those who have invested their personal resources, time and energy in uplifting people and communities long before seeking public office, and those whose claim to public relevance began only after political power was handed to them on a platter.

“More often than not, the difference in these backgrounds becomes even more evident in the quality of leadership and the outcomes they deliver while in office.

“Once again, I heartily congratulate my brother, Ambassador Abdulfatai Yahaya Seriki-Gambari, on this remarkable milestone of generosity and service to humanity”.

Senator Mustapha added, “To all the beneficiaries, there is a clear thin line between luck and opportunity. I urge you to make the most of these opportunities, put the items received to productive use, improve your livelihoods, and contribute meaningfully to the development of our society”.

A Human Rights activist, Mr.. Deji Adeyanju in his remarks urged young Nigerians to embrace discipline, patience and delayed gratification, stressing that financial assistance should be used responsibly.

He warned that spending money meant for business development on expensive phones and other luxury items could undermine beneficiaries’ financial future.

Nigerian fashion designer and founder of Vodi Group, Seyi Vodi, in his remarks at the event said that, providing vocational tools and equipment was a more sustainable form of empowerment than distributing cash without proper assessment of beneficiaries.

“The best form of grant is empowerment through skill acquisition tools. You don’t just give people grants or empowerment without first doing due diligence. You don’t pluck money from a tree. Money doesn’t come easily,” he said.

Recounting his entrepreneurial journey, Vodi said his first monthly allowance as a National Youth Service Corps member was N3,600, which he used to start a small trading business.

He recalled travelling to Aba market to purchase boxers, which he resold to fellow corps members at a profit, adding that the experience taught him to identify business opportunities and reinvest available resources.

The fashion designer said it took him more than 26 years of hard work, discipline and gradual business expansion to attain his current level of success.

“For my business, we grew step by step. It took me almost 26 years and more to get here,” he said.

Vodi urged beneficiaries to invest empowerment funds and equipment in productive ventures rather than spending them on luxury items, warning that poor financial decisions could undermine their prospects of building sustainable businesses.

“You have to be prudent. You need money to scale up your business. A beneficiary who receives an industrial machine can multiply it in the coming years if they are prudent,” he said.

Senator Yahaya Oloriegbe also described the empowerment initiative as an opportunity to support the progress and development of Kwara State, expressing confidence in the capacity of such interventions to improve people’s livelihoods.

World.title: ESDIAC Launches Mobile Platform, Offers Lower International Call Rates
World.content:
Oghenevwede Ohwovoriole in Abuja

A technology service provider ESDIAC has launched a mobile platform to give Nigerians lower call rates and connectivity both in calls and data with the promise of offering the lowest rates in international calls.

The Chief Executive Officer of ESDIAC, Austin Ugbebor speaking at a media engagement on Friday in Abuja, said that the platform will integrates Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) calling, electronic SIM (eSIM), mobile airtime and data top-up services.

Ugbebor said, the platform was designed to easy the financial burden of expensive international calls that Nigerians bore. And yay ESDIAC, was designed to address the challenges of expensive international calls and limited connectivity options, particularly for people travelling abroad.

“ESDIAC is an all-in-one solution, offering international and local calls, eSIM services and data packages through a single platform.

“With our platform, subscribers can make calls to Canada, United Kingdom, US, Germany, Australia for as low as N13.

“ESDIAC’s VoIP technology enables subscribers to call people who do not have the ESDIAC application or an internet connection, and calls can be made directly to regular telephone numbers,” he said.

He said the service also allows users to retain their phone numbers when making calls, making it easier for recipients to identify callers.

The CEO added that the platform provided mobile airtime and data top-ups, while its eSIM service enabled travelers to access connectivity in supported destinations without necessarily purchasing a physical SIM card.

He added that the company was committed to offering affordable services and improving the calling experience by addressing connectivity challenges associated with internet-based communication platforms.

On concerns about tariff stability and consumer protection, Ugbebor said the company has adopted a policy of respecting subscribers’ money by avoiding hidden connectivity charges.

“Subscribers will not be charged additional fees merely for initiating calls, and unused balances will remain available to customers.”

He said subscribers who believed they had been wrongly charged could contact the company’s customer service team for investigation.

“If you are right and there is an error, we promise to refund your money,” he said.

According to him, ESDIAC operated under the regulatory requirements of the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) and the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) in the United States.

But however, he noted that changes in telecommunications tariffs could sometimes result from regulatory directives, adding that operators were required to comply with applicable regulations.

Mr Tope Fasua, Special Adviser to the President on Economic Matters, Office of the Vice-President, described the platform as a promising development for Nigeria’s telecommunications sector.

Fasua said his experience with an expensive eSIM purchased during an international trip, which failed to provide connectivity across all his destinations, underscored the need for more reliable and affordable services.

He expressed hope that ESDIAC would provide better value to travellers through its services.

Mr Adoga Ibrahim, Government Liaison Officer for ESDIAC, said the company was bringing to Nigeria a fully developed Nigerian-owned product to the telecom market. And commended the NCC for its cooperation and professionalism in granting the company the required operating license recently,while expressing confidence that ESDIAC would deliver quality services to Nigerians.

The company’s Legal Adviser, Mr Aja Nwaani, said the protection of subscribers’ personal information was central to its operations.

“ESDIAC has put measures in place to ensure that subscribers’ information are not improperly accessed, disclosed or used, including when shared with third-party carriers and service providers,” he said.

He said the company was committed to complying with the Nigeria Data Protection Act and applicable regulations, warning against the unlawful sale or misuse of subscribers’ personal information.

Human Resources representative of ESDIAC, Mohammed Sani said the platform was particularly useful to travellers and Nigerians seeking to maintain affordable communication with family members and business associates abroad.

World.title: 2027: Why Adeola Stands Out as the Candidate to Beat in Ogun
World.content:
Femi Ogbonnikan

There is, as yet, no compelling reason for the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to review the list of governorship candidates for the 2027 general election.

This is without prejudice to the case instituted by the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ogun State, Oladipupo Adebutu, challenging his alleged exclusion from the final list recently released by the commission.

Adebutu and his counterpart in Gombe State, Professor Isa Pantami, were conspicuously missing from the portal. While the legal implications of their absence remain subject to judicial determination, the development has inevitably introduced another dimension to the unfolding political contest in Ogun State.

It is often said that the legitimacy of a candidate in an election is only as strong as the health of the political platform on which he seeks the people’s mandate.

This is particularly relevant to Adebutu’s predicament. His decision to seek the PDP ticket, despite the persistent crisis and internal contradictions within the party, suggests a failure to appreciate the political landmines that could undermine his ambition long before the electorate has an opportunity to decide his fate.

The consequences could be far-reaching.

Unless the court decides otherwise, Adebutu may not appear on the ballot, leaving his political future hanging in the balance.

For a politician who has invested considerable resources and political capital in pursuing the Ogun governorship, such an outcome would represent a serious setback.

This is a potential double whammy for the opposition. First, the contest could be significantly altered by the absence of a major opposition candidate.

Second, the PDP, already weakened by internal divisions and the struggle for political relevance, could find itself further disorganised, particularly if Adebutu’s camp loses its rallying point.

It would be another reminder that political ambition cannot thrive indefinitely on the misfortunes of others or the assumption that opponents can be weakened without strengthening one’s own political foundation.

However, there is nothing to gloat about. Adebutu’s alleged exclusion neither enhances nor diminishes Adeola’s credentials as a candidate. The APC flag bearer must be judged on his own record, political standing, experience, capacity to govern and the confidence he can inspire among the electorate.

The 2027 election is not an automatic victory waiting to happen. It is a contest that must be earned through convincing arguments, effective mobilisation and a demonstrable capacity to deliver.

On these considerations, Senator Solomon Olamilekan Adeola, popularly known as Yayi, occupies a particularly strong position.

Indeed, what distinguishes Adeola from several contenders is not merely his standing as the candidate of the ruling APC or the institutional advantage that comes with being backed by a party controlling the federal and state governments. It is the depth of his political experience, his understanding of legislative and executive processes, his extensive political network and the strategic influence he has acquired through years of public service.

Unlike a politician whose political relevance is largely confined to election cycles, Adeola has built a career through successive electoral contests and increasingly demanding responsibilities. His political journey, which began in the Lagos State House of Assembly, took him to the House of Representatives and subsequently to the Senate. He represented Alimosho Constituency in the Lagos Assembly for eight years, served Alimosho Federal Constituency in the House of Representatives and later represented Lagos West Senatorial District before moving to Ogun West. This progression is significant because it demonstrates an ability to operate at different levels of government and build political relationships across constituencies.

It also provides him with an understanding of governance that goes beyond campaign promises. Having spent years participating in lawmaking, budgetary processes, constituency representation and national policy discussions, Adeola understands the institutional machinery through which government programmes are conceived, funded and implemented. This experience is an important asset in a state as economically strategic and administratively complex as Ogun.

His current position as Chairman of the Senate Committee on Appropriations further strengthens this argument. The committee occupies a strategic position in the nation’s fiscal architecture, overseeing the budgetary process through which national priorities are translated into financial commitments. The position offers Adeola an intimate understanding of public finance, resource allocation, project financing and the relationship between policy objectives and available resources.

For a state seeking to consolidate its economic potential, these are not insignificant credentials. Ogun requires a governor who understands not only how to attract investments but also how to mobilise resources, establish priorities, manage competing demands and ensure that public expenditure produces measurable benefits. Adeola’s legislative experience and exposure to national budgetary processes give him a useful foundation for addressing these challenges.

More importantly, his position places him in a strategic relationship with the federal government and other national institutions. In a federation where states must constantly negotiate for federal interventions, infrastructure support, investment partnerships and policy cooperation, the ability to navigate the corridors of national decision-making is a considerable advantage.

Ogun is not an ordinary state. Its geographical proximity to Lagos, extensive industrial base, agricultural resources, border communities, expanding urban centres and international boundaries give it enormous economic possibilities.

Yet, converting these advantages into sustainable prosperity requires more than political popularity. It requires strategic planning, institutional understanding and the ability to connect state development priorities with opportunities at the federal level.

This is where Adeola’s experience becomes particularly relevant.

Another factor that distinguishes him is his political reach beyond Ogun West, the senatorial district he currently represents. Although his emergence from Ogun West gives the district a historic opportunity to produce the next governor, his political ambition must necessarily be statewide.

His years in Lagos politics, combined with his subsequent political engagement in Ogun, have provided him with networks and relationships that extend beyond a single constituency.

His electoral calculations, therefore, are not limited to the traditional political strongholds of Ogun West. The real test is his ability to consolidate support in Ogun Central and Ogun East while maintaining the enthusiasm of his home base.

His legislative profile, party structure and relationships with political stakeholders provide a platform for pursuing that objective.

There is also the question of political acceptability. Winning a governorship election in Ogun requires a candidate capable of appealing to different interests, communities and political tendencies.

The state has a sophisticated electorate with competing expectations shaped by its commercial importance, educational heritage, industrial development and complex political history. A candidate must demonstrate the capacity to bring these interests together.

Adeola’s political experience across Lagos and Ogun gives him an opportunity to build such a coalition. His task is to translate his existing political relationships into a broad-based movement that cuts across the three senatorial districts, local governments, traditional institutions, professional groups, business communities and the youth population.

His emergence as the APC candidate also places him in a position to benefit from the party’s existing political structures. But party machinery alone cannot win an election.

The APC must convince voters that its candidate represents continuity in areas where the administration has performed creditably and a credible opportunity for improvement where expectations remain unmet.

This distinction is important because the 2027 election will inevitably become a referendum on the direction of Ogun State. Voters will assess the achievements of the outgoing administration, the quality of its infrastructure, its economic policies, its handling of social welfare and the prospects of sustaining ongoing development projects.

Adeola must therefore demonstrate how his experience and legislative influence can complement the development agenda already established in the state. His argument should not simply be that he belongs to the ruling party, but that he possesses the experience, institutional access and political capacity to consolidate existing gains while introducing fresh ideas to address emerging challenges.

The economy will be another decisive consideration. Ogun’s development prospects are increasingly tied to industrial expansion, infrastructure, agriculture, transportation, technology and private-sector investment. The state has the potential to become one of Nigeria’s leading economic centres, but that potential must be supported by reliable infrastructure, a predictable business environment, efficient public institutions and policies that create employment opportunities.

Adeola’s legislative background offers him an opportunity to articulate a development strategy that connects these sectors. His experience in national budgeting should enable him to approach the state’s financial challenges with a clearer appreciation of revenue generation, expenditure management, capital investment and fiscal sustainability.

Furthermore, his political relationship with President Bola Tinubu and the APC leadership could become an important factor in attracting federal attention to Ogun’s development priorities. While such relationships cannot substitute for sound governance, they can facilitate cooperation between the state and federal governments, particularly in areas requiring large-scale infrastructure investment and national policy coordination.

However, the most compelling argument for Adeola must ultimately be about the people. The electorate is becoming increasingly demanding. Political loyalty cannot indefinitely replace performance, and impressive political connections will mean little if they do not translate into better living conditions.

Roads, schools, hospitals, employment opportunities, affordable transportation, agricultural development and improved security remain central to the expectations of ordinary citizens.

Adeola must therefore take his campaign beyond political endorsements and elite consensus. He must explain how his administration intends to improve the quality of life across Ogun, including communities that have yet to experience the full benefits of the state’s economic expansion. His legislative experience should be translated into a practical programme of governance that addresses the needs of urban and rural communities alike.

The strength of his candidacy will also depend on his ability to manage the expectations of the APC family. The party’s nomination is only the beginning of the political journey. Reconciliation, inclusion and effective mobilisation will be essential to preventing internal grievances from becoming opportunities for the opposition. A governorship candidate must be capable of carrying the party along, not merely commanding its ticket.

This is particularly important in Ogun, where political alignments and local interests can significantly influence electoral outcomes. Adeola must demonstrate that his candidacy represents an opportunity for all tendencies within the APC and not the exclusive political project of a particular group. The wider the coalition he builds, the stronger his prospects of translating party dominance into electoral victory.

For the opposition, the challenge is equally formidable. It must present a candidate with sufficient political credibility, organisational strength and a convincing alternative development agenda. If Adebutu eventually fails to secure his place on the ballot, the opposition will have to contend with the additional difficulty of reorganising its political machinery and convincing its supporters to rally behind another candidate.

But even if he returns to the contest through judicial intervention, Adeola’s electoral prospects will still have to be determined by the quality of the campaign and the choices of the electorate.

The lesson from the unfolding development is that political fortunes are shaped not only by the strength of individual ambitions but also by the stability of the platforms on which those ambitions rest. Adebutu’s predicament, if sustained by the courts, would illustrate the danger of underestimating the consequences of party instability. But it would be equally misleading to assume that the difficulties of an opponent automatically translate into victory.

Adeola’s advantage, therefore, must be located in the strength of his own political credentials. He has accumulated legislative experience, developed national political relationships, occupied a strategic position in the country’s budgetary process and established a political presence that gives him a considerable head start in the unfolding contest.

These are significant assets that distinguish him from a number of those seeking the same office.

Ultimately, the 2027 Ogun governorship election will be decided by the electorate, not by political calculations in Abuja, the fortunes of opposition parties or the outcome of internal party disputes alone.

Adeola must earn the confidence of the people through a clear vision, credible commitments and a compelling demonstration of his readiness to govern.

But on the strength of his experience, institutional standing, political networks and the opportunities available to the ruling party, he enters the race as a formidable contender and arguably the candidate to beat. The challenge before him is to convert these advantages into a statewide electoral coalition and convince Ogun voters that his candidacy represents not just a continuation of political power, but an opportunity to accelerate the state’s development.

*Ogbonnikan writes from Okeagbede, in Imeko-Afon LGA of Ogun state

World.title: CBM Dismisses Claims of Electoral Interference, Says Membership Registration Voluntary
World.content:
The City Boy Movement (CBM) has dismissed reports suggesting that its ongoing membership registration exercise is linked to or interferes with Nigeria’s electoral process, insisting that the exercise is entirely voluntary and separate from the Independent National Electoral Commission’s (INEC) statutory voter registration.

The Movement said its registration was strictly for building its membership database, strengthening its organisational structures and coordinating activities, stressing that its membership forms and cards could neither confer voting rights nor serve as substitutes for official INEC voter registration documents.

In a statement by its Deputy Director-General, Media, Communication and Public Affairs, O’tega Ogra, CBM said registration was open to existing members and Nigerians willing to join the organisation voluntarily.

It disclosed that interested individuals could register physically or through its official website, www.cbmnigeria.org.

The Movement stressed that its membership registration and INEC’s voter registration served different purposes, noting that the electoral commission remained constitutionally responsible for registering eligible voters and maintaining the national register of voters.

According to CBM, registration with the organisation does not confer voting eligibility, amend anyone’s details in INEC’s register or replace any requirement prescribed by the electoral commission.

It also explained that its membership forms and cards were not electoral registration documents or substitutes for Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs).

“The existence of a membership register does not, by itself, establish interference with or manipulation of the electoral register,” the statement said.

CBM further maintained that participation in its activities was entirely voluntary, adding that individuals remained free to decline membership, withdraw from the organisation or exercise independent political and electoral choices.

It said no Nigerian was being coerced or compelled to register with the Movement, insisting that it neither impersonated INEC nor misrepresented the purpose of its registration exercise.

The organisation also rejected suggestions that its activities interfered with the electoral rights of Nigerians, maintaining that its operations were conducted within the framework of applicable laws.

On concerns surrounding the collection of personal information during registration, CBM said protecting members’ data remained an important obligation of the organisation.

It assured Nigerians that personal information collected during the exercise would be processed fairly, lawfully and transparently, with appropriate safeguards against unauthorised access, use or disclosure.

The Movement added that members of the public participating in the exercise would receive information from its officers regarding how their personal data were processed and their applicable privacy rights.

It also maintained that any consent required under the law would be freely given, specific and informed.

CBM said it welcomed legitimate enquiries, lawful criticism and evidence-based scrutiny of its activities, urging anyone with specific concerns or evidence of misconduct to report through its verified official communication channels.

It pledged to review complaints fairly and cooperate with lawful investigations while respecting the rights of complainants and individuals against whom allegations might be made.

World.title: Google launches FREE AI, digital skills hub in SA with isiZulu and isiXhosa support
World.content:
The new African skills hub has also been designed with connectivity challenges in mind. Image: Pixabay

Google has launched a free online learning hub aimed at expanding access to artificial intelligence (AI) and digital skills across Africa, including South Africa.

Called Skilling Africa with Google, the new platform brings more than 15 training initiatives together in one place.

“Today, more than 90% of companies across the region report a critical deficit in AI-ready professionals,” the tech giant said on Monday.



“[The] new learning hub [is] designed to expand access to digital and AI skills, equipping three million people across the continent by 2030.”

Google said the initiative builds on its existing training programmes, which have already provided foundational digital training to more than seven million young Africans.

Free digital training at your fingertips

The hub gives learners access to a range of courses and programmes, including Google Career Certificates, Hustle Academy and Google Cloud Skills.

These cover everything from IT support, data analytics and cybersecurity to entrepreneurship and cloud technology.

Learners can also access bite-sized modules covering AI, career development and other technical skills.

Getting started requires a Google account, with one-click sign-in available. There is no need to download an app.



Google said the platform is entirely free and open to everyone, from students and entrepreneurs to developers and IT professionals.

AI learning platform adds African language support

The new hub has also been designed with connectivity challenges in mind.

Users can download lessons while connected to Wi-Fi and complete them offline. The platform is also optimised for low-bandwidth connections and entry-level smartphones.

Another feature is SCOUT (Smart Companion for Online Understanding and Training), an AI-powered study assistant.

It can answer questions, recommend next steps and tailor study schedules to individual learning goals.

According to BizCommunity, Google said it is also adding support for more African languages, with isiZulu and isiXhosa among the first planned additions.

English, Swahili and Arabic are currently available.

The platform launched across Africa on 2 November 2026, with Google positioning it as a way to help bridge the continent’s AI skills gap.

World.title: Transfer report: Kaizer Chiefs sign 11-capped Bafana Bafana winger
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs are expected to announce the 27-year-old winger. The KwaMhlanga-born attacker has been a free agent since leaving Tunisian giants Esperance in September.

According to Unplayable, the speedy winger, who has two goals in 11 games for South Africa, has put pen to paper at Naturena.

KAIZER CHIEFS TO ANNOUNCE ELIAS MOKWANA

“UNPLAYABLE can reveal Kaizer Chiefs have signed Elias Mokwana. Deal done. Official announcement this week,” the outlet reported on X.



Known for his blistering pace, agility and dribbling ability on the right flank, Mokwana never enjoyed a smooth rise.

Financial difficulties forced him to quit his sports science studies, but he continued pursuing his football dream. He began making a name for himself in the ABC Motsepe League with Gemsbok Classic before earning a move to National First Division side Platinum City Rovers.

His performances at Platinum City Rovers attracted attention from top-flight clubs. During the 2021/22 season, he made 22 appearances and scored three goals, paving the way for a major breakthrough.

ELIAS MOKWANA’S BREAKTHROUGH AT SEKHUKHUNE UNITED

In May 2022, Mokwana signed a three-year contract with Sekhukhune United. He quickly adapted to the demands of the Betway Premiership, becoming a regular starter and an important attacking player. Across two productive seasons, he made more than 50 league appearances, contributed goals and assists, and earned several Player of the Match awards.

His club performances also opened the door to international football. Mokwana received his first Bafana Bafana call-up in November 2023 and went on to be part of the South African squad that claimed bronze at the Africa Cup of Nations. He also scored important goals in international matches against Andorra and Congo.

In August 2024, Mokwana took the next step in his career by joining Tunisian giants Espérance de Tunis on a three-year deal. He made an immediate impact, becoming the first South African player to win the Tunisian Ligue Professionnelle 1 title.



His debut season in Tunisia proved highly successful. He featured in more than 30 matches across all competitions, including the CAF Champions League, and helped Espérance secure a domestic treble consisting of the league title, Tunisian Cup and Tunisian Super Cup.

Mokwana then moved to the Saudi Pro League in August 2025, joining Al-Hazem on a season-long loan. He became an important part of the team, making 24 appearances and 16 starts. The winger also opened his scoring account in the Gulf region with a memorable individual goal against Al-Taawoun.

World.title: Four arrested as illegal firearms and ammunition found in vehicle
World.content:
Four men have been arrested after illegal firearms and a large quantity of ammunition were found in the vehicle they were driving in.

On Sunday, 1 November 2026, City Highway Patrol officers stopped a vehicle at the N2 weighbridge in Somerset West. They found four illegal firearms and ammunition within the vehicle.

The officers then arrested four of the five occupants and transported them to Somerset West Police Station. The fifth occupant reportedly fled the scene, per a media statement from the City of Cape Town.



INFLUX OF ILLEGAL FIREARMS ‘DEEPLY CONCERNING’

Alderman JP Smith, the mayoral committee member for Safety and Security, lauded the officers for their efforts on Sunday.

“I want to commend the Highway Patrol officers for their vigilance,” said Smith. “Their sharp observation skills led to more illegal guns being taken out of circulation, and possibly fewer crimes committed or lives destroyed.”

He continued: “The influx of weapons, including more and more automatic and semi-automatic assault rifles, remains deeply concerning, and it’s one of the reasons we have long called for better and more aggressive policing along the metro’s borders to curb the smuggling of firearms into the Metro.”



CITY ENFORCEMENT MAKES 199 ARRESTS

In this past week, the City of Cape Town’s enforcement departments made 199 arrests.

In addition to the Somerset West bust, these arrests include the detainment of 70 suspects by Traffic Officers. Fifty-three were for drunk driving, seven were for reckless and negligent driving, and ten were on other charges. Officers executed 2 076 warrants, impounded 118 public transport vehicles and issued 46 511 fines.

On the Metro Police front, they arrested 105 suspects. They also recovered eight hijacked and/or stolen vehicles, four firearms and 63 rounds of ammunition and issued 4 445 fines for various transgressions.



As for Law Enforcement officers, they made 24 arrests and issued 7 405 notices.

Members of the public are encouraged to report incidents, emergencies or suspicious/criminal activities to the Public Emergency Communication Centre on 021 480 7700. Alternatively, you can log by-law and traffic-related complaints using the Safety and Security feature on the City App.

In other Cape Town news, an eight-year-old Grade 1 learner has passed away following a suspected firecracker incident in Manenberg.

World.title: SAHRC responds to Andile Mngxitama’s farm attack tweet
World.content:
The SAHRC has responded to backlash of Andile Mngxitama's farm attack tweets about Donovan Marx. Images via X

The South African Human Rights Commission (SAHRC) has responded to widespread backlash over comments by MK Party MP Andile Mngxitama condoning the attack on North West cattle farmer Donovan Marx.

In a tweet, Mngxitama claimed that the attackers’ decision to chop off Marx’s ears was “symbolic”.

Five suspects have since been arrested in connection with the Ventersdorp attack.



SAHRC RESPONDS TO ANDILE MNGXITAMA TWEET ABOUT FARM ATTACK

Over the weekend, social media users have called on the SAHRC to investigate and take action against Andile Mngxitama.

On Monday, 2 November, SAHRC Commissioner Tshepo Madlingozi told The South African in a statement: “The South African Human Rights Commission confirms that it has received complaints against Mr Andile Mngxitama regarding a post on Mr Donovan Marx. The Commission is assessing the complaints in line with its Complaint Handling Procedure.

“The decision of the assessment will be communicated in due course as empowered by section 13(3)(b) of the South African Human Rights Commission Act 40 of 2013 (SAHRC Act), read with section 20 of the Equality Act, 2000”.



It continued: “The Commission wishes to remind members of the public that the right to freedom of expression is not absolute. The Constitution and the Promotion of Equality and Prevention of Unfair Discrimination Act of 2000 prohibit utterances that are intended to be harmful or propagate hatred on any of the listed grounds. ”

HISTORY OF TWEETS ABOUT RACISM, FARM ATTACKS AND WHITE SOUTH AFRICANS

Andile Mngxitama began trending over the weekend, when he tweeted: “Ventersdorp white farmer Donovan Marx had his ears cut off during a Plaas moord aanval [farm murder attack]. Attacking the ears is symbolic to denote the refusal of land thieves to listen. No land, no peace.

He added, “Farm life is overdetermined by systematic violence! Blacks got killed and fed to pigs!”



The MK Party MP later deleted the tweet but did not deny having posted it. In several responses, he poked fun at the backlash of his racially inflammatory comments.

Andile Mngxitama, a former member of the EFF who later started his own party, Black First Land First (BLF), has a long history of controversial social media and public comments on race, land ownership, white South Africans, and farm attacks.

His comments on X [formerly Twitter] have led to his account being permanently suspended.



Here are a few of his most controversial statements…

“We take the land by force. We’re not going to buy this land because it was stolen from us.” – October 2016, speaking at a rally.

“For those claiming the legacy of the holocaust is ONLY negative, think about the lampshades and Jewish soap.”



“I concur with @helenzille that the aroma of the burning flesh from the furnace of the holocaust may whet the appetite of the S.A. cannibals.” – August 2017 via X.

“All land owned by white people should be returned to black people. That includes land in Orania and Stellenbosch; all that land must be returned” – September 2018, speaking in parliament.

“For every one black life taken, five whites would be taken!” – December 2018 during a rally.



“Let’s repeat: if you kill black people. Will kill you too! Tell Johann Rupert” – December 2018 via X.

“I agree with Trump: the land thieves must leave SA and go to the USA. Our land shall be free of colonialists – Mabahambe!” – February 2025 via X.

World.title: Orlando Pirates have something Kaizer Chiefs don’t have
World.content:
Soweto giants Kaizer Chiefs finally tasted defeat in the Betway Premiership this season. Coach Da Cruz’s side succumbed to a 2-1 loss to rivals Orlando Pirates.

The result left Amakhosi 11 points behind the second-placed Buccaneers.

FERNANDO DA CRUZ ON KAIZER CHIEFS’ EXPLAINS THE GAP

The result was a heavy one to take but Da Cruz feels his side showed promising signs. According to the Frenchman, the Glamour Boys have some work before matching the likes of Pirates.



Da Cruz believes Pirates’ experience has played a major role in their consistency, something he wants to see his young Chiefs squad develop.

“The difference between Pirates and us, they have more experienced players and they have more consistency because of that,” he said.

“Our young players need to develop this consistency game by game. It takes time, it’s a process we need to take step by step and for the moment we’re not there. We will work hard to reach this step.”



The Chiefs coach was particularly pleased with his team’s first-half performance against the Buccaneers. However, he stressed that positive spells are not enough to compete at the highest level.

“We must use this type of game to grow up. The players must reach the next steps, but the players must understand we played well, we did good things, but it’s not enough. We must reach the next steps now,” he added.

A PLEA TO AMAKHOSI FANS

The Frenchman also warned against expecting an immediate turnaround, explaining that experience is something players develop over time through training and exposure to different competitions.



“We must continue to work but it takes time, it takes time, it’s not overnight these things can be fixed. We cannot get experience from one day to the next day. It’s training, many games and we must continue to learn, with competitions of different levels,” he added.

In the meantime, Kaizer Chiefs have a cup game to focus on. The Carling Knockout quarter-finals are coming up. The Glamour Boys will be home to Siwelele FC at FNB Stadium this Friday, kick off time to be confirmed.
