World.title: Rahul can be PM only in mock Parliament: Amit Shah
World.content:
CHANDIGARH/NEW DELHI: BJP derided INDIA bloc's rally against 'vote chori' as a "flop show", while Union minister Amit Shah said Rahul Gandhi could hope to be PM only in a 'mock parliament', referring to Congress's mock CEC impeachment.

Addressing a gathering on Chandigarh Police's 60th Raising Day on Sunday, Shah said Sonia Gandhi had resorted to the move since her dream of Rahul becoming PM was not fulfilled. "You (Rahul) want to become PM, stay in mock parliament your entire life; your turn won't come," Shah said.

His remarks highlighted BJPâs counterpunch to the oppositionâs campaign against Election Commission and govt over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, with BJP functionaries, including CMs, participating in âSave Democracy, Defeat Anarchyâ marches across the country.

BJP president Nitin Nabin, who travelled to Rohtak as part of the anti-Congress campaign, accused Rahul of deliberately destroying the credibility of constitutional bodies as part of his plan to sow anarchy.

As BJP functionaries, like former party chief and Union health minister J P Nadda, expressed jubilation over what they called a âsuper flop showâ at Ramlila Maidan, the party also homed in on Congressâs choice of the date for the rally â the anniversary of the 1984 anti-Sikh riots which took place in the wake of former PM Indira Gandhiâs assassination â to accuse the opposition party of mocking the tragedy suffered by the community.





âThey chose the very day when genocide of Sikhs happened to hold a rally. It is like rubbing salt into the wounds of 1984 victims,â said Shah in Chandigarh. Recalling Rajiv Gandhiâs controversial âwhen a big tree falls, the earth shakesâ remark, which was seen by many as the former PM seeking to rationalise the mass killings of Sikhs, a combative Shah emphasised that BJP had urged Congress not to hold the rally between Nov 1 and 3, days associated with the massacre.

World.title: IISc develops 3D-printed model to study how cancer drugs penetrate tumours
World.content:
BENGALURU: Researchers from

have developed a low-cost, 3D-printed device that could help scientists understand why cancer drugs are less effective in deeper regions of solid tumours.

The device recreates the nutrient- and oxygen-deprived conditions found inside tumours and allows researchers to examine how cancer cells respond to drugs at different depths.

The platform, developed by researchers from IIScâs Department of Chemical Engineering, addresses a longstanding challenge in cancer research: reproducing the complex microenvironment of solid tumours in laboratory conditions while retaining access to cells from different regions for analysis.

In solid tumours, blood vessels are often poorly developed and unevenly distributed.

Consequently, cells closer to blood vessels receive more oxygen and nutrients, while those farther away experience shortages. These differences can influence how cancer cells grow and respond to treatment.

Conventional laboratory methods that grow cancer cells in flat, two-dimensional layers do not adequately reproduce these conditions.





One approach to overcoming this limitation is the 'Cells-in-Gel-in-Paper' (CiGiP) model, in which cancer cells embedded in a gel are grown on stacked paper layers.

Nutrients and oxygen supplied from one side diffuse through the stack, creating conditions resembling different depths of a tumour. However, existing versions of this technique rely on wax-printed or hydrophobic barriers to contain the cell culture within each paper layer.

The discontinuation of solid-ink printers, which were used for this purpose, has made the method less accessible to laboratories.

The IISc team has replaced this requirement with a simple press-fit enclosure made using fused deposition modelling (FDM) 3D printers. Designed by Ankit Kumar, a PhD student in the laboratory of Bhushan J Toley, the device holds eight circular paper discs together through gentle, uniform pressure, preventing nutrients and drugs from leaking around their edges.

Culture medium is supplied through an inlet at the top.

The researchers tested the platform using MDA-MB-231 breast cancer cells embedded in Matrigel. After 72 hours, they found that the number of live cells progressively decreased from the topmost to the bottommost layer, while dead cells increased. Expression of HIF-1alpha, a gene associated with low-oxygen conditions, also rose towards the deeper layers, confirming that the model recreated a hypoxic tumour-like environment.

The team then examined how the chemotherapy drug doxorubicin penetrated the tissue. Drug uptake declined progressively across the eight layers, indicating that deeper regions received less of the drug. Longer treatment periods partially overcame these diffusion limitations.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

The researchers also tested doxorubicin and paclitaxel, individually and in combination.

Using a statistical method called the Bliss synergy score, they found that the two drugs had an antagonistic interaction across all eight layers when administered together.

This means their combined effect was lower than what would be expected if the drugs acted independently.

Published in Analytical Methods in 2026, the study was led by Toley, with Kumar and Shweta Kumar as co-authors. The researchers have made the deviceâs design files publicly available to facilitate reproduction.

They believe the approach could make paper-supported 3D tumour models more accessible for drug screening and studies of treatment response.

World.title: First in 47 years: CRPF completes 12 months without any operational casualties
World.content:
The previous time the CRPF went such a long period without an operational fatality was before January 1979.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF) has completed 12 consecutive months without losing any personnel in operational fatalities, marking an achievement not recorded in the force in 47 years.CRPF Director General GP Singh congratulated personnel on the milestone, saying the last operational death in the force was recorded on October 30, 2025. The previous time the CRPF went such a long period without an operational fatality was before January 1979.Sharing the achievement on X, Singh wrote, âA significant milestone in the history of CRPF - 12 consecutive months (One Year) have passed without any Operational fatality in the force, the last operational fatality in the force being on Oct 30th 2025. This has happened after 47 Years (last such period ended in January 1979).âHe attributed the achievement to improvements in equipment, training and operational planning. The force's focus on responding quickly to incidents, particularly by evacuating injured personnel to secondary and tertiary medical facilities, had also played an important role, he said.âItâs especially significant since this has happened while we continue to be deployed and engage intensely in all the major operational theatres, achieving significant breakthrough results.We remain committed to keeping the country peaceful & safe for all its citizens,â wrote the CRPF D-G.However, the milestone comes against the backdrop of another serious challenge facing the force, the rising number of personnel dying by suicide. Such deaths are recorded separately from fatalities during security operations.In August, the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) took suo motu cognisance of a media report stating that 19 CRPF personnel had died by suicide in less than five months, between January and May 2026.The Commission observed that the reported deaths, if true, raised serious concerns about the right to life of personnel serving in the country's largest Central Armed Police Force. It issued notices to the Union Home Secretary and the CRPF Director General, seeking detailed reports on the matter.According to the media report published on August 11, a total of 281 CRPF personnel died by suicide over the previous five years, of whom around 216 were on duty.The force recorded 57 suicides in 2021, 43 in 2022, 57 in 2023, 46 in 2024 and 59 in 2025. The 59 deaths recorded last year were reportedly the highest annual toll from suicides in the five-year period.

World.title: 'NCP united under Sunetra Pawar': Party rejects rift rumours as she skips Amit Shah meet
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The

(NCP) on Monday sought to put speculation about an internal rift to rest, with party leaders dismissing reports of differences following a high-profile meeting between Union Home Minister Amit Shah and a delegation of senior NCP leaders in New Delhi.

The speculation was fuelled by the absence of Maharashtra deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her sons, Parth and Jay, from Sunday's meeting with Shah. The development raised questions about whether the party's leadership was being sidelined in discussions over its future following the death of

.

NCP national chief spokesperson Umesh Patil rejected reports suggesting that Sunetra Pawar and Rajya Sabha MP Parth Pawar had been excluded from the Delhi discussions, describing the claims as "incorrect, baseless and misleading".

Patil accused sections of the media of giving the meeting an unnecessary political angle and creating an impression that the party was divided.

"Attempts are being made to give an unnecessary political twist to the meeting and create a narrative of internal differences and lack of coordination within the party. The NCP is an important constituent of the Mahayuti alliance and remains united under the leadership of Sunetra Pawar," he said.





He also urged the media to verify information before reporting on the party.

"Do not politicise formal meetings between leaders of alliance partners. Speculation should not be portrayed as fact," the NCP leader added.

NCP leaders meet after Delhi parleys

The delegation that met Shah late on Sunday included Praful Patel, Sunil Tatkare, Dilip Walse Patil, Hassan Mushrif, Chhagan Bhujbal and Dhananjay Munde.

After returning to Maharashtra, the leaders held closed-door discussions at Bhujbal's residence.

Walse Patil, who was part of the delegation, told PTI that all the leaders who had met Shah had returned to the state.

"The core group will meet now and DCM Sunetra Pawar in the evening," Walse Patil said.

Patil said Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar had met Shah earlier to discuss issues facing the party after Ajit Pawar's death. During that meeting, she had informed Shah that a delegation of senior party leaders would meet him and requested an appointment.

"Sunetra Pawar and Parth Pawar had earlier met Shah and discussed various issues facing the party following the death of Ajit Pawar. During that meeting, she had informed Shah that a delegation of senior party leaders would meet him and requested him to give them time," Patil said.

World.title: Cyclone Murusu: 19 flights cancelled, NDRF on standby as coastal states brace for severe storm - top development
World.content:
Here are the top developments:

Andhra govt rolls out grievance reporting mechanism

19 flights cancelled in Andhra Pradesh

Tamil Nadu sends NDRF, power teams to Andhra

Heavy rainfall in Chennai, schools shut

Odisha evacuates people, puts 300 rescue teams on standby

Farmers fear fresh crop losses

NEW DELHI: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu is set to make landfall along the south Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Narsapur in the early hours of Tuesday, bringing heavy rainfall and winds of up to 120 kmph. The approaching cyclone has put several coastal states on alert, disrupted flight operations and triggered evacuation and relief measures.The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said Murasu was very likely to move northwestwards and cross the coast near Ongole between 11.30pm on Monday and 4am on Tuesday, with wind speeds of 100-110 kmph, gusting up to 120 kmph.Heavy rainfall has already lashed parts of Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh, while Odisha has stepped up preparedness amid concerns over fresh damage following Cyclone Arnab.Andhra Pradesh government rolled out a dedicated grievance reporting mechanism to provide swift assistance to citizens affected by Cyclone Murasu.Residents in cyclone-hit regions can report emergencies and civic disruptionsâsuch as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situationsâby sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009.The facility is designed to establish direct communication between citizens and administration, enabling prompt on-ground intervention and effective coordination during disaster management operations.According to officials, citizens can report cyclone-related grievances by following a simple step-by-step process: Send a "Hi" to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the "Services" option from the menu. Choose "Murasu Cyclone Issues". Click on "Report Issue" and confirm.Select "Registration" and enter essential details, including name, district, and mandal.At least 19 domestic flights were cancelled across Vijayawada, Visakhapatnam and Tirupati airports as the cyclone approached the Andhra Pradesh coast.Vijayawada Airport director M Lakshmi Kantha Reddy said IndiGo cancelled 10 flights and Air India Express two. Four flights were cancelled at Visakhapatnam airport, while three were cancelled at Tirupati airport.Chennai airport authorities also cancelled some flights and advised passengers to contact their respective airlines for updates.Andhra Pradesh on high alertChief minister N Chandrababu Naidu directed officials to remain on alert as moderate to heavy rainfall and strong winds were expected across south coastal Andhra Pradesh and Rayalaseema.Naidu expressed hope that the impact would be limited, citing forecasts of lower wind speeds and rainfall intensity compared with Cyclone Arnab.The state energy department also placed power utilities on high alert, directing officials to take precautionary measures to minimise damage to electricity infrastructure and ensure uninterrupted power supply.Energy minister G Ravi Kumar asked distribution companies to remain particularly vigilant in the vulnerable regions.Tamil Nadu extended assistance to its neighbouring state, deploying three National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams comprising 90 personnel and 25 electricity department teams with 500 personnel and essential equipment.Karnataka also announced that it would send 500 skilled power personnel along with equipment to help restore electricity infrastructure damaged by Cyclone Arnab.Heavy rainfall also lashed several parts of Chennai, Chengalpattu and Tiruvallur districts, with showers continuing since Sunday night.The weather department warned of very heavy rainfall in Chennai and Tiruvallur, while heavy showers were forecast for Chengalpattu, Kanchipuram, Ranipet, Vellore and the Nilgiris.Schools in Chennai were closed on Monday as authorities braced for further rainfall. The IMD said rain intensity was likely to ease only after the cyclone completely crossed the coast.Odisha stepped up evacuation efforts in vulnerable areas as the cyclone was expected to bring heavy rainfall to its southern districts, including Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri.Disaster management minister Suresh Pujari said district collectors had been alerted and more than 300 rescue teams from the NDRF, Odisha Disaster Rapid Action Force (ODRAF) and fire services had been kept on standby.Schools and colleges in some southern districts have been closed until November 3.The fresh weather threat has also raised concerns over the ongoing search for 10 people missing in a landslide.The approaching cyclone has added to the concerns of farmers whose standing crops were damaged by Cyclone Arnab and subsequent flooding.Ganjam district reported the maximum damage to paddy crops, with several fields inundated. Farmers fear another spell of heavy rainfall could cause further losses and damage crops nearing harvest.Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P Patil said Cyclone Arnab and the subsequent floods had affected 1.18 lakh people, damaged 1,672 houses and impacted 75,388 hectares of agricultural land.The agriculture department, however, estimated the damaged crop area at around 90,000 hectares.Chief minister Mohan Charan Majhi announced a special relief package for those affected by Cyclone Arnab, adding that it would be reviewed after an assessment of the damage caused by Murasu.

World.title: 'Azam the, Azam hain': Will the Khan factor help or haunt Akhilesh in 2027 UP elections?
World.content:
NEW DELHI: "

Azam the, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge"

(

Azam was, Azam is and Azam will remain

).

With that emphatic declaration,

chief

sought to end speculation about his equation with one of the party's tallest Muslim leaders. But the political reality surrounding Mohammad

is far more complicated than the slogan suggests.

Nine days after Akhilesh's October 22 visit to Azam at Rampur jail, the veteran leader walked out of prison with his son Abdullah Azam after the Allahabad high court granted them bail in the dual PAN card case. His freedom, however, lasted barely minutes. The Enforcement Directorate arrested him in a separate money-laundering case linked to Mohammad Ali Jauhar University, and a court subsequently remanded him to 14 days' judicial custody.

The dramatic turn has put Akhilesh's declaration to the test. Once among the most powerful figures in the SP, Azam remains central to the party's political calculations in Rampur and its relationship with Muslim voters. But his legal battles, the erosion of his family's electoral stronghold and the growing challenge from Asaduddin Owaisi have turned his return into a complicated political proposition.

As Uttar Pradesh heads towards the 2027 assembly election, Akhilesh faces a question that goes beyond personal loyalty: can he hold on to Azam's political legacy without becoming hostage to its baggage?

The brief freedom

Azam and Abdullah had been in custody since November 2025 following their conviction in the dual PAN card case.





The Allahabad high court's order suspended their 10-year sentences and granted them bail, paving the way for their release.

However, the ED had a separate case waiting. The agency arrested Azam shortly after he walked out of Rampur jail, while Abdullah was allowed to go home.

Azam Khanâs rise in SP was closely tied to his long-standing association with Mulayam Singh Yadav.

The money-laundering investigation relates to alleged financial irregularities in the construction of Mohammad Ali Jauhar University in Rampur.

The ED has alleged that government funds were diverted for the university's construction. Azam is the founder of the university and heads the trust that runs it. These are allegations being investigated by the agency, not findings of guilt in the present case.

Speaking to reporters after his release, Azam alleged that he was being punished for being a Muslim and for establishing a university and schools. "What is there left to say? What can I say? The law has ceased to exist.

Is this the punishment for being a Muslim?" he said.

The following day, a special PMLA court in Ghaziabad sent him to 14 days' judicial custody. The court proceedings ensured that the brief release did not translate into a return to political activity.

Akhilesh turns arrest into political battle

Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav responded sharply to the ED action, accusing the BJP government of using cases to repeatedly send an elderly political leader to jail.

In a post on X, the SP chief said: "Let today's rulers remember that thrones change when the time changes. The conspiracy being hatched against Mr Azam Khan through these cases is being watched not just by the entire country, but by the whole world."

He added that repeatedly implicating an elderly man in cases and sending him to jail was "an utterly cowardly act", warning that injustice could eventually turn into a calamity for those responsible.

The response was significant because it came barely nine days after Akhilesh had visited Azam in jail. That meeting had already signalled that the SP chief was unwilling to distance himself from the veteran leader despite the legal controversies surrounding him.

The ED arrest has now sharpened the political messaging. For Akhilesh, the issue is no longer simply Azam's return to the party's political fold. It is also about positioning the SP against what it describes as the misuse of investigative agencies to target opposition leaders.

The BJP, on the other hand, has defended the ED action, maintaining that the law applies equally to everyone.

The Muslim vote and the Owaisi challenge

For the Samajwadi Party, the stakes in the Azam Khan question go well beyond the fortunes of one leader. They concern the party's hold over a crucial section of its traditional support base: Muslim voters. Muslims account for roughly 19% of Uttar Pradesh's population, making them one of the state's largest voting blocs.

Their concentration in several constituencies gives them considerable electoral influence.

In the 2022 assembly election, the community was a decisive factor in around 70 constituencies where Muslims formed at least 30% of the population.

The 2022 results also showed how strongly the community rallied behind the SP. The party fielded 64 Muslim candidates, of whom 31 won, taking the total number of Muslim MLAs in the assembly to 36, up from 24 in 2017.

The BSP fielded 88 Muslim candidates and the Congress 75, while AIMIM fielded more than 60. Yet neither the BSP nor Congress managed to elect a single Muslim MLA. The results suggested that the SP had emerged as the principal beneficiary of Muslim consolidation, even as smaller parties remained relevant in individual constituencies.

Muslims account for at least 30% of the population in around 70 constituencies.

Azam Khan was central to this political equation. His influence in Rampur and his standing among sections of the Muslim community gave the SP an important local and regional network.

His electoral record, along with that of his wife Tazeen Fatima and son Abdullah Azam, made the family one of the most prominent Muslim political establishments in the state. His absence from active politics has therefore left a space that other political players may seek to occupy.

It is this space that AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi is attempting to enter. His October 18 rally in Tanda was a reminder that the SP cannot take Muslim support for granted.

Owaisi accused Akhilesh of treating Muslims as a vote bank while prioritising the Yadav community, and questioned why the SP leadership had not done more for Azam Khan. His pitch was for independent Muslim political representation, arguing that the community should produce its own MLAs and MPs rather than remain a support base for established political families.

Owaisi's intervention is significant because the SP's electoral arithmetic depends not just on retaining Muslim support but also on preventing its fragmentation.

The 2022 results showed the limits of smaller parties: although BSP and AIMIM fielded substantial numbers of Muslim candidates, neither managed to convert that presence into Muslim representation in the Assembly. However, even without winning seats, such parties can potentially affect the outcome in closely contested constituencies by splitting votes.

Akhilesh's October 22 visit to Azam in Rampur jail was therefore also a political signal.

His declaration, "Azam they, Azam hain aur Azam rahenge" (Azam was, is and will remain), aimed to reassure the veteran leader's followers that the SP had not abandoned him. The visit came amid growing questions over whether Owaisi could use sympathy for Azam to make inroads among Muslim voters.

The challenge is compounded by the SP's wider social coalition strategy. Akhilesh has sought to move beyond the traditional Muslim-Yadav combination through his PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) framework, bringing backward classes, Dalits and minorities under a broader political umbrella.

But the party cannot afford to lose its Muslim support base while attempting to expand its reach among other communities.

Owaisi has attacked Akhilesh Yadav over the treatment of Azam Khan's family.

As the 2027 assembly election approaches, Akhilesh faces a delicate balancing act. He must reassure Azam's supporters that the SP continues to value the veteran leader and his political legacy, while ensuring that the party's Muslim support base does not become an opening for Owaisi or other rivals.

The 2022 election demonstrated the electoral value of Muslim consolidation behind the SP. The question now is whether Akhilesh can hold that coalition together without relying too heavily on one leader or one political family.

From kingmaker to political liability?

To understand Akhilesh Yadav's dilemma, one must first understand the extent of Azam Khan's influence in Rampur. For decades, Khan was not just the Samajwadi Party's most powerful face in the district but the man who dominated its political landscape.

He challenged the influence of Rampur's erstwhile Nawab family and gradually built a formidable political network, winning the Rampur Sadar assembly seat 10 times.

His influence extended beyond his own electoral victories: his wife, Tazeen Fatima, succeeded him as MLA in a 2019 bypoll, while his son Abdullah Azam twice won the Suar assembly seat. The Azam family's political presence became so entrenched that Rampur's electoral fortunes were often seen through the prism of Khan's influence.

That hold was not easily broken. In the 2022 assembly election, Azam Khan won Rampur Sadar for the 10th time despite campaigning from jail. The BJP's Akash Saxena, one of his most prominent political adversaries who had pursued several cases against Azam Khan and his family, lost that contest. But the equation changed after Khan was disqualified following his conviction in a hate speech case. In the December 2022 bypoll, Saxena defeated Azam Khan's close aide Asim Raza by around 34,000 votes, delivering the BJP its first victory in Rampur Sadar and making Saxena the first Hindu candidate to win the constituency.

The result marked a significant breach in a political stronghold that Khan and his family had dominated for decades.

The erosion of the Azam family's influence became more apparent in the 2024 Lok Sabha election. With Khan, his wife and son facing imprisonment, the SP fielded Maulana Mohibullah Nadvi from Rampur. The choice reportedly upset Khan's loyalists, many of whom stayed away from campaigning, exposing a growing rift between the local Azam camp and the party leadership.

It was a reminder that Azam Khan's network could still matter to the SP even in his absence, but also that Akhilesh could no longer assume the family would automatically fall in line with the party's decisions.

His treatment by the central agencies gives the party an opportunity to frame the issue as one of political targeting and due process. But the party will have to contend with the electoral consequences of being closely associated with a leader whose legal record has become a recurring political flashpoint.

The challenge for Akhilesh is to retain the political value of the Azam network without allowing the controversies surrounding Khan and his family to define the SP's wider campaign. In Rampur, the question is no longer simply whether Azam Khan can return to politics. It is whether the political machinery he built can still deliver for the Samajwadi Party, and on whose terms.

BJP's counter: 'Mafia raj' and law and order

In 2022, UP CM Yogi Adityanath famously said: "Even Akhilesh doesnât want Azam Khan to come out of jail because it will pose a threat to his position [chair].

The state government has nothing to do with these cases, whether they are related to Azam Khan or anyone else. It is the court that grants bail."

"Under previous governments, mafias were running a parallel administration. When we took action against the land mafia who grabbed poor farmers' land for private universities and personal fiefdoms, the Samajwadi Party developed sympathy for criminals instead of the victims," he had said.

The above remarks are at the core of the BJP's attack.

The BJP has consistently used the Azam Khan issue to attack the Samajwadi Party's record on law and order. The party's broader political narrative has sought to associate the SP's previous tenure with alleged criminal influence and what it describes as 'mafia raj'.

That gives the BJP an obvious line of attack if Akhilesh makes Azam's rehabilitation a central political theme.

The ruling party can frame the SP's outreach as evidence that it has not moved away from its past.

UP accused Akhilesh of opposing Azam Khanâs release out of concern that the veteran leader could challenge his position in party.

The SP, meanwhile, has to navigate the distinction between allegations, court findings and the political narrative built around them. It can point to the legal process and the need for due process, but it cannot wish away the electoral impact of the cases and convictions.

The BJP's attack also puts the SP's broader coalition strategy under pressure.

Akhilesh has sought to expand the party's social base beyond its traditional support groups through the PDA framework. A campaign dominated by the Azam Khan controversy could complicate that effort.

Akhilesh's jail visit, his response to the ED arrest and the party's continued engagement with Azam Khan send a message to the SP's traditional supporters: the party has not abandoned a leader who played a major role in building its political presence.

But the message also carries risks. The SP has to decide how much political space to give the Azam family, how prominently to project its association with them and how to prevent the issue from becoming a defining feature of its 2027 campaign.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

For Akhilesh, the Azam question will ultimately be about the political arithmetic as much as loyalty. He needs to reassure sections of the Muslim electorate that the SP remains attentive to their concerns, while keeping the PDA coalition broad enough to bring together backward classes, Dalits and minorities.

As Uttar Pradesh moves towards 2027, Akhilesh's tightrope walk will be to retain the political value of an old ally without inheriting all the baggage that comes with him. Azam may be an asset the SP cannot easily discard, but he may also turn out to be a liability the party cannot afford to let define its next election.

World.title: Netanyahu pressing Trump to attack Iran after midterms, says officials
World.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pushing for another wave of strikes on Iran after Tuesday's (November 3, 2026) midterm elections in the United States, according to two regional officials and a third person familiar with the matter.

A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Mr. Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections. U.S. President Donald Trump has alternated between threatening major strikes while pushing for a deal with Iran.

The two officials said diplomatic efforts have made progress, with Qatari mediators holding two rounds of talks last week with Iranian officials. The two officials said the mediators are trying to advance a framework for Iran to cease its attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in return for the U.S. lifting its blockade on Iran's ports.

They said more talks are planned for this week. The two officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they were discussing classified briefings they had received from American, and in one case Israeli, officials.

One official said Mr. Netanyahu was working with senior officials in the U.S. administration to persuade Mr. Trump to launch a quick but extensive air campaign and that the president does not appear to have made a decision.

Mr. Netanyahu pressed for strikes during a call over the weekend with Mr. Trump, who would not commit to taking military action, according to a person who was briefed on it.

Other U.S. allies in West Asia are warning against more strikes, saying it would destabilise the region and could lead Iran-allied Houthi rebels in Yemen to step up their attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea shipping, a third regional official said. Iran-backed militias in Iraq could also get involved.

That official, and the person familiar with the Netanyahu-Trump call, were not authorised to speak publicly and spoke on condition of anonymity.

The Israeli government did not immediately comment. The White House did not directly respond to questions about Mr. Netanyahu and Mr. Trump's discussion of potential new strikes during the weekend call.

Trump says he had a 'very good' call with Netanyahu

Mr. Trump told reporters on Sunday (November 1, 2026) that he and Mr. Netanyahu had a “very good” call the day before. He said they discussed Iran but gave no details. Mr. Netanyahu had pushed for renewed strikes even before the Israeli election as he sought to highlight his security credentials to a public deeply scarred by Hamas' October 7, 2023, attack.

Asked at a news conference on Saturday (October 31, 2026) about the possibility of new U.S. strikes on Iran and Iranian retaliation, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio would not say what would happen next but reiterated that the Trump administration prefers a diplomatic solution and that talks were ongoing.

“He hasn't made a decision,” Mr. Rubio said, referring to Mr. Trump.

“He'd prefer to solve it diplomatically," Mr. Rubio said, adding that Mr. Trump has “incredible confidence” in military action if that is needed.

Mr. Netanyahu has not commented on Iran since the election, and there was no word from his office on the latest call with Mr. Trump.

“The standoff in the Gulf between the U.S. and Iran is really between Qatar and Israel,” Andreas Krieg, a professor at King's College London, who previously worked as an adviser to Qatar's military, said on X.

“Qatar is tirelessly working on a diplomatic offramp with the region's backing while Israel is looking for military ways to throw the region under the bus.”

Iran says it is prepared for war while pursuing diplomacy

Iran wants guarantees that the U.S. will implement its side of any agreement. The U.S. and Israel have attacked Iran twice while it was engaged in negotiations over its disputed nuclear program.

Iranian officials say publicly they are prepared for war or diplomacy.

The new supreme leader, Ayatollah Mojtaba Khamenei, met with Iran's military chiefs and said the response to “any kind and level of threat” from the U.S. or Israel should be immediate and without “geographic limits,” and urged an expansion of the list of potential targets.

A recent analysis by The Associated Press found that Iranian strikes on more than two dozen U.S. bases since the start of the war have caused billions of dollars in equipment damage.

Mr. Khamenei has not been seen publicly since the opening strikes by Israel and the U.S. on February 28 killed his father, the previous supreme leader.

Iran's security chief, Mohsen Rezaei, told state television that “the tone has completely changed” from the U.S. and called it a “very good sign.” He gave no details about the letter he received from U.S. Vice President J.D. Vance, which Iran acknowledged last week, and said he had not responded.

Arab allies are caught in the middle

October saw the most attacks on commercial ships in the Strait of Hormuz since March, as Iran has tried to ramp up economic pressure on the U.S. to get it to lift its blockade.

The mood was grim at the Manama Dialogue, an annual security summit in Bahrain organised by the International Institute for Strategic Studies.

United Arab Emirates presidential adviser Anwar Gargash told attendees that the U.S. and Iranian stances are far apart, and “if these positions are not bridged, then we have to worry about the worst.”

Gulf nations have spent billions of dollars to boost their defence capabilities since the war began. Egypt's Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty told the gathering in Bahrain that the next escalation “will be more dangerous, more destructive, and it will lead to nowhere.”

China will send a special envoy to Iran, Oman and Saudi Arabia in early to mid-November, Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told reporters Monday.

“The Middle East Gulf region should not become an arena for great-power rivalry and geopolitical conflict,” Chinese President Xi Jinping told Oman's sultan, according to a readout from China's Foreign Ministry. China and Oman called for a return to dialogue.

World.title: Amit Shah backs SIR, alleges 3 crore ‘illegal infiltrators’ identified in 13 crore deleted voters
World.content:
Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday alleged that the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) exercise had identified around three crore ‘unaccounted voters’, whom he described as ‘illegal infiltrators from Bangladesh’, among the 13 crore names removed from electoral rolls. He asserted that all such infiltrators would be expelled from the country.

Addressing a public meeting at MJ Market in Hyderabad’s Old City after a ‘Save democracy-Remove anarchy’ foot march, Mr. Shah claimed that of the nearly 13 crore names deleted from voter lists during the SIR process, 4.25 crore voters were registered in two different locations, three crore were deceased, and another one crore were duplicate entries. He questioned if such names should continue to remain on the electoral rolls. “Do we need to remove infiltrators from the country’s voter lists or not?” he asked.

The Home Minister accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of defending the alleged three crore ‘unaccounted’ voters. “No matter how hard Rahul Gandhi or Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy may try, the BJP is committed to driving every infiltrator out of the country,” he said.

Mr. Shah alleged that the Congress and other Opposition parties were opposing the SIR exercise to protect ‘infiltrators from Bangladesh’, whom he described as their ‘vote bank’ and maintained that only genuine Indian citizens should be included in electoral rolls.

Ridiculing Sunday’s joint rally of Opposition parties in New Delhi, Mr. Shah described it as a ‘Save Infiltrators’ rally and urged BJP workers to counter what he termed ‘fear-mongering’ by the former on the SIR exercise through a door-to-door campaign.

The Congress was determined to halt SIR while the BJP would continue to support it, he said. Mr. Shah said the Centre was prepared to convene a special session of Parliament to discuss the issue and challenged Mr. Rahul Gandhi to participate in a debate. He said the Congress leader was not allowing Parliament to function. Taking a swipe at Mr. Gandhi, he remarked that while he might become Prime Minister in a ‘mock Parliament’, he would never attain the position in reality.

Defending the BJP’s electoral record, the Union Minister noted that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had won the 2014, 2019 and 2024 Lok Sabha elections without any SIR exercise. He also rejected allegations about Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs), asking how the Congress had won elections in Telangana, Kerala and Himachal Pradesh if the machines were flawed.

Turning his attention to Telangana, Mr. Shah alleged that the Congress government had become an ‘ATM’ for the party through the so-called ‘RR tax’. He accused the State government of failing to implement its six election guarantees and predicted that voters would reject the party in the next election.

Earlier, Mr. Shah led a foot march from the Babu Jagjivan Ram statue near Nizam College in Fateh Maidan to the meeting venue. Flanked by senior Telangana BJP leaders, including State president N. Ramchander Rao, Union Minister G. Kishan Reddy and Union Minister of State for Home Bandi Sanjay Kumar, he marched amid tight security and chants of ‘Jai Shri Ram’ and ‘Bharat Mata Ki Jai’. He had arrived by a special aircraft from Delhi and was received by the party leaders at Begumpet airport. From there he offered prayers at the Bhagyalakshmi temple at Charminar before the programme.

World.title: Eight labourers electrocuted after machine touches power line
World.content:
Eight labourers were electrocuted and five others injured when a road construction machine came into contact with an overhead 11 KV high-tension power line at Chhapoli village in Rajasthan’s Jhunjhunu district on Monday (November 2, 2026). The gravel mixing machine was being used to build a road with public participation.

Chhapoli village is near the Sikar-Neem Ka Thana State Highway and falls under the Udaipurwati police station area. Work on a narrow road connecting Chhapoli to Kadamkund was underway when a hydraulic jack made contact with the power line.

A massive electric current spread through the equipment instantly, striking labourers at the site. Five workers died on the spot, while three others succumbed during treatment. All the deceased were residents of Chhapoli village.

Villagers rushed to the spot and helped in the rescue efforts, as those injured were shifted to the Community Health Centre at Udaipurwati. The incident triggered anger among villagers, who staged a demonstration, alleging negligence by the administration and the power discom.

The protesters said power lines and poles were touching trees and claimed that no staff member was available at the Grid Sub-Station when they called to have the power supply disconnected.

Also read | Rajasthan IPS officer removed after ACB probe ordered against IAS husband

Prime Minister Narendra Modi has expressed his grief and announced ex-gratia assistance of ₹2 lakh each from the PM’s National Relief Fund to the next of kin of each deceased person. The injured will receive ₹50,000 each.

Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma has ordered a high-level inquiry into the accident and instructed officials to provide all possible relief to the affected families, besides seeking a factual report from the District Collector. Minister of State for Urban Development Jhabar Singh Kharra has been deputed to visit the accident site.

Veteran Congress leader and former CM Ashok Gehlot said a thorough investigation was essential to determine how the mishap had occurred and fix accountability for the deaths.

World.title: M.P. Police inspector mowed down by truck carrying illicit liquor in Dewas; racket supplying liquor to Gujarat uncovered
World.content:
An inspector of Madhya Pradesh Police was on Monday mowed down in Dewas district by a truck that he had intercepted on suspicion of smuggling illegal liquor, police said on Monday. The officer has been identified as Khategaon police station in-charge Dilip Puri.

An investigation launched following the incident has uncovered an illicit trade network spanning in multiple districts of Madhya Pradesh that supplies liquor to Gujarat.

According to the police, the incident took place around 1.30 a.m. on Indore-Betul highway when Mr. Puri was leading one of the four teams formed based on intelligence inputs that large amounts of illicit liquor was being transported from Harda district’s Timarni to Gujarat.

During the checking, a parked truck was spotted near Sandalpur in Dewas district and Mr. Puri had asked the driver to step down for a search.

“The driver, however, with the intent of killing Dilip Puri, ran him over with the truck and fled the scene. Mr. Puri died during treatment. The driver also tried to run over constable Sohan Jaat, who has suffered injuries,” an official police statement said.

The driver abandoned the truck after some distance and fled the scene. Dewas Superintendent of Police Aditya Mishra said that the truck was seized and more than 1,800 litres of illicit liquor in about 200 cartons were recovered from it. A video of the truck’s inspection showed that the cartons had been kept in a hidden chamber, made by laying down an additional metal surface to project the vehicle as empty.

Special Director General (DG) of Police Upendra Jain, who has been deputed by Chief Minister Mohan Yadav to oversee the probe, told The Hindu that the driver has been identified as Gajendra Rawat alias Akku, a resident of Alirajpur district, and a search is on for him. He said that the vehicle had been provided by Kairam Singh Changod, also from Alirajpur, and the local police has taken him into custody and is being questioned.

Mr. Jain said that a case under BNS Sections 103(1), 109(1), 121(2), 3(5) and Section 34(2) Madhya Pradesh Excise Act, 1915, has been lodged.

The Special DG said that the investigation has been revealed that the illicit liquor was being taken from Harda to Gujarat.

Mr. Jain said that the police have identified several people involved in the illicit liquor network. They are Patendra Jaiswal, a resident of Badwani district who owns a government licensed liquor shop in Harda, and his business partners — Manish Jaiswal of Indore, Mohin Jaiswal who lives in Gujarat, and Rahul Jaiswal of Harda’s Timarni and his associate Vijay Rao, a resident of Indore.

The officer said that Mr. Rahul Jaiswal has been identified as a key accused, ran the network to supply illicit liquor to Gujarat. He and Mr. Rao have been taken into custody and are being questioned about their entire network.

Mr. Rahul Jaiswal has been identified as a Congress functionary, and is the party’s in-charge for the Khategaon Assembly seat.

“Rahul Jaiswal operates the network from Harda to smuggle illegal liquor to Gujarat. He runs the racket to supply liquor from three shops to various regions. All the money from the illicit liquor trade would go to him which he then distributed to others,” the officer said.

Mr. Jain said that the police have uncovered the entire racket of illicit liquor trade and that the SPs of five districts have formed multiple teams in their respective regions that are conducting raids to nab people involved in the cartel.

The Dewas Police have also announced a reward of Rs10,000 each for the absconding accused in the case.

Meanwhile, the State Excise Department suspended Assistant District Excise Officer, Harda, Amar Singh Baghel and two excise constables for negligence.

Harda Collector Kumar Satyam also cancelled the licenses of three shops of Mr. Patendra Jaiswal in the district.

A post-mortem has been conducted on the deceased officer’s body and a special investigation team (SIT) has been formed in the case.

Mr. Puri, a resident of Dhar district, had joined the service in 2007 as a sub-inspector and had been posted in Dewas just a few months ago. He is survived by his wife, a daughter and a son. His body was dispatched to his village in Dhar.

The incident comes amid the ongoing investigation into the death of 13 people in two villages of the district, allegedly due to spurious liquor. Following the incident, the government had also transferred both the then Collector and SP of the district amid the controversy.

In the past one week, the police had also arrested 11 people in connection with manufacturing and sale of illicit and counterfeit liquor in the region.

Mr. Yadav expressed grief over the officer’s demise, announcing financial aid of Rs1 crore for Mr. Puri’s family and a sub-inspector post job for his wife on compassionate grounds.

“My deepest condolences are with the bereaved family members in this difficult time. The state government stands with the affected family. Special DG Shri Upendra Jain has been immediately dispatched to the scene for the investigation of the incident. Instructions have been given for a fair investigation and strict action in the matter,” he said on X.

The Opposition Congress, that has been alleging “government protection” to liquor mafia, hit out at the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government over law and order in the State. The Congress has alleged that no action has been taken senior government officials, despite various hooch tragedies in the State.

State Congress president Jitu Patwari said, “This incident shows how high the courage of the criminals doing illegal liquor business in the state is. The question is, how did the liquor business continue to flourish right under the nose of the administration?”

He demanded a high-level investigation into all illicit liquor related incidents in the State.

Earlier in September, more than 25 people had died after drinking counterfeit, poisonous liquor in Sagar district, after which the government had claimed that an operation to crackdown on illicit liquor trade had been launched in the State.

World.title: Former Ranji Trophy cricketer cremated
World.content:
Former Ranji Trophy cricketer and sports coach N.M. Amarnath, popularly known as Lalettan, was cremated at the Payyambalam crematorium on Monday (October 2, 2026) afternoon.

Scores of sports enthusiasts and well-wishers gathered to pay their last respects to the 78-year-old. His death in a road accident in Kannur on Sunday (October 3, 2026) evening has left the sporting community in mourning. Amarnath’s mortal remains were brought to his residence on Monday afternoon, where several people gathered to pay their final respects.

The accident reportedly occurred at South Bazar in Kannur when Amarnath was returning from a temple at Talap. A car allegedly hit the scooter he was riding, throwing him off it and under a tanker, resulting in his death.

Amarnath made notable contributions to cricket, badminton and hockey. He served as a coach with the Kerala Cricket Association and continued to train aspiring badminton players at three centres across Kannur and Kasaragod. His contribution to badminton was particularly noteworthy.

He was the son of the late Nakkadi Madhavan. His wife, Suguna, predeceased him.

World.title: Cyclone Murasu Live updates: Landfall to begin in A.P. around 2-3 a.m.
World.content:
Cyclone Murasu is expected to cross south Andhra Pradesh overnight, bringing winds up to 120 kmph. Extremely heavy rain is forecast for coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema on November 2–3, and Telangana on November 3.

Residents in cyclone-hit regions in A.P. can report emergencies and civic disruptions—such as power outages, uprooted trees, collapsed walls, waterlogging, and other distress situations—by sending a message to the dedicated WhatsApp number 9552300009. According to officials, citizens can send a “Hi” to WhatsApp number 9552300009. Select the “Services” option from the menu. Choose “Murasu Cyclone Issues”. Click on “Report Issue” and confirm. Select “Registration” and enter essential details, including name, district, and mandal.

Watch: Days after Cyclone Arnab, Cyclone ‘Murasu’ forms over Bay of Bengal

The Odisha government on Monday (November 2, 2026) expedited the evacuation of people from vulnerable areas after Murasu intensified into a severe cyclonic storm in the Bay of Bengal, officials said. A total of eleven flights arriving and departing from Chennai airport and Ten IndiGo flights scheduled from Gannavaram Airport today (November 2, 2026) have been cancelled due to Cyclone Murasu on Monday (November 2, 2026).

A deep depression over the Bay of Bengal on Sunday (November 1, 2026) intensified into a cyclone named “Murasu”, which means war drum. The latest storm is set to make landfall on the morning of November 3 between Nellore and Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh.

Also read: A.P. seeks assistance from Tamil Nadu, Karnataka for cyclone power restoration

World.title: Severe Cyclone Murasu: Landfall to begin in A.P. around 2-3 a.m.
World.content:
The IMD said in a bulletin at 1 a.m. that the landfall of the Severe Cyclonic Storm ‘Murasu’ near Ongole in Prakasam district, Andhra Pradesh, will commence before 3 a.m.

Cyclone Murasu Live updates

The outer spiral band in the northern sector entered southern Coastal Andhra Pradesh. The wall cloud region in the forward sector is approaching the coastline.

As Severe Cyclonic Storm Murasu moves closer to the A.P. coast, the A.P. State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) has warned of extremely heavy rainfall on the intervening night of November 2-3 in parts of Ongole Rural, Kothapatnam and Chinaganjam mandals of Prakasam district.

Very heavy rainfall is expected in Ongole Urban, Naguluppalapadu, Vetapalem, Tangutur, Singarayakonda, Ulavapadu, Maddipadu, Gudluru, Zarugumilli, Santhanuthalapadu and Kandukur mandals of the district.

Between 8.30 a.m. and 10.30 p.m. on Monday (November 2, 2026), none of the districts that are likely to be affected received any rainfall, as seen from the real-time rainfall information provided by the Directorate of Economics and Statistics. However, gales of speed of 70-90 kmph, gusting to 100 kmph, have been being reported along and off the A.P, coast, according to the India Meteorological Department(IMD). Experts say the rainfall activity is likely to pick up at night and sounded a word of caution to the public and officials.

As of 11.30 p.m. on Monday (November 2, 2026), the Severe Cyclonic Storm, centred over the West Central Bay of Bengal, off the South Andhra Pradesh coast, is moving in the northwest direction with a speed of 10 kmph and is likely to further move northwestwards with the same speed.

According to the latest update, the cyclone is currently located approximately 50 km from Kavali, 60 km off southeast of Ongole, 90 km northeast of Nellore and 150 km southwest of Machilipatnam. .

For assistance or to report any problems or emergencies at any time, people in Prakasam or any other affected district can contact Mana Mitra at 9552300009.

World.title: An anti-climactic outcome in the Knesset elections
World.content:
For the Israeli Knesset election hyped as “consequential” and a “day of reckoning for the October 7 Hamas attack”, the verdict points to new trends and the normalisation of trenchant nationalism. The inconclusive outcome risks disappointing most stakeholders. Israel, being at the epicentre of the ongoing regional tumult, needs a real-time analysis.

Israel’s total electorate is 7.3 million. Yet it has 38 officially recognised political parties vying for 120 Knesset seats, of which only 11 parties are likely to cross the 3.25% voting threshold needed to enter the legislature. The elections are on a proportional representation basis. The parties are currently arrayed in three coalitions: the ruling extreme right, the centrist bloc and the Israeli-Arab bloc which got 53, 48 and 19 seats, respectively. The last group representing a 21% minority is largely untouchable for mainstream Jewish parties. The electorate is also split along ethnic and origin-based lines into occidental, oriental and orthodox cohorts. Since the last elections in 2022, nearly half a million new voters have come of age. The voter turnout jumped by nearly a tenth to 77.7% — a sign of sharp political engagement.

World.title: Govt slashes high-speed diesel price by Rs7.76 per litre, petrol by Rs3.40
World.content:
The government on Monday slashed the price of petrol by Rs3.40 per litre, and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs7.76.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs374.51 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs395.20.

The prices are applicable for Nov 3 (Tuesday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

However, under a new arrangement, oil refineries would contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a monthly cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price on consumers’ end.

“The [petroleum levy] impact on estimated total country volume of Rs. 14.71/litre shall be surrendered by refineries @ Rs49.02/litre on their sales to [oil marketing companies],” reads a document by Ogra.

The government announced the arrangement during a press conference in Islamabad, held by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

“I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government’s help … increased their throughput,” Malik said, adding that these refineries had made profits from this throughput in the last three months.

“They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us … the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that. Because of that, we were able to maintain the price.”

On Oct 27, Jamaat-i-Islami (JI) chief Hafiz Naeemur Rehman met with Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad to discuss his party’s demand to provide relief to the public by abolishing the levy.

The two sides agreed to form a joint committee of the JI and the government to consider the expansion of the ongoing fuel relief scheme , being offered to owners of motorcycles, rickshaws and vehicles of up to 800cc since Sept 17 .

For his part, Rehman declared that his party would march to Islamabad in protest of the petroleum levy in mid-November if the government did not announce any major relief by then.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Additional input by Khaleeq Kiani

World.title: Govt enlists oil refineries to shield citizens from global price hikes
World.content:
The government said on Monday that oil refineries would bear a burden of approximately Rs15 billion each month, which would allow petrol to be sold Rs15 cheaper than what it was in the global market amid the US-Israeli war on Iran.

The statement came at a press conference in Islamabad addressed by Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik and Information Minister Attaullah Tarar.

Addressing the conference, Malik said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had made efforts to meet with oil refineries and consult with them regarding interventions to ensure that people got the cheapest petrol amid impending steep fuel price increases, including an increase of about Rs15 that would have taken effect on Friday.

“I am grateful to all the refineries that saw the public is in difficulty and with the government’s help … increased their throughput,” the minister said, adding that these refineries had made profits from this throughput in the last three months.

“They were requested to take a step to support the public during this difficult time, and I am glad that they listened to us … the Rs15 increase that was coming in the petrol prices on Friday, they helped the government with that. Because of that we were able to maintain the price.”

He added that more improvement would be seen by the public, expressing his gratitude to the refineries for standing with the government to provide assistance to the public during a time that had caused everyone difficulties — even the government as it struggled to procure oil at increasing prices.

As a result of this step, he highlighted, a load of approximately Rs15 billion a month would be borne by these refineries, allowing petrol to be sold at a rate Rs15 per litre cheaper than what it would be in the international market.

He expressed his hope that the crisis in the Middle East would soon move towards a peace agreement and that the government could advance with its purposes of “taking the system towards improvement, deregulation and refinery upgrades”.

“The government doesn’t want to be cruel to anyone,” Malik stressed, saying that it intended to take actions “with consultations, keeping the public’s interests in mind, in a fair way”.

He added that before the crisis, the premium of the refineries was $5 per barrel, and even today a $20 limit had been established. He further said that the government would have to step in and protect the public in case of further difficulties.

Tarar also addressed the conference, noting that the premier’s vision “from the first day” had been to put as little burden on the country as possible.

He said that even though the situation in the Middle East had affected every economy, including that of Pakistan, “our macroeconomic indicators have remained largely stable — Pakistan’s economy hasn’t taken as much of a hit as other countries”.

Regarding Friday’s situation, when petrol prices were increasing in the international market, he said that PM Shehbaz had directed refineries to absorb the price hike in order to prevent the Rs15 increase.

“During this difficult time … I think this is a great effort, as a result of which the public has been saved from this difficulty,” the information minister said.

He also discussed the fuel subsidy scheme announced by the premier on Sept 13, saying: “If you told me two months ago that there would be a scheme in which, upon SMS registration, motorcycle users get a weekly concession of Rs500 on petrol, and 800cc car users, every 10 days, get 10 litres of petrol for Rs100 less per litre, then I would have told you that it’s probably not possible to implement such a scheme.”

He praised PM Shehbaz’s “will power, intent and empathy for the public” that served as the foundation for the scheme.

Tarar highlighted that the number of unique users who had registered for the scheme had now crossed 15 million. He said that about Rs27bn had so far been allocated towards this relief and highlighted its success.

“This is a unique relief that is not available in the rest of the world,” he said, referring to both the fuel subsidy scheme and the steps taken by the government to prevent the increase in prices on Friday.

Answering questions, Malik said that he was the “biggest advocate for deregulation” and for bringing competition into sectors, seeing it as the way to protect people’s welfare and deliver good service.

However, he pointed out, “Have you seen any incident in the last 50 years that has been happening in the last six to eight months? What rules-based order do you want to adopt in the middle of this disaster?”

He stressed that once the crisis in the region ended, the government would make efforts to return to deregulation; however, currently the focus was on public relief.

The two ministers also stressed that there was no fuel shortage and that the country’s needs were being met even during difficult times. Malik said that November’s supply was fully covered, while decisions would be taken on supplies for the winter months of December and January and the prime minister had directed any necessary steps to be taken to ensure supplies.

The price of high speed diesel has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28. The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

The government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

As of July, fuel prices are now fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices.

World.title: PTI lawyer Salman Safdar says he met Imran, Bushra Bibi at Adiala jail
World.content:
PTI lawyer Barrister Salman Safdar on Monday said he met with party founder Imran Khan and his spouse, Bushra Bibi, at Rawalpindi’s Adiala jail, where they are both incarcerated.

Imran has been in prison since Aug 5, 2023, while his wife was arrested on Jan 17, 2025 in a separate case in which the couple were sentenced.

The IHC has allowed Imran twice-a-week meetings — on Tuesdays and Thursdays — with his family, lawyers and other associates. Despite multiple court directives, Imran’s meetings with his family and party leaders have been largely restricted in recent months.

In a post on X on Monday, Safdar said the meeting was his first with Imran after seven months and with Bushra in 11 months.

The last time he met Imran, the Supreme Court designated him as amicus. However, this time he met Imran Khan as his lawyer.

It lasted 40 minutes and was “insufficient to cover all cases [and] legal matters”, the PTI counsel contended.

“Both briefed me on their health conditions [and living] conditions and gave Fresh instructions for some legal matters and cases,” he wrote on X.

PTI Central Information Secretary Sheikh Waqas Akram told Dawn that he spoke to Safdar in detail.

“Salman told me that the meeting was held in connection with a number of applications which have been filed in courts to arrange meetings with Imran Khan,” he said.

“Salman has told me that he reached Adiala Jail at around 4:30pm and the meeting continued for around 40 to 45 minutes. However, he said that it was not sufficient time for the meetings, as there were so many cases which had to be discussed and as the meeting was being held after such a long time.“

Replying to a question, Akram said that no political issues were discussed during the meeting, which he added was also attended by Bushra Bibi. Safdar spoke about the cases and asked about future strategy.

When asked about Imran’s health, Akram replied that although health issues were discussed, the PTI would only speak about the legal cases.

Barrister Safdar’s last publicly reported meeting with Imran was held on April 8 this year, a day after the Islamabad High Court (IHC) directed authorities to arrange the meeting.

His previous meeting on Feb 10 with the former premier was also on the directives of the Supreme Court, where concerns about Imran’s health were raised.

Imran’s eye ailment — right central retinal vein occlusion (CRVO) — came to light in late January. While he has undergone eye procedures at the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims), his family demands that he be shifted to a hospital of his choice.

The government and the opposition have been engaged in a blame game , with the latter accusing the former of a lack of transparency on the matter, of not ensuring appropriate treatment for Imran, and of not allowing his personal physicians access to him. The government denies these allegations.

Imran was sent to jail for a three-year term on Aug 5, 2023 for concealing details of Toshakhana gifts. However, he and Bushra are also serving a 14-year sentence in a £190 million corruption case, also known as the Al-Qadir Trust case .

The couple were convicted in another Toshakhana case in December 2025, with 10-year and seven-year terms handed to them. The PTI founder also faces pending trials in terrorism cases related to the May 9, 2023 riots .

Imran’s sisters Aleema Khan, Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan, along with opposition leaders, have staged frequent sit-ins outside the Adiala jail demanding the PTI founder’s release.

They remain unable to stage more sit-ins since their detention in late September under the Punjab Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, as the PTI geared up for a protest march to Islamabad.

World.title: At Kazakhstan forum, Pakistan presents Karachi and Gwadar ports as 'strategic gateways' for Central Asian trade
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan can serve as an important trade and transit corridor for the landlocked Central Asian countries, providing them with access to international maritime trade routes and global markets, Minister for Board of Investment (BoI) Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh said on Monday.

He made the remarks while addressing the opening session of the Second Tianshan Forum for Central Asian Economic and Quality Investment, being held in Kazakhstan’s Almaty.

The minister termed Pakistan’s three major seaports — Karachi Port, Port Qasim and Gwadar Port — “strategic gateways that could facilitate regional trade, strengthen transportation links and provide alternative routes for the movement of goods”, according to a press release by the BoI.

Sheikh particularly underscored Karachi’s importance as Pakistan’s major industrial and commercial hub, noting that its established industrial base, business infrastructure, financial institutions and port facilities offered significant opportunities for trade, industrial partnerships and foreign investment.

He also highlighted Gwadar’s potential to further strengthen regional connectivity and economic cooperation.

Regional connectivity was “not merely about linking roads, ports and markets, but also about connecting economies, creating investment opportunities, generating employment and building shared prosperity across the region”, he remarked.

The minister invited regional and international investors to explore opportunities in key sectors, including energy, infrastructure, logistics, transportation, manufacturing and trade. He emphasised that improved connectivity and reliable energy supplies were essential for unlocking the region’s economic potential, the BoI statement said.

Highlighting the importance of regional cooperation, the minister acknowledged the contribution of the Central Asia Regional Economic Cooperation (Carec) Programme in promoting transport connectivity, facilitating trade and supporting economic integration among participating countries.

He observed that Carec provided a valuable platform for strengthening economic partnerships between Pakistan and Central Asian states, the statement said.

The minister emphasised that Pakistan’s strategic geographical location, youthful population, industrial capacity and seaport infrastructure positioned the country to play an important role in connecting Central Asian economies with international markets.

The Second Tianshan Forum will conclude in Almaty on Tuesday under the theme “Strengthening Resilient Connectivity and Quality Investment in Central Asia”.

According to information provided in its official agenda, the two-day forum is a follow-up to the success of the inaugural Tianshan Forum for Central Asia Economic Cooperation, and is aligned with the new Carec Institute Strategy 2026–2030, as well as the Carec 2030 Strategy Midterm Review Rolling Implementation Action Plan.

“In 2026, the Carec region continues to face a highly uncertain external environment. Rising geopolitical tensions have raised energy and food prices, disrupted transport and logistics, and weakened the reliability of trade corridors,” the agenda said.

At the same time, it added that intra-regional trade remained limited due to similar economic structures, weak production complementarities, and incomplete market opening. Persistent transport and logistics bottlenecks such as uneven infrastructure quality, fragmented asset management, and capacity mismatches kept trade costs high, it added.

“Non-physical barriers, including inconsistent customs procedures, weak digitalisation, non-harmonised standards, and inefficient border operations, further constrain cross-border flows. Meanwhile, digital infrastructure — especially cloud services, data centres, and AI applications — is expanding rapidly and reshaping connectivity and competitiveness,” it said.

It pointed out that Carec countries were progressing unevenly with “large gaps in backbone infrastructure, digital skills, and regulatory coherence”, calling for these gaps to be bridged to “effectively support inclusive growth, resilient connectivity, and regional integration”.

Senior representatives from multilateral development banks, financial institutions, high-level policymakers, business leaders, local governments, and academia across the Carec countries are attending the forum to discuss policy and operational issues in strategic areas such as transport, trade, logistics, energy, and digital connectivity, and promote pragmatic, sustainable investment in the region.

World.title: Adrian Hamilton-Manns appointed new PIA chief executive officer
World.content:
The board of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA) on Monday announced the appointment of Adrian Hamilton-Manns as its chief executive officer (CEO).

In a press release, PIA said Hamilton-Manns “brings a wealth of leadership and strategic experience within the global aviation sector”, adding that his appointment “marks a pivotal chapter” in the airline’s ongoing transformation.

It said that he had managed three airlines as CEO and was considered a “world expert” in transforming and reviving airlines, with over 30 years of experience.

“As Hamilton-Manns assumes the role of CEO, the consortium and the entire management board extend their deepest gratitude to the outgoing CEO, Air Vice Marshal (AVM) Amir Hayat, for his outstanding service and dedication to this vital national role,” the statement said.

It added that over his four-and-a-half-year tenure, Hayat’s leadership was “instrumental in navigating the airline through significant industry challenges”.

“His relentless efforts were central to initiating comprehensive structural reforms, optimising operational efficiencies and successfully preparing the airline for its highly anticipated privatisation phase,” it said.

“The foundation he has laid will be critical to the carrier’s future commercial viability and success,” it added.

The statement said that with Hamilton-Manns at the helm, PIA was confident that his extensive industry expertise would accelerate strategic objectives, elevate service standards and drive sustainable profitability in this new era.

According to Forbes Middle East, Hamilton-Manns was previously the CEO of Oman’s SalamAir and Kazakhstan-based FlyArystan. He also held roles at South African Airways and Virgin Australia.

The national flag carrier was privatised in December last year through an auction. A consortium led by Arif Habib Corporation Limited had won the auction for 75 per cent shares of PIA in December last year, making a winning bid of Rs135 billion.

The Arif Habib-led consortium, which took charge in June this year, had vowed to transform the loss-making airline through operational restructuring, fleet expansion, and improved customer service.

On Sunday, the carrier’s first Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner, acquired on lease last month, arrived in Islamabad from London as flight PK786. A PIA spokesperson said that the carrier was the first Pakistani airline to have added a Boeing 787-9 to its fleet.

World.title: 'Over a million' abuse images found on phone of UK man who drugged, raped wife: prosecutor
World.content:
A man who drugged and raped his wife over two decades and allegedly invited strangers to participate had “over a million photographs and videos” on his phone cataloguing the abuse, a UK court heard on Monday.

The court in Manchester, northwest England, is hearing the trial of nine men accused of various sexual offences against a woman who was abused by her husband — a man in his 60s who cannot be named to protect the victim’s identity.

The husband filmed and shared images of the abuse on the “internet and social media applications” with “other like-minded men”, prosecutor Louise Oakley told the court.

Some of the defendants allegedly “hid behind a screen” and conspired with the husband over the years to administer substances to the woman so she could be “used and abused”.

And starting 2023, the prosecutor said, the husband began inviting men around to their home and filmed himself and others raping her while she was unconscious.

It is the second case involving a man accused of inviting strangers to take part in abusing his wife currently being heard in Britain. A trial in Winchester in the south involving four men opened last week.

Global awareness of the crime, known as organised drug-facilitated sexual assault (DFSA), has grown following the high-profile conviction in France of Dominique Pelicot, who drugged and raped his then-wife Gisele for nearly a decade alongside strangers.

Oakley told the jury in Manchester that the husband’s phone, which was seized when he was arrested, was like a “confession booth” including “barbaric sexual fantasies” going back to 2004.

“There were over a million photographs and videos cataloguing not only his abuse of his wife but abuse on her committed by others, including those in the dock today,” Oakley said.

“There is no doubt he lived a double life masked in respectability,” the prosecutor said.

The husband pleaded guilty in September to some 60 sexual offences against his wife, including administering a substance with intent to stupefy or overpower her.

He and 13 other men are accused of conspiring to abuse the woman. Four of the men have since pleaded guilty to various offences.

The remaining nine men, aged between 28 and 70, deny various charges including rape, sexual assault and conspiracy to administer a substance with intent.

They include a taxi driver, a recruitment agency worker, a building supplies worker and a senior medic.

World.title: Pakistan, China discuss regional and global developments in high-level meetings
World.content:
